Datasets are stored in ubt_IL/dataset/ and models in ubt_IL/model/. See HF Data & Models for details.

docs.title: Data Conversion (HDF5 -> LeRobot)
docs.text: The conversion scripts turn raw HDF5 data from each robot into a LeRobot v3 dataset (meta/, chunk-000/ data parquet, videos/) for training, evaluation, and visualization.

docs.title: Script layout
docs.text:
Robot Script Config tienkung_pro ubt_IL/scripts/convert/tienkung_pro/ (convert.sh, convert_grasp_bottle.sh) ubt_IL/scripts/convert/tienkung_pro/configs/ walker_s2 ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/ (convert.sh, convert_real_to_lerobot_v3.py) ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/configs/

Shared converters (not robot-specific) live in ubt_IL/scripts/convert/common/:

Script Description convert_to_lerobot.py Generic HDF5 -> LeRobot converter (called by each robot's *.sh) isaaclab2lerobot.py / isaaclab2lerobotv3.py IsaacLab simulation conversion (v2/v3) lerobot2isaaclab.py Reverse conversion from LeRobot to a single HDF5 fix_stats_format.py Repair dataset stats formatting merge_datasets.sh Merge multiple dataset batches (e.g. several real-robot batches) hf_manager.py Hugging Face dataset/model management (see HF Management) all_robot_h5_info*.md Cross-robot HDF5 layout reference (see HDF5 Layouts)

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Each robot's convert.sh passes through these environment variables (defaults can be omitted; see bash convert.sh -h for the rest):

Variable Default Description SRC_ROOT Per robot HDF5 source root (one subdirectory per episode containing the HDF5 file) TGT_PATH /ubt_IL/dataset LeRobot output root CONFIG Per robot Conversion config JSON: field filtering + joint/camera mapping REPO_ID - Output dataset name (local directory name + HF repo name; keep it consistent with training) ROBOT_TYPE - Robot type (tienkung / walker_s2, written to metadata) TASK_NAME - Task name (written to each frame's task field and used as the language condition) FPS Per robot (15/13) Target frame rate; auto uses the source HDF5 rate VCODEC h264 Video codec (h264/jpeg/png) HDF5_REL_PATH Per robot HDF5 path relative to each episode directory RESAMPLE_FPS Empty (no resampling) Target frame rate; enables resampling LABEL_ROOT Empty Label root (used when task labels exist) TRIM_STATIONARY Empty (off) 1 enables stationary-frame trimming (see below)

Pass-through options: --overwrite replaces an existing dataset; --save_one true uses single-file mode.

docs.title: Stationary-frame trimming
docs.text:
Stationary frames can trap the policy in a local stationary state (motion stops). Set TRIM_STATIONARY=1 during conversion to truncate stationary runs longer than the cap.

Variable Default Description STATIONARY_KEY action Key used for stationary detection STATIONARY_WINDOW Auto (0.3 × fps) Stationary detection window STATIONARY_THRESH 0.03 Detection threshold (normalized, handling the scale difference between grip travel 0.05 and joint travel 0.5) STATIONARY_CAP 8 Maximum consecutive stationary frames STATIONARY_MIN_RUN 3 Minimum valid run length STATIONARY_RANGE_EPS 1e-3 Stationary interval tolerance STATIONARY_DIAGNOSE Empty 1 only reports the stationary distribution without writing data (for threshold calibration) 
# Usage: prefix the conversion command with TRIM_STATIONARY=1
TRIM_STATIONARY=1 \
CONFIG=... SRC_ROOT=... TGT_PATH=... REPO_ID=... \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/<robot>/convert.sh

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Problem Fix FileNotFoundError (HDF5) Wrong SRC_ROOT; make sure HDF5 was synced to a container-accessible directory "config does not exist" Specify an existing config file under configs/ Real-robot data reports a missing depth stream (TienKung) Real HDF5 has no depth; use a *_real.json config (RGB only) Normalization explodes during training (QUANTILES NaN/Inf) Constant dimensions (locked joints/grippers) give std=0 and division by zero; convert with a lower-dimensional config that drops dead dimensions Dataset frame rate differs from expected Use FPS=auto for the source rate or RESAMPLE_FPS to resample

For robot-specific commands and config choices, see Walker TienKung Pro / Walker S2 EDU.

docs.title: Container Environment (ubt_IL/docker)
docs.text: ubt_IL/docker/ provides a LeRobot + ROS 2 Humble containerized environment for training and deployment across the supported robots. Two architectures are supported: x86_64 workstations and Jetson/aarch64 robots. env.sh selects the Dockerfile and default parameters from the host architecture.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
File Purpose Dockerfile x86_64 image build (base huggingface/lerobot-gpu:latest, ships /lerobot/.venv) Dockerfile.arm64 Jetson aarch64 image build (base dustynv/l4t-pytorch:r36.4.0-linuxarm64, builds a Python 3.12 venv) run.sh CLI orchestrator: build / start / stop / restart / bash / rm / check entrypoint.sh Idempotent startup: editable installs lerobot and plugins, builds Walker ROS 2 messages, fixes opencv/numpy, validates sm_87 torch env.sh Selects default image / Dockerfile / GPU arguments from uname -m fastdds_no_shm.xml Disables FastDDS shared-memory transport to fix ROS 2 subscription failures inside Docker ros2_msgs/ Prebuilt ros-humble-bodyctrl-msgs_0.0.1-1_amd64.deb (x86) + bodyctrl_msgs_src/ source (built on arm64) torch-*-aarch64.whl etc. torch/torchvision wheels built from source for Jetson sm_87, shipped with the image (~261 MB)

Project code is bind-mounted at /ubt_IL; lerobot and each plugin are installed in editable mode at every startup, so sources do not need to be copied into the image.

docs.title: Automatic architecture selection
docs.text: Host architecture Dockerfile Default image Default GPU arguments x86_64 / amd64 Dockerfile lerobot-tienkung:humble --gpus all aarch64 / arm64 Dockerfile.arm64 lerobot-tienkung:humble-arm64 --runtime nvidia

docs.title: Build and run commands
docs.text:
cd ubt_IL/docker

bash run.sh build     # build the image (first build takes several minutes)
bash run.sh start     # idempotent start: warn if running, start if stopped, run if absent
bash run.sh check     # health check: mounts / lerobot / plugins / ROS 2 msgs / GPU / network
bash run.sh bash      # enter the container shell (ROS 2 and walker workspace sourced)
bash run.sh stop      # stop the container
bash run.sh restart   # restart the container (stop + start)
bash run.sh rm        # stop and remove the container

start follows the container log in the background and waits until the entrypoint has installed/compiled lerobot, the robot plugins, and the Walker ROS 2 messages and they import successfully. If imports still fail after installation, it exits with an error. The container runs with --network=host --shm-size=16g and forwards X11 for GUI tools.

docs.title: Environment overrides
docs.text:
# Use another base image
BASE_IMAGE=nvcr.io/nvidia/l4t-pytorch:<tag> bash run.sh build

# Use another Dockerfile or output image name
DOCKERFILE=./Dockerfile.arm64 IMAGE=my-lerobot:arm64 bash run.sh build

# Newer NVIDIA Container Toolkit on Jetson can use --gpus all
DOCKER_GPU_ARGS="--gpus all" bash run.sh start

# Disable explicit GPU arguments for debugging
DOCKER_GPU_ARGS="" bash run.sh start

# Change the ROS 2 domain ID (default 0 for hardware)
DOMAIN_ID=1 bash run.sh start

# Change the container name
CONTAINER_NAME=my-container bash run.sh start

The ARM64 base image can also be pulled and tagged manually to avoid re-pulling on every build:

sudo docker pull swr.cn-north-4.myhuaweicloud.com/ddn-k8s/docker.io/dustynv/l4t-pytorch:r36.4.0-linuxarm64
sudo docker tag \
  swr.cn-north-4.myhuaweicloud.com/ddn-k8s/docker.io/dustynv/l4t-pytorch:r36.4.0-linuxarm64 \
  docker.io/dustynv/l4t-pytorch:r36.4.0
BASE_IMAGE=docker.io/dustynv/l4t-pytorch:r36.4.0 bash run.sh build

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
1. Architecture-bound; both cannot coexist on one machine. The arm64 image is not generic arm64 but Jetson-specific (JetPack 6 base, torch wheels built for Orin sm_87, GPU arguments requiring Jetson's --runtime nvidia). An x86 host can only build and run x86 containers; arm64 containers must be built and run on a Jetson.
  2. bodyctrl_msgs is available on both architectures but installed differently. x86 uses a prebuilt deb (dpkg into /opt/ros/humble); arm64 has no matching deb and builds from source with colcon into /opt/bodyctrl_msgs_ws during Dockerfile.arm64. Walker S2 EDU does not depend on bodyctrl_msgs (its messages are built by entrypoint.sh from /ubt_IL/walker/walker_sdk_ros2, 8 packages).
  3. FastDDS shared memory must be disabled. Even with --network=host, shared-memory transport inside the container makes ros2 topic list work while echo/subscribe fail. The fastdds_no_shm.xml whitelist includes 127.0.0.1 plus the robot's direct-link subnet by default. ⚠️ This file changes with the robot subnet and must be edited before building (it is copied into the image at build time; changes afterwards have no effect). See each robot's real-robot workflow.
  4. TORCH_HOME is redirected to the bind mount /ubt_IL/.cache/torch, so torchvision pretrained weights such as ResNet can be downloaded and persisted.
  5. The entrypoint installs runtime dependencies on every start. lerobot, lerobot_robot_tienkung, and lerobot_robot_walker are editable installs, so source changes take effect after a container restart. It also replaces opencv-python-headless with the GUI build and pins numpy<2; on Jetson it defensively checks that torch.cuda.get_arch_list() contains 8.7.
  6. Jetson torch wheels ship with the image. Generic cu128 wheels from download.pytorch.org are not built for SM_87 and fail with no kernel image is available; the wheels here are built locally (CUDA 12.6, cuDNN 9.4, cp312) and copied to /opt/jetson-wheels to avoid rebuilding on every Jetson.
  7. LeRobot's [dataset] extra is preinstalled (datasets pandas pyarrow av, installed at build time), satisfying the hard dependency of the rollout module.

docs.title: Cross-Robot HDF5 Data Layout Reference
docs.text: Source: ubt_IL/scripts/convert/common/all_robot_h5_info_v1.2.md. This page documents the dimensions and units of HDF5 data from each source robot (end_effector / joint_position / cameras / depth). Consult it before writing a custom conversion config.

docs.title: HF Dataset/Model Management (hf_manager.py)
docs.text:
Script: ubt_IL/scripts/convert/common/hf_manager.py

A single tool for Hugging Face dataset and model operations: list, push, pull, bookmark (add/delete), and model cards. Datasets and models share the same commands; use --type to switch (default dataset).

docs.title: Installation and directory conventions
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.10+ and huggingface_hub>=1.0:

pip install "huggingface_hub>=1.0"
python ubt_IL/scripts/convert/common/hf_manager.py list --local   # no network required; verifies the setup immediately
Type Local root (default) dataset ubt_IL/dataset model ubt_IL/model

Override with the global --dataset-dir / --model-dir options.

docs.title: Login and mirror
docs.text:
Token priority: environment variable HF_TOKEN (recommended) -> huggingface_hub login cache (hf auth login).

export HF_TOKEN=hf_xxxxxxxx     # option A
hf auth login                   # option B (interactive)

In mainland China, set the mirror first (the script probes huggingface.co for 5 seconds and warns if unreachable):

export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com
  • Read-only commands (list / pull) allow anonymous access to public repos; write operations (push / card set / rm, etc.) require login.
  • --remote-user <account> explicitly selects the remote namespace, useful for viewing or operating on another user's public repos.

docs.title: Listing (list)
docs.text:
python hf_manager.py list              # datasets by default (local + remote + bookmarks)
python hf_manager.py list model        # model list
python hf_manager.py list --bookmarks  # bookmarks only
python hf_manager.py list --type model --local   # local models
Argument Description Default {model,dataset} (positional) Repo type shorthand, equivalent to --type dataset --local / --remote / --bookmarks List only local / remote / bookmarked repos Off

docs.title: Upload (push)
docs.text:
Upload a local dataset/model to your namespace. The repo is created automatically if absent, and the directory structure is preserved.

python hf_manager.py push walker_pick_sort                        # upload a dataset
python hf_manager.py push --type model tienkung_pick_up_act       # upload a model
python hf_manager.py push walker_pick_sort --sync                 # incremental sync (only new/changed files)
python hf_manager.py push walker_pick_sort --path meta/info.json  # upload a single file
python hf_manager.py push --all                                   # upload everything
Argument Description Default names (positional) Local directory names; multiple allowed - --all Upload every subdirectory under the root Off --path <rel> Upload only the specified file/subdirectory - --sync Incremental sync: only upload new/changed local files Off --prune With --sync, also delete extra remote files (dangerous) Off --delete <path...> Delete remote files/subdirectories - --description / --description-file Card description text / read it from a file - --no-readme Do not automatically use the local README.md as the card description Off --revision <ref> Upload to the specified branch main

docs.title: Download (pull)
docs.text:
Targets support four forms, in priority order: URL -> full repo_id -> bookmark match -> {account}/short-name; the repo type is detected automatically.

python hf_manager.py pull qingxiangliu/walker_pick_sort                    # full repo_id
python hf_manager.py pull https://huggingface.co/datasets/qingxiangliu/walker_pick_sort   # HF URL
python hf_manager.py pull walker_pick_sort --dry-run                       # bookmark name; preview first
python hf_manager.py pull --all --jobs 4                                   # download all remote repos concurrently
Argument Description Default --all Download every remote repo under the account Off --path <rel...> Download only the specified files/subdirectories - --revision <ref> Branch/tag/commit (reproduce historical experiments) main --jobs N Number of concurrent repo downloads 1 --show-card Show the card description before downloading Off

Download paths: dataset -> ubt_IL/dataset/<name>, model -> ubt_IL/model/<name>. If a non-empty local directory already exists, the download is merged automatically (same-name files are reused; only missing/changed files are fetched).

docs.title: Bookmarks (add / delete)
docs.text:
Bookmark public repos from other users for quick lookup/download. Bookmark file: ubt_IL/dataset/bookmarks.json.

python hf_manager.py add qingxiangliu/walker_pick_sort                    # bookmark a repo (URL or repo_id)
python hf_manager.py add https://huggingface.co/qingxiangliu/datasets     # bookmark an entire namespace
python hf_manager.py delete walker_pick_sort --dry-run                    # remove a bookmark
python hf_manager.py list --bookmarks                                     # view bookmarks

To copy a bookmarked repo into your own account, use the duplicate server-side clone (below).

docs.title: Other extensions
docs.text:
Subcommand Description Example card init/get/set Card management (init generates a local README; get reads the remote card; set edits it, requires login) card init walker_pick_sort --dry-run collection create/add/show/list Official collection management collection add <slug> <items...> --create rm (dangerous) Delete a remote repo rm qingxiangliu/old_dataset --yes visibility Toggle public/private visibility <repo_id> --private duplicate Server-side repo copy (no local transfer) duplicate <repo_id> --to <new_repo_id> --private

Legacy compatibility: upload -> push, download -> pull, delete-repo -> rm, copy -> duplicate; legacy forms such as --list model / --add <url> are converted to subcommands automatically.

docs.title: Global options
docs.text: Argument Description Default --type {dataset,model} Repo type dataset --dataset-dir <dir> / --model-dir <dir> Override the local root ubt_IL/dataset / ubt_IL/model --remote-user <account> Remote namespace (user/organization) Logged-in account --dry-run Print the plan without executing Off --revision <ref> pull: download branch; push: upload branch main

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Q: list shows "not logged in or network unavailable" for remote repos? Check the network and mirror: export HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com, export HF_TOKEN=hf_xxx, curl -I https://huggingface.co.

Q: Upload fails with create_commit() got an unexpected keyword argument 'branch'? huggingface_hub 1.0+ renamed branch to revision; upgrade with pip install -U "huggingface_hub>=1.0".

Q: The local model directory has no README.md? pull downloads the remote README.md; you can also run card init <name> to generate one from local files.

Q: card set --type model reports unrecognized arguments? Nested subcommands already register global options; make sure hf_manager.py is the latest version from the repository.

docs.title: Data Visualization and Playback
docs.text:
Reads ubt_sim/dataset/{walker_s2,tienkung_pro,walker_c1,tienkung_dex}/<timestamp>/trajectory.hdf5 in two modes:

Mode Purpose Dependency Preview (--mode preview) Inspect recorded camera images + joint/hand/gripper curves in Rerun; timeline scrub, frame stepping, and looping are built in rerun-sdk (control Python) Control (--mode control) Replay recorded actions to simulation or hardware at the original rate ROS 2 (rclpy + robot message packages)

Entry scripts live in ubt_sim/teleoperation/tools/:

  • playback_walker_s2.py - Walker S2 EDU (17 body joints + 7+7 V4 hands + 2 grippers + 4 cameras)
  • playback_tienkung_pro.py - Walker TienKung Pro (7+7 arms + 6+6 hands + 1 camera with depth)
  • playback_walker_c1.py - Walker C1 EDU (31 body joints + 6+6 hands + 1 camera)
  • playback_tienkung_dex.py - Walker TienKung Dex (right arm 7 + right hand 6/13 + 1 camera with depth)

Architecture: a shared core playback/common.py (HDF5 loading, pacing, CLI, Rerun preview) + robot adapters in playback/robots/ (schema + ROS 2 publishers + first-frame alignment), with thin entry scripts under tools/.

docs.title: Environment (container)
docs.text:
# rerun-sdk is included in the Dockerfile control environment; install it in an old container without rebuilding:
# (pin 0.23.0: 0.24+ requires numpy>=2, conflicting with the container's numpy<2 constraint)
docker exec -it ubt-sim /usr/bin/python3 -m pip install "numpy<2" "rerun-sdk==0.23.0" -i https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn/simple

# Control mode additionally needs (Walker requires SDK messages; TienKung only needs ROS 2):
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
source /opt/ubt_sim/walker_sdk_ros2_msgs/install/setup.bash   # Walker only

# Always use system Python:
/usr/bin/python3

docs.title: Preview mode
docs.text:
⚠️ Use the web viewer (browser) inside the container: the native Rerun viewer is a wgpu/egui application, but the container only provides NVIDIA vendor GL (no Mesa, no Vulkan surface); wgpu cannot obtain an adapter and fails silently. The local pop-up mode only works on hosts with a working GL/Vulkan window environment.

cd /ubt_sim

# ① Browser preview (recommended, works in the container)
python3 teleoperation/tools/playback_walker_s2.py \
    --episode dataset/walker_s2/1786681892 --mode preview --web-port 9090

# ② Save .rrd (no viewer) and open it with a rerun viewer on the host
python3 teleoperation/tools/playback_walker_s2.py \
    --episode dataset/walker_s2/1786681892 --mode preview --save-rrd /tmp/walker_ep.rrd

# ③ Local pop-up (only with a GPU window environment: run directly on a workstation/host)
python3 teleoperation/tools/playback_walker_s2.py \
    --episode dataset/walker_s2/1786681892 --mode preview
  • For other robots, switch to playback_tienkung_pro.py / playback_walker_c1.py / playback_tienkung_dex.py.
  • After starting the web viewer, the script prints the full URL (like http://localhost:9090/?url=rerun%2Bhttp%3A%2F%2F127.0.0.1%3A9876%2Fproxy); open it as printed. ⚠️ The trailing ?url= parameter is the data source and must not be omitted. For a remote browser, forward both ports 9090 and 9876 (ssh -L 9090:localhost:9090 -L 9876:localhost:9876).
  • --episode defaults to the newest episode under dataset/<robot>/ (largest timestamp directory); --max-frames N records only the first N frames.
  • Rerun panels: cameras/color/<camera> (images), cameras/depth/... (TienKung depth), action/<group>/<channel> (command curves), observation|puppet/... (observation curves), all synchronized on the frame_index / timestamp timelines.

docs.title: Control mode
docs.text:
Playback sends the raw recorded frame values (most faithful). Published ROS 2 topics:

  • Walker S2 EDU: 17 joints RobotCommand(MODE_POSITION) @ /mc/sdk/robot_command + both hands JointCommand(mode=5) + both grippers GripCmd
  • Walker TienKung Pro: CmdSetMotorPosition (14 motors) @ /arm/cmd_pos + both hands JointState
  • Walker C1 EDU: RobotCommand(MODE_POSITION) @ /mc/sdk/robot_command + both hands JointCommand(mode=5)
  • Walker TienKung Dex: ArmCtrl @ /arm/cmd (+ /head/cmd, /waist/cmd) + right hand angle_set / set_motor_multi (per hand variant)

Simulation (via the bridge) and hardware use exactly the same topics; one script works for both, only ROS_DOMAIN_ID differs.

# Always start with a dry run (no ROS 2 init, no publishing, just per-frame summaries)
python3 teleoperation/tools/playback_walker_s2.py \
    --episode dataset/walker_s2/1786681892 --mode control --dry-run --end 3

# Playback (same command for simulation and hardware; distinguish by ROS_DOMAIN_ID: hardware 0 / simulation 146, verify locally)
# Simulation: start simulation + bridge with start_sim.sh first, and confirm $ROS_DOMAIN_ID matches the bridge
python3 teleoperation/tools/playback_walker_s2.py \
    --episode dataset/walker_s2/1786681892 --mode control --align-first --end 200

# Hardware: set ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0 and run the same command
ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0 python3 teleoperation/tools/playback_tienkung_pro.py \
    --episode dataset/tienkung_pro/1786638182 --mode control --align-first

Common arguments (--help shows all):

Argument Default Description --start/--end 0/last frame Frame index or "5s" (5th second); --end is exclusive --rate Dataset fps Publish rate (Walker simulation bridge body limit is 100 Hz; >100 is silently rate-limited) --loop Off Loop until Ctrl-C --align-first Off Smoothly move to the first-frame pose before playback (Walker: 3 s quintic interpolation; TienKung: ~2 s joint-space ramp) --dry-run Off Print only, do not publish --interp Off [Walker] Linearly interpolate between recorded frames to --rate (smoother, deviates from the recording) --spd/--cur 0.2/5.0 [TienKung] Default motor speed/current --arm-clamp-lo/hi ±2.5 [TienKung] Arm limits (teleoperation has no arm limit constants; conservative assumption)

docs.title: Safety notes
docs.text:
• Limit clipping is enabled by default (Walker uses the hardware limit table; TienKung uses hand [0,1] and conservative arm limits); data containing NaN/inf is rejected.
  • --align-first aligns the first-frame pose before playback, avoiding a jump from an arbitrary current pose.
  • After Ctrl-C the robot holds the last command (simulation uses HoldTargetManager; hardware must be reset manually).
  • Always run --dry-run first, confirm ROS_DOMAIN_ID matches the target, and place the robot in a safe position.

docs.title: Imitation Learning Platform
docs.text:
ubt_IL is an imitation learning platform built on HuggingFace LeRobot. It covers the full pipeline from HDF5 collection data to deployable policies. Conversion, training, and evaluation all run inside the LeRobot + ROS 2 container; each robot has isolated configurations but follows the same workflow:

HDF5 data ─► LeRobot v3 conversion ─► visualization ─► training (ACT / Pi0.5) ─► offline MSE ─► deployment (sim / real)

Data comes from simulation or real-robot teleoperation. Main use cases:

  • Data conversion: convert simulation / real-robot HDF5 data into the standard LeRobot v3 format
  • Policy training: ACT recipes for Walker TienKung Pro, Walker TienKung Dex, Walker S2 EDU, and Walker C1 EDU; Pi0.5 VLA for Walker S2 EDU
  • Offline evaluation: run MSE evaluation after training to filter under-fitted models before real deployment

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
A single-container pipeline. Every stage is a script plus JSON configuration, organized per robot:

Stage Location Description Conversion scripts/convert/<robot>/ convert.sh + configs/*.json, HDF5 -> LeRobot v3 Visualization LeRobot visualizer Replay actions and images to catch bad data before training Training scripts/train/<robot>/ train.sh + configs/*.json, ACT / Pi0.5 Evaluation scripts/eval/eval_policy.py Offline MSE evaluation, shared by all robots Deployment scripts/deploy/<robot>/ rollout.sh and other inference/deployment scripts Output dataset/ · model/ LeRobot datasets and model checkpoints

docs.title: Imitation Learning Platform: Container Setup
docs.text:
ubt_IL runs in a LeRobot + ROS 2 Humble container. The build process is identical for all robots and maintained on this page; robot-specific steps start from the corresponding robot page.

The host project is mounted at /ubt_IL; all conversion/training/evaluation commands run inside the container.

docs.title: Build and enter the container (host)
docs.text:
cd ubt_IL/docker
bash run.sh build      # build the image (first time; selects the Dockerfile automatically)
bash run.sh start      # start the container
bash run.sh bash       # enter the container shell

docs.title: Automatic architecture selection
docs.text:
The build script selects a Dockerfile based on the host CPU architecture:

Host architecture Dockerfile Notes x86_64 / amd64 Dockerfile x86 workstation training / simulation deployment aarch64 / arm64 (Orin) Dockerfile.arm64 Jetson Vision board deployment (arm image must be built on the Jetson) aarch64 / arm64 (Thor) Dockerfile.thor Walker C1 EDU onboard compute (L4T r38 / sm_110); selected automatically by run.sh

docs.title: Common run.sh commands
docs.text:
build    Build the image
start    Idempotent start: warn if running, start if stopped, run if absent
check    Health check: mounts / lerobot / plugins / ROS 2 msgs / GPU / network
bash     Enter the container shell (ROS 2 and walker workspace sourced automatically)
stop     Stop the container
restart  Restart the container (stop + start)
rm       Stop and remove the container

docs.title: Python environments in the container
docs.text:
• Two Python environments: use /usr/bin/python3 for ROS-related code and /lerobot/.venv/bin/python (default) for LeRobot scripts.
  • The x86 image is based on huggingface/lerobot-gpu:latest and ships with /lerobot/.venv.
  • The container runs with --network=host --shm-size=16g and forwards X11 for GUI tools.
  • Communication: LeRobot (Python 3.12) -ZMQ-> Bridge2 (system Python 3.10) -ROS 2 DDS-> robot/simulator. Each robot uses its own ports: Walker TienKung Pro / Walker TienKung Dex 5559/5560 + camera 5558; Walker S2 EDU 5561/5562/5563; Walker C1 EDU 5661/5662/5663.
  • For real-robot deployment, the container is built on the robot Vision board (Jetson / Thor); the build script detects the board type (Thor selects Dockerfile.thor).

For full details on the image and entrypoint.sh (Dockerfile internals, environment overrides, FastDDS shared memory, Jetson torch wheels), see Container Environment.

docs.title: Simulation Platform
docs.text:
ubt_sim is a robotics simulation platform built on NVIDIA Isaac Sim (Isaac Lab 2.2.0). It supports four robots: Walker TienKung Pro, Walker TienKung Dex, Walker S2 EDU, and Walker C1 EDU. A ROS2-ZMQ bridge publishes simulation state and images on exactly the same topics as the real robot, so teleoperation and data-collection scripts switch between simulation and hardware without modification, enabling seamless sim-to-real transfer. Main use cases:

  • Simulation data collection: generate HDF5 training data in batches without occupying the real robot
  • Algorithm validation: low-risk testing of imitation learning and control policies before real deployment

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Three processes (Python versions must not be mixed):

Isaac Sim (Py3.11)  ──ZMQ──►  ROS2-ZMQ Bridge (Py3.10)  ──ROS2──►  teleop / collection scripts
  • Simulation /isaac-sim/python.sh: loads the task scene selected by UBT_SIM_TASK (the task name also determines the robot type) and sends camera images directly over ZMQ.
  • Bridge /usr/bin/python3: bidirectional ZMQ↔ROS 2 forwarding, started automatically by start_sim.sh.
  • Collection /usr/bin/python3: publishes commands and records 15 Hz HDF5.

docs.title: Simulation Platform: Container Setup
docs.text:
ubt_sim runs in a Docker container to isolate it from the host environment and simplify migration. The image contains ROS 2 and Isaac Sim and supports multiple robots.

Commands are split into two parts: build/enter the container on the host; launch simulation and collect data inside the container (project root is /ubt_sim).

docs.title: Build and start the container (host)
docs.text:
cd ubt_sim/docker
bash run.sh build      # build the ROS 2 + Isaac Sim image
bash run.sh start      # create/start the ubt-sim container
bash run.sh init       # install dependencies in the container (first build only)
bash run.sh check      # verify GPU / ROS 2 / message packages / numpy<2
bash run.sh bash       # enter the container (ROS 2 environment sourced automatically)

⚠️ Robot-specific, must be changed before building: edit interfaceWhiteList in ubt_sim/docker/fastdds_no_shm.xml and set <address> to the robot's direct-link subnet: Walker TienKung Pro 192.168.41.99, Walker S2 EDU / Walker C1 EDU 192.168.11.99, Walker TienKung Dex (Thor board 192.168.11.3). The file is copied into the image at build time, so editing it afterwards has no effect.

To separate simulation and real-robot ROS 2 domains, set ROS_DOMAIN_ID when starting the container (default 0):

ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0 bash run.sh start

docs.title: Common run.sh commands
docs.text:
build         Build the image
start         Create/start the container
stop          Stop the container (stops the bridge first)
restart       Restart the container
bash          Enter the container shell (ROS 2 sourced automatically)
rm            Remove the container
init          Install dependencies, build ROS 2 messages and the C++ image bridge
check         Verify the environment
bridge-start  Start the ROS2-ZMQ bridge separately
bridge-stop   Stop the bridge separately

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• bash run.sh check fails: follow the prompt and rerun bash run.sh init; verify numpy<2 and that bodyctrl_msgs plus the robot-specific SDK ROS 2 message packages are available.
  • X11 unavailable / simulation window not shown: run xhost + on the host and check that DISPLAY is forwarded; on a headless server use UBT_SIM_LOAD_ONLY=1 for preview only.

docs.title: Walker TienKung Pro
docs.text: Walker TienKung Pro is a humanoid robot with 50 DOF and two 12-DOF five-finger dexterous hands.

docs.title: Specifications
docs.text:
Item Specification DOF 50 End effectors 2 × 12-DOF five-finger dexterous hands Common training dimensions 26D (both arms 7+7 + both hands 6+6) / 13D (right arm 7 + right hand 6, single arm) LeRobot plugin ubt_IL/tienkung/lerobot_robot_tienkung USD model ubt_sim/assets/robots/tienkung_pro/tienkung_pro_v2.usd State/action order (26D) [left arm 7 | right arm 7 | left hand 6 | right hand 6]

In single-arm data (for example, right-hand-only collection), the locked dimensions are constant, which breaks normalization during training (QUANTILES NaN/Inf). Convert such data with the 13D config to drop the dead dimensions.
