docs.text:
Real-robot collection (trajectory.hdf5)
      │  right arm 7 + right hand 13 (or BrainCo 6)
      ▼
scripts/convert/tienkung_dex/convert.sh  ──► dataset/tienkung_dex_real_<task>
      ▼
scripts/train/tienkung_dex/train.sh      ──► model/tienkung_dex_real_<task>_act
      ▼
scripts/eval/eval_policy.py
      ▼
robot_ready.sh --real → rollout.sh        ──► real-robot execution

Training and deployment are essentially identical to simulation, using the same scripts with slightly different dataset configuration.

docs.title: 1. Prerequisite: real-robot data collection
docs.text:
Data is currently collected with the Thinker Studio teleoperation platform (see the official documentation), which can export LeRobot v3.0 datasets directly. You can also place collected real-robot HDF5 data under /ubt_IL/dataset/hdf5/ (or any SRC_ROOT) and proceed to conversion.

Verified real-robot dataset: tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d (32 episodes / 16,956 frames / 30 fps; both observation.state and action are 13D = right arm 7 + BrainCo hand 6; head camera observation.images.head 640×360 h264). The first sim2real validation reused a simulation-trained policy; once enough real data was available (≥30 episodes), training switched to real data directly. To mix simulation and real data, collect more first, then merge and convert.

docs.title: 2. Start the container (ubt_IL)
docs.text:
cd ubt_IL/docker
bash run.sh build      # first time (an x86 workstation build is sufficient)
bash run.sh start
bash run.sh check
bash run.sh bash

To run the policy directly on the robot (Thor) without a container, see On-robot deployment.

docs.title: 3. Data conversion (HDF5 -> LeRobot)
docs.text:
Verified path: BrainCo 13D real-robot data (config configs/tienkung_dex_13d_1RGB_brainco_real.json; 13D = right arm 7 + BrainCo hand 6 closure values 0~1; head camera observation.images.head 640×360, monocular RGB):

# Real-robot BrainCo 13D conversion (real HDF5 has no depth; this is expected)
CONFIG=/ubt_IL/scripts/convert/tienkung_dex/configs/tienkung_dex_13d_1RGB_brainco_real.json \
SRC_ROOT=/ubt_IL/dataset/hdf5/tienkung_dex_real \
REPO_ID=tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d \
TASK_NAME=pick_the_apple \
FPS=30 \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/tienkung_dex/convert.sh --overwrite

FPS=30 matches the real recording rate (the verified dataset is 30 fps). TRIM_STATIONARY can be enabled as needed for real data: the recording rate matches the main loop and there are no simulation-style duplicate frames spread across the motion, so trimming long stationary ready-pose segments at the start and end is beneficial.

Other hand variants:

Hand / dataset Conversion config Dimension Inspire r13 (pico6, 6D 0~1) tienkung_dex_real_pick_r13_1RGB.json 13D Inspire 20D (13D rad) tienkung_dex_20d_1RGB_inspire.json 20D BrainCo (6D 0~1) tienkung_dex_13d_1RGB_brainco_real.json 13D (verified)

Visualize after conversion:

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 lerobot-dataset-viz \
  --repo-id tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d \
  --episode-index 0 \
  --root /ubt_IL/dataset/tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d

docs.title: 4. Policy training
docs.text:
Verified path: BrainCo 13D real-robot training (config train_config_tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d.json, dataset tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d, output tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d_act):

CONFIG_PATH=/ubt_IL/scripts/train/tienkung_dex/configs/train_config_tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d.json \
OUTPUT_DIR=/ubt_IL/model/tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d_act \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/tienkung_dex/train.sh

train.sh defaults CONFIG_PATH to the simulation config; real-robot training must override it explicitly. train_config_tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple.json is a copy of the simulation config that only changes dataset.repo_id / dataset.root / policy.repo_id / output_dir / job_name; if the real REPO_ID differs from the conversion, update those fields. When real lighting differs strongly from simulation, add image_transforms (color jitter / random affine) by referring to train_config_tienkung_pro_real_pick_place.json.

Everything else is identical to simulation (see Simulation workflow · Training).

docs.title: 5. Policy evaluation (offline MSE)
docs.text:
/lerobot/.venv/bin/python /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/eval_policy.py \
  --policy-path /ubt_IL/model/tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
  --dataset-path /ubt_IL/dataset/tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d \
  --episodes 5 --inference-freq 1 --plot \
  --plot-dir /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/output/eval_tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d_act \
  --output /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/output/eval_tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d_act/results.json \
  --device cuda

With small real datasets, inspect per-dimension curves for plausibility (hand jitter, wrist overshoot) instead of relying only on the total MSE.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Enter topic-control mode: use the remote to switch to the half-body policy (toggle right while standing).
  2. Legs are owned by motion control: robot_ready.py never publishes to /leg/cmd; Bridge2 publishes only /arm/cmd and hand commands.
  3. Hand variant matches: --variant inspire|brainco must match the physical hand (HAND_VARIANT / JOINT_CONFIG must follow).
  4. Emergency stop available: Bridge2 monitors is_estop on /power/board/key_status and stops publishing when true.
  5. Inspire r13 uses 6→13 expansion: JOINT_CONFIG=tienkung_dex_inspire_13 automatically derives HAND_ACTION_MODE=pico6 — the policy outputs a 6D normalized 0~1 right_hand (0=open, 1=closed), and Bridge2 expands it into 13 0.1° codes with pico6_to_inspire13(); state echoes the same 6D command (open loop). Passing 13D is rejected as a dimension mismatch; passing rad moves the fingers barely at all.

docs.title: First run: ready pose only
docs.text:
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/robot_ready.sh --real

Hardware uses READY_POSE (not the simulation READY_POSE_TARGET, which is a gravity feed-forward compensation that makes command equal actual; using it on hardware leaves the robot about 13 cm lower).

The READY_POSE was validated against the simulation view during real-robot integration. With arms hanging naturally, the hands are at 0.80 m, below the table (0.987 m), so the motion must be staged in four segments (READY_CLEARANCE_POSE → READY_FOREARM_POSE → READY_UPPER_VERTICAL_POSE → final, 5 s each by default).

docs.title: Deployment: short duration and small limits first
docs.text:
Verified path: BrainCo 13D real-robot deployment (JOINT_CONFIG=tienkung_dex_brainco_13, policy 13D = right arm 7 + BrainCo hand 6 values 0~1; FPS matches the dataset, 30):

# Bridge2 is started by rollout.sh (--robot.bridge_enabled=true); do not start it manually.
# Any leftover dex bridge process on the same host is killed before startup.
ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0 \
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
JOINT_CONFIG=tienkung_dex_brainco_13 \
CAMERA_PORT=5558 IMAGE_ENABLED=1 \
FPS=30 \
DURATION=10 MAX_RELATIVE_TARGET=0.01 \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/rollout.sh

Demo:

docs.title: Hand representations
docs.text:
Mode JOINT_CONFIG Policy-side right_hand Conversion BrainCo 13D tienkung_dex_brainco_13 6D closure 0~1 Action code = round(1 + v*999); state v = (code-1)/999 Inspire 20D tienkung_dex_20 13D joint angles in rad Bridge2 converts each channel with inspire_rad_to_code to 0.1° codes Inspire r13 tienkung_dex_inspire_13 6D normalized 0~1 pico6_to_inspire13() expands to 13 codes

When bypassing the plugin and feeding right_hand directly to Bridge2: brainco / pico6 must be 0~1; rad13 must be 13D rad. Passing 0~1 to rad13 is interpreted as rad and the fingers barely move.

docs.title: On-robot deployment (Thor / Jazzy, no container)
docs.text: The path above runs the policy in an x86 workstation container while the robot only executes. To run the policy directly on the robot's ARM board (NVIDIA Thor, Ubuntu 24.04 + ROS 2 Jazzy + Python 3.12), use the host scripts in On-robot deployment, with no Docker. Data conversion and training are still recommended on a workstation/container; the robot only performs deployment.

docs.title: Warm-started inference service
docs.text:
ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0 \
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/tienkung_dex_real_pick_apple_brainco_13d_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
JOINT_CONFIG=tienkung_dex_brainco_13 CAMERA_PORT=5558 IMAGE_ENABLED=1 FPS=30 \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/inference_server.sh

bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/inference_client.sh status   # wait for READY
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/inference_client.sh start
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/inference_client.sh stop
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/inference_client.sh shutdown

Dex does not support load (model hot-swap): the server's robot reconstruction path hard-codes --robot.type=walker without --robot.cameras, which rebuilds a camera-less robot for Dex. To change models, shutdown and launch again.

docs.title: 7. FAQ
docs.text: Symptom Check Topics are visible but no data arrives Cross-distro type hash mismatch: compare ros2 topic info -v on both sides; or fall back to running Bridge2 on the compute host /arm/cmd is published but the robot does not move Is topic-control mode active (remote half-body/full-body policy + toggle up)? Is is_estop true on /power/board/key_status? Arm motion is too large / starts too abruptly Is MAX_RELATIVE_TARGET set? Is DURATION still the short first-run value? Pose is lower than expected The simulation READY_POSE_TARGET was used; hardware should use robot_ready.sh --real (READY_POSE) Hand variant is clearly wrong HAND_VARIANT / JOINT_CONFIG does not match the physical hand (Inspire 13 channels ↔ BrainCo 6 motors) Inspire hand does not move / log reports right_hand dimension mismatch r13 models need JOINT_CONFIG=tienkung_dex_inspire_13 (pico6, 6D actions 0~1); only the older 20D model uses tienkung_dex_20 (rad13, 13D rad actions) Thumb abduction differs from the ready pose Channel 10 of the pico6 expansion is determined by thumb_roll (all zeros → code 1750); the first policy frame overrides the ready-pose code 850 from robot_ready No camera image Does Bridge2 run with image_enabled=true? Is the port 5558? Does /ob_camera_head/color/image_raw publish? Bridge2 exits immediately "Channel table mismatch" means the plugin and Bridge2 constant copies have drifted; "message package missing" means /opt/tienkung_dex_msgs_ws was not sourced Robot still moves slightly after emergency stop Bridge2 only stops publishing new commands; previously sent targets remain in the drives. Press the physical emergency stop

docs.title: Walker TienKung Dex: Simulation Platform
docs.text:
Walker TienKung Dex simulation is built on NVIDIA Isaac Sim 5.0 (Isaac Lab 2.2.0). A ROS2-ZMQ bridge publishes simulation state and images on exactly the same ROS 2 topics as the real robot, enabling sim-to-real consistent teleoperation and data collection. Everything runs in a Docker container and supports both the Inspire RH5DG2 (67 revolute joints) and BrainCo Revo2 (53 revolute joints) hands.

Three-process architecture (Python versions must not be mixed):

Isaac Sim (Py3.11)  ──ZMQ──►  ROS2-ZMQ Bridge (Py3.10)  ──ROS2──►  teleop / collection scripts

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: Commands are split into two parts: build/enter the container on the host; launch simulation and collect data inside the container (container root is /ubt_sim).

docs.title: 1. Build and start the container (host)
docs.text:
cd ubt_sim/docker
bash run.sh build      # build the ROS 2 + Isaac Sim image
bash run.sh start      # create/start the container
bash run.sh init       # build ros2_bridge_msgs / Inspire / BrainCo messages and the C++ image bridge (first time only)
bash run.sh check      # verify GPU / ROS 2 / message packages / numpy<2

See Simulation Platform · Container Setup for the build workflow.

⚠️ run.sh init is mandatory: the Dex bridge exits if /opt/ubt_sim/tienkung_dex_msgs/install/setup.bash is missing. It also writes the robot message workspaces into the container's /root/.bashrc, so interactive shells source them automatically.

⚠️ Must be changed before real-robot integration: set the docker/fastdds_no_shm.xml whitelist to the robot's direct-link NIC IP (restart the container after editing). Pure simulation only needs 127.0.0.1.

docs.title: 2. Launch simulation (container)
docs.text:
# Enter the container
cd ubt_sim/docker/
bash run.sh bash

# Start simulation and the ROS2-ZMQ bridge
UBT_SIM_TASK=UBTSim-TienkungDex-Parlor-v0 bash scripts/start_sim.sh

The two scenes correspond to the two hand variants:

Task ID Hand Joints Config UBTSim-TienkungDex-Parlor-v0 Inspire RH5DG2 67 config/tienkung_dex/parlor.yaml UBTSim-TienkungDex-Brainco-Parlor-v0 BrainCo Revo2 53 config/tienkung_dex/brainco_parlor.yaml

start_sim.sh infers the variant from the task name (Brainco → brainco) and passes --variant to the bridge. Press R to reset the robot/scene.

Demo (picking an apple from the table):

Common environment variables:

Variable Default Description UBT_SIM_TASK UBTSim-TienkungPro-Parlor-v0 Set to UBTSim-TienkungDex-Parlor-v0 to enable DEX UBT_SIM_NUM_ENVS 1 Number of parallel environments UBT_SIM_LOAD_ONLY Unset Render only, no ROS (--device cpu by default) UBT_SIM_NO_BRIDGE Unset Set to 1 to skip starting the bridge UBT_SIM_TIENKUNG_DEX_CMD_PORT / _STATUS_PORT / _IMAGE_PORT / _JPEG_PORT 5755/5756/5757/5758 ZMQ ports (must match bridge_config.yaml) ROS_DOMAIN_ID 0 Default 0 (same domain as hardware); simulation and deployment containers must use the same value; set both to 146 to isolate

A shell entered with run.sh bash presets ROS_DOMAIN_ID from docker/env.sh (default 0). When launching from there, explicitly export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0 to avoid mixing with hardware.

docs.title: 3. Data collection (container, system Python 3.10)
docs.text:
# Batch collection: each episode runs reset -> ready pose -> grasp -> place on plate -> ready pose, and is saved only on success
bash teleoperation/control/tienkung_dex/save_data.sh --batch 20
  • Sampling rate 15 Hz; one camera_head RGB stream plus depth; right arm 7 + right hand 13 (Inspire) or 6 (BrainCo).
  • Output: /ubt_sim/dataset/tienkung_dex/<epoch>/trajectory.hdf5, with attributes for joint names / fps / hand variant / task.
  • With 20 collected episodes, proceed directly to conversion.

docs.title: 4. Camera test (container)
docs.text:
# Live preview (cv2.imshow, requires X11; press Q/ESC to exit)
/usr/bin/python3 teleoperation/control/tienkung_dex/tienkung_dex_controller.py camera --preview

# Save 5 frames
/usr/bin/python3 teleoperation/control/tienkung_dex/tienkung_dex_controller.py camera --save --count 5

Camera topics: /ob_camera_head/color/image_raw (rgb8) and /ob_camera_head/depth/image_raw (16UC1, millimetres).

docs.title: 5. Dataset preview and playback (container)
docs.text:
# Preview the dataset (Rerun Web Viewer)
/usr/bin/python3 teleoperation/tools/playback_tienkung_dex.py --mode preview --web-port 9090

# Replay on the same topics as hardware (run the ready pose first)
/usr/bin/python3 teleoperation/control/tienkung_dex/tienkung_dex_controller.py play ready
/usr/bin/python3 teleoperation/tools/playback_tienkung_dex.py \
    --episode dataset/tienkung_dex/<timestamp>/trajectory.hdf5 --mode control

The message workspaces are written into /root/.bashrc by run.sh init and loaded automatically in interactive shells. See Playback for all options and real-robot notes.

docs.title: Simulation modules
docs.text: Module Path Description Docker orchestration ubt_sim/docker/run.sh Image build, container lifecycle, message compilation Simulation launcher ubt_sim/scripts/start_sim.sh Detects the hand variant from UBT_SIM_TASK and starts the bridge Task definitions ubt_sim/source/ubt_sim/task/tienkung_dex_parlor/, tienkung_dex_brainco_parlor/ Apple-picking scenes for both hands Runtime config ubt_sim/config/tienkung_dex/parlor.yaml, brainco_parlor.yaml Scene/camera/device parameters ROS2-ZMQ bridge ubt_sim/teleoperation/bridges/tienkung_dex/ Bridge script + bridge_config.yaml Control and collection ubt_sim/teleoperation/control/tienkung_dex/ tienkung_dex_controller.py / save_data.sh / reset.py Playback ubt_sim/teleoperation/tools/playback_tienkung_dex.py Preview / action playback Data output ubt_sim/dataset/tienkung_dex/<timestamp>/trajectory.hdf5 Collected episodes

docs.title: ZMQ ports
docs.text:
Port Purpose 5755 Control commands (bridge PUB → sim SUB) 5756 Robot state (sim PUB → bridge SUB) 5757 Raw camera images (sim publishes RGB + uint16 depth; the C++ image bridge converts them to ROS topics) 5758 JPEG stream (published by simulation, for debugging)

The ubt_IL Dex plugin uses 5559/5560 (actions/state) + 5558 (real-robot camera JPEG). See Architecture · ZMQ ports for the cross-robot overview.

docs.title: ROS 2 topics
docs.text: Direction Topic Type sub /arm/cmd ArmCtrl (right arm; same family as hardware) sub /head/cmd HeadCtrl sub /waist/cmd ArmCtrl sub /leg/cmd ArmCtrl (published in simulation, not on hardware) sub /right_hand/angle_set, etc. Inspire / BrainCo hand messages pub /robot_state RobotState (about 200 Hz) pub /ob_camera_head/color/image_raw sensor_msgs/Image (rgb8) pub /ob_camera_head/depth/image_raw sensor_msgs/Image (16UC1, millimetres) pub /sim/task_completed std_msgs/Float32 (apple-center to plate-center distance; task success metric)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Simulation reports missing USD: pull all Git LFS assets (git lfs pull); --variant must match the task ID.
  • bash run.sh check / bridge reports missing message packages: rerun bash run.sh init; verify numpy<2, ros2_bridge_msgs, and the Inspire/BrainCo hand packages.
  • Collection script fails to import rclpy / message types: use /usr/bin/python3, not Isaac Sim Python.
  • save_data.sh --batch trips the consecutive-failure breaker: usually the bridge is not ready. Verify the simulation window is running and pgrep -f tienkung_dex_ros2_zmq_bridge returns a process. run.sh bridge-start only starts the Pro bridge; Dex must be started via start_sim.sh or the bridge script directly.
  • Head/arm still catching up after the trajectory ends: the simulation loop runs at about 11 Hz (RTF≈0.11); wall-clock trajectories exceed joint velocity limits when converted to simulation time. This is a time-base issue and does not affect hardware.
  • Keyboard teleoperation / preview has no window: requires X11 and DISPLAY; run xhost + on the host. On headless machines use save_data.sh --batch.
  • Hardware receives no topics: check that the docker/fastdds_no_shm.xml whitelist contains the direct-link NIC IP and that ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0.

After collection, continue with Imitation Learning Platform.

docs.title: Walker TienKung Dex Simulation Workflow: Collect -> Convert -> Train -> Evaluate -> Deploy
docs.text: Robot: Walker TienKung Dex — right arm 7 + right hand 13 (Inspire) Data source: Isaac Sim collection (ubt_sim, task UBTSim-TienkungDex-Parlor-v0) Container: lerobot-tienkung (built/started by ubt_IL/docker/run.sh, project mounted at /ubt_IL)

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• 0. Workflow overview
  • 1. Prerequisite: simulation collection (ubt_sim)
  • 2. Start the container (ubt_IL)
  • 3. Data conversion (HDF5 -> LeRobot)
  • 3.1 Conversion command
  • 3.2 Data visualization
  • 3.3 Stationary-frame trimming (TRIM_STATIONARY, off by default)
  • 4. Policy training
  • 5. Policy evaluation (offline MSE)
  • 6. Model deployment (simulation)
  • 7. FAQ

docs.title: 0. Workflow overview
docs.text:
ubt_sim collection (trajectory.hdf5)
      │  right arm 7 + right hand 13 (other dimensions are constant and dropped)
      ▼
scripts/convert/tienkung_dex/convert.sh  ──► dataset/tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple (20 episodes / 20D / 15 fps)
      ▼
scripts/train/tienkung_dex/train.sh      ──► model/tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple_act
      ▼
scripts/eval/eval_policy.py              ──► offline MSE + per-dimension curves
      ▼
robot_ready.sh → rollout.sh              ──► feedback into simulation, judge success

Two constraints to remember:

  1. Keep only effective dimensions in the action space. The left arm / waist / head / legs have a range ≤ 0.007 rad in the data (dead dimensions); including them breaks QUANTILES normalization (NaN/Inf ruins training). The current conversion config excludes them.
  2. Move the robot to the ready pose before deployment (robot_ready.sh); otherwise the initial pose mismatch may cause a collision with the table.

docs.title: 1. Prerequisite: simulation collection (ubt_sim)
docs.text:
See Simulation Platform for the environment, task scenes, reset, and playback.

# ① Launch simulation inside the ubt_sim container (with the task name)
cd ubt_sim
UBT_SIM_TASK=UBTSim-TienkungDex-Parlor-v0 bash scripts/start_sim.sh

# ② Collect data
bash teleoperation/control/tienkung_dex/save_data.sh --batch 20         # 20 episodes

Output: ubt_sim/dataset/tienkung_dex/<epoch>/trajectory.hdf5, with attributes for joint names / fps / hand variant / task.

With 20 collected episodes, jump directly to section 3.

docs.title: 2. Start the container (ubt_IL)
docs.text:
cd ubt_IL/docker
bash run.sh build      # first time
bash run.sh start
bash run.sh check      # expect [OK] for "tienkung_dex plugin / bridge / ROS2 msgs"
bash run.sh bash

docs.title: 3. Data conversion (HDF5 -> LeRobot)
docs.text: ubt_sim/ is mounted read-only at /ubt_sim by docker/run.sh; convert directly inside the container. If ls /ubt_sim fails, the container was created with an old mount; rebuild with bash run.sh rm && bash run.sh start. SRC_ROOT is optional: when the default ubt_IL/dataset/tienkung_dex does not exist, convert.sh falls back to /ubt_sim/dataset/tienkung_dex.

docs.title: 3.1 Conversion command
docs.text:
cd /ubt_IL

# Convert one episode first to validate the pipeline
SRC_ROOT=/ubt_sim/dataset/tienkung_dex \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/tienkung_dex/convert.sh --save_one true --overwrite

# Then convert everything
SRC_ROOT=/ubt_sim/dataset/tienkung_dex \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/tienkung_dex/convert.sh --overwrite

Defaults: CONFIG=configs/tienkung_dex_20d_1RGB_inspire.json, REPO_ID=tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple, FPS=15, HDF5_REL_PATH=trajectory.hdf5, ROBOT_TYPE=tienkung_dex.

On the simulation side, the Inspire hand records the 13 hand joints of the hardware channel driver, while the BrainCo hand uses 6 joint values. Output is written to /ubt_IL/dataset/tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple/.

Validation:

python - <<'PY'
import json
info = json.load(open("/ubt_IL/dataset/tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple/meta/info.json"))
print(info["total_episodes"], info["features"]["observation.state"]["shape"],
      info["features"]["observation.images.head"]["shape"])
PY

Expected output: 20 [20] [3, 360, 640] (the episode count depends on how much data was collected).

docs.title: 3.2 Data visualization
docs.text:
--episode-index is required (one episode at a time; choose 0~19 for 20 episodes):

# Inside the container, open the rerun window directly (the container needs X access with DISPLAY set)
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 lerobot-dataset-viz \
  --repo-id tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple \
  --episode-index 0 \
  --root /ubt_IL/dataset/tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple

docs.title: 3.3 Stationary-frame trimming (TRIM_STATIONARY, off by default)
docs.text:
Stationary-frame trimming prevents long stationary actions from trapping the policy in a local stationary loop. convert.sh exposes all --stationary-* options. Measurements on 20 episodes from Oct 2026 (STATIONARY_DIAGNOSE=1):

Metric Value Leading stationary run 0 frames (recording starts from the ready pose) Trailing stationary run mean 13 frames / max 14 In-segment stationary runs 160 runs across 20 episodes; mean 23 frames, max 56; 120 runs ≥10 frames Frames classified as stationary 36%–39%

Actual effect of enabling trimming with defaults (thr=0.03, W=5, cap=8):

TRIM_STATIONARY=1 bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/tienkung_dex/convert.sh --overwrite
  • 10,937 frames -> 8,269 frames (-24.4%), 411–416 frames per episode (originally 539–563).
  • No motion lost: all 20D ranges preserved; the maximum per-frame step matches the raw data (hands identical, arms at most +0.0056 rad).
  • Hand-closing motion is not trimmed: fingers close over 4.5 s, moving about 0.075 within a 5-frame window (threshold 0.03), so it is classified as motion.

Still disabled by default. Note: stationary trimming only handles "long stationary runs" and cannot fix adjacent duplicate frames (15 Hz recording runs on an ~11 Hz simulation loop, so duplicates are spread across the whole motion) — that is a sampling-rate issue, not a pause issue.

Tuning order: run STATIONARY_DIAGNOSE=1 to inspect the distribution first, then decide whether to enable it; STATIONARY_CAP / STATIONARY_THRESH are the two most frequently changed parameters.

docs.title: 4. Policy training
docs.text:
# Default config: 20 episodes / 20D / 60000 steps / checkpoint every 10000
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/tienkung_dex/train.sh

# Override common parameters
OUTPUT_DIR=/ubt_IL/model/tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple_act_v2 \
STEPS=50000 SAVE_FREQ=10000 BATCH_SIZE=16 bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/tienkung_dex/train.sh

# Resume (CONFIG_PATH points to train_config.json inside the checkpoint)
CONFIG_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model/train_config.json \
RESUME=true bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/tienkung_dex/train.sh
Environment variable Default CONFIG_PATH configs/train_config_tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple.json OUTPUT_DIR /ubt_IL/model/tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple_act STEPS / SAVE_FREQ 60000 / 10000 BATCH_SIZE Value from the config (16) RESUME false WANDB_ENABLE false

Output: checkpoints/<step>/pretrained_model (with config.json + model.safetensors) + checkpoints/last.

20 episodes are about 8.3k frames; 60k steps at batch 16 is ≈ 116 epochs, far beyond typical training. This is a "rather long than short" strategy: save every 10k steps (10k/20k/30k/40k/50k/60k, six checkpoints) and pick the best by offline MSE + simulation feedback. To reduce overfitting risk, STEPS=15000 (≈29 epochs) is enough.

docs.title: 5. Policy evaluation (offline MSE)
docs.text:
/lerobot/.venv/bin/python /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/eval_policy.py \
  --policy-path /ubt_IL/model/tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
  --dataset-path /ubt_IL/dataset/tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple \
  --episodes 5 --inference-freq 1 --plot \
  --plot-dir /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/output/eval_tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple_act \
  --output /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/output/eval_tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple_act/results.json \
  --device cuda

--inference-freq 1 means step-by-step inference, closest to deployment behavior; the default queues by n_action_steps.

Example output (020000 checkpoint, episode 0, prediction vs ground truth):

Comparison of two checkpoints (5 episodes / --inference-freq 1):

Checkpoint Mean MSE (5 episodes) Episode 0 010000 0.003661 0.003219 020000 0.002130 0.002750

This simulation deployment used 020000. Offline MSE is computed on the training set; a low absolute value does not guarantee closed-loop success — it only ranks checkpoints from the same run. The final criterion is /sim/task_completed after feedback deployment.

Check: in the 20D per-dimension curves, hand dimensions should not be flat all the way; otherwise the conversion columns are likely mis-sliced or the model did not learn the hand.

docs.title: 6. Model deployment (simulation)
docs.text:
# ① Inside the ubt_sim container: start simulation (separate terminal)
cd ubt_sim
UBT_SIM_TASK=UBTSim-TienkungDex-Parlor-v0 bash scripts/start_sim.sh

# ② Inside the inference container: move to the ready pose (four stages + hand pose), check the camera view, and confirm ROS_DOMAIN_ID
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/robot_ready.sh
/usr/bin/python3 /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/preview_camera.py

# ③ Run the policy
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
JOINT_CONFIG=tienkung_dex_20 FPS=15 DURATION=60 \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/rollout.sh

# ④ Reset the scene (robot returns HOME, not the ready pose)
/usr/bin/python3 /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/reset.py

# ⑤ Rerun the ready pose before the next episode: after reset head_pitch returns to ~0.000, losing the training view (45° down)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/robot_ready.sh

reset.py only sends /sim/cmd_reset to the simulator so the scene and robot return to their initial state; it does not restore the ready pose. For consecutive episodes, ②③⑤ form one group — do not jump from ④ straight to the next episode.

Warm-started inference service (warm up once, then start/stop in seconds):

POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/tienkung_dex_sim_pick_apple_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
JOINT_CONFIG=tienkung_dex_20 FPS=15 \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/inference_server.sh

bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/inference_client.sh status
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/inference_client.sh start
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/inference_client.sh stop
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/tienkung_dex/inference_client.sh shutdown

Success criterion: /sim/task_completed error < 0.15 m, with at least 3 of 5 episodes successful.

Demo:

docs.title: Control rate
docs.text: The dataset is 15 Hz and the simulation loop runs at about 11 Hz (RTF≈0.11). Start with FPS=15 and monitor the actual publish rate printed by rollout and the /robot_state rate; if the actual rate is far below 15, the same motion is stretched on the simulation timeline (the arm appears to lag), and you can adjust FPS then — keep the dataset at 15 Hz.

docs.title: 7. FAQ
docs.text: Symptom Check robot_ready.sh reports "Bridge2 is running" robot_ready.py and Bridge2 both write /arm/cmd and cannot run together; stop rollout first (--force skips the check; use with care) Arm does not move in simulation Is ROS_DOMAIN_ID consistent with simulation (ubt_sim defaults to 0)? Is /robot_state publishing (ros2 topic hz /robot_state)? No camera image Is 5758 publishing a JPEG stream? Is the camera type dex_camera (not image_server)? Action dimension precheck fails JOINT_CONFIG does not match training (20 ↔ 13) Hand motion globally misaligned HAND_VARIANT does not match the physical hand; Bridge2 prints the "right-hand channel → joint" table at startup Arm jumps far in one step after deployment MAX_RELATIVE_TARGET is empty and the plugin does not limit steps; set 0.05 for simulation debugging Training runs out of memory Reduce BATCH_SIZE; close simulation first if it is occupying GPU memory

docs.title: Walker C1 EDU
docs.text: Walker C1 EDU is a humanoid robot with 53 DOF and 41 controllable upper-body joints. Each arm has 7 DOF; each hand is an 11-joint dexterous hand (exposed as 6 SDK channels); the head carries a monocular RGB camera.

docs.title: Specifications
docs.text:
Item Specification DOF 53 (arms 14 + hands 11×2 + head 2 + waist 3 + legs 12) End effectors 2 × dexterous hands (11 joints each; 6 SDK channels: thumb_swing / thumb_mcp / index_mcp / middle_mcp / ring_mcp / little_mcp) Common training dimensions 26D (left arm 7 + right arm 7 + left hand 6 + right hand 6) / 13D (right arm 7 + right hand 6, single-arm tasks) Joints not controlled by the policy Head 2 / waist 3 / legs 12 (hold their current position; simulation anchors to HOME_POSE) LeRobot plugin ubt_IL/walker_c1/lerobot_robot_walker_c1 (robot type walker_c1) USD model ubt_sim/assets/robots/walker_c1/usd/walker_c1_with_hands.usd Cameras Head monocular RGB: simulation /sensor/camera/head/color/raw, real robot /sensor/camera/head_stereo_left/color/raw Training resolution Simulation 320×240; real robot 640×512 (5:4) ROS domain ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0 by default (simulation and real robot share domain 0; isolate by domain ID)

Verified on hardware (Nov 2026): 13D (right arm 7 + right hand 6), 30 fps, head camera 640×512. Dataset walker_c1_real_13d_1RGB (34 episodes / 11,406 frames) -> model walker_c1_real_13d_act_1RGB; the real-robot deployment loop is working.

docs.title: Simulation task
docs.text:
Task ID Scene Description UBTSim-WalkerC1-Parlor-v0 Parlor pick-and-place Apple pick-and-place with online IK collection (default)

Walker C1 EDU and Walker S2 EDU use the same simulation ZMQ ports (5655-5658); only one robot can run at a time.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Platform entry points (shared architecture and commands are on the platform overview pages):

  • Simulation Platform · Walker C1 EDU - Container build, launching simulation, batch collection, reset and playback
  • Imitation Learning Platform · Walker C1 EDU - HDF5 -> LeRobot conversion, ACT training, offline evaluation, deployment parameters

In order of use:

  1. Simulation workflow - End to end: simulation collection -> conversion -> training -> evaluation -> sim deployment
  2. Real-robot workflow - End to end: half_sdk prerequisite -> real collection -> conversion -> training -> real deployment
  3. Real-robot deployment - half_sdk guard, ready/home poses, ROBOT_MODELS registry, safety prechecks
  4. Inference server - Warm start, ZMQ commands, remote launch, model hot-swap
  5. Architecture - 26D/13D contract, ZMQ ports, ROS 2 topics, hand mapping

docs.title: Walker C1 EDU: Architecture
docs.text: Code: ubt_IL/walker_c1/ (LeRobot plugin lerobot_robot_walker_c1) and ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Dual-process bridge (same pattern as walker_s2 / tienkung). C1 is fully decoupled from Walker S2 EDU (separate package, registration name, and ports):

LeRobot inference (Python 3.12)                Bridge2 (Python 3.10)
  ZMQ PUB → 5661 (actions)        ──►         ZMQ SUB ← 5661
  ZMQ SUB ← 5662 (status)         ◄──         ZMQ PUB → 5662
  ZMQ SUB ← 5663 (JPEG images)    ◄──         camera relay ← ROS 2 /sensor/camera/head/color/raw
                                                  │
                                              ROS 2 DDS
                                                  │
                                        mc_state_msgs / mc_task_msgs
                                                  │
                                          Walker C1 EDU hardware / ubt_sim

docs.title: ZMQ ports
docs.text:
Port Purpose Owner 5661 ZMQ actions (PUB→SUB) plugin / bridge 5662 ZMQ state (PUB→SUB) bridge / plugin 5663 ZMQ images (JPEG base64) camera relay / plugin 5690 / 5691 Inference server REQ / PUB inference_server

Do not reuse walker_s2's 5561-5563 or the ubt_sim C1 bridge ports 5655-5658.

docs.title: 26D vector
docs.text:
[0-6]   Left arm 7    L_shoulder_pitch/roll/yaw, L_elbow_pitch/yaw, L_wrist_pitch/roll
[7-13]  Right arm 7   R_shoulder_pitch/roll/yaw, R_elbow_pitch/yaw, R_wrist_pitch/roll
[14-19] Left hand 6   left_thumb_swing/thumb_mcp/index_mcp/middle_mcp/ring_mcp/little_mcp
[20-25] Right hand 6  right_thumb_swing/thumb_mcp/index_mcp/middle_mcp/ring_mcp/little_mcp
  • Single source of truth: lerobot_robot_walker_c1/constants.py::ACTION_ORDER
  • Dataset names, deployment action_order, and bridge name-based scattering all follow this order
  • Head 2 / waist 3 / legs 12 are not part of the policy: the bridge does not command them and the robot holds its current position. In simulation, to_controller_data uses _hold_joint_targets (anchored to HOME_POSE) to fill all 53 joints, so uncommanded joints do not fall.

docs.title: 13D variant (single arm)
docs.text:
[0-6]  Right arm 7   R_shoulder_pitch/roll/yaw, R_elbow_pitch/yaw, R_wrist_pitch/roll
[7-12] Right hand 6  right_thumb_swing/thumb_mcp/index_mcp/middle_mcp/ring_mcp/little_mcp
  • Registry key walker_c1_13d (constants.ROBOT_MODELS); deployment config configs/walker_c1_13d.json
  • body.groups still contains left_arm / left_hand; inactive_fill (13 keys) fills the left arm 7 + left hand 6 with home values and sends them — this keeps the left arm from going slack and isolates it from the policy
  • Dataset walker_c1_sim_13d_1RGB (converted with DIM=13)

docs.title: 31-joint state order (state parsing only)
docs.text: BODY_JOINT_NAMES (constants.py) = L arm 0-6 / R arm 7-13 / head_yaw 14 / head_pitch 15 / waist_yaw 16 / waist_pitch 17 / waist_roll 18 / left leg 19-24 / right leg 25-30. The bridge selects only the 14 arm joints by name (body_groups has empty head/waist lists).

docs.title: ZMQ messages
docs.text:
Action (single step):

{"left_arm": [7], "right_arm": [7], "head": [], "waist": [],
 "left_hand": [6], "right_hand": [6], "ts": 1700000000.0}

Chunk (act_async): adds n_points / fps / inference_time_sec / obs_time_sec / chunk_id, with each group's value shaped [C, n].

{"hold": 1} clears the trajectory immediately and stops sending RobotCommand (in half_sdk, C1 motion control holds the joint positions itself; the bridge no longer repeats the last frame at 300 Hz, avoiding servo jitter).

State (bridge → plugin): {"left_arm": [7], "right_arm": [7], "head": [], "waist": [], "left_hand": [6], "right_hand": [6], "ts": ...}.

docs.title: ROS 2 interfaces
docs.text:
Direction Topic Type sub /mc/sdk/robot_command mc_task_msgs/RobotCommand (JointCmd.control_mode=MODE_POSITION=2) sub /mc/left_hand/command, /mc/right_hand/command mc_task_msgs/JointCommand (mode=[5], names + position) pub /mc/sdk/robot_state mc_state_msgs/RobotState (joint_states, 31 joints) pub /mc/{left,right}_hand/joint_states sensor_msgs/JointState (SDK 6-joint order) pub /sim/cmd_reset std_msgs/Bool (simulation only) Camera (sim) /sensor/camera/head/color/raw sensor_msgs/Image (rgb8, BEST_EFFORT) Camera (real) /sensor/camera/head_stereo_left/color/raw shm_msgs/Image6m (1920×1536 yuv422/UYVY, BEST_EFFORT) Camera override WALKER_C1_CAMERA_TOPIC / WALKER_C1_CAMERA_MSG_TYPE Override topic and type; /compressed is inferred as a compressed image; shm_msgs/Image6m must be specified explicitly

The mc_task_msgs / mc_state_msgs packages match the fields in walker_s2's walker_sdk_ros2 workspace and reuse /ubt_IL/walker_s2/walker_sdk_ros2/install by default. Set WALKER_C1_ROS_WS to use a separate workspace.

docs.title: File responsibilities
docs.text: File Responsibility constants.py Joint names/limits/READY_POSE/ACTION_ORDER/ROBOT_MODELS/inactive_fill_for config_walker_c1.py WalkerC1RobotConfig (registration name walker_c1), JSON loading and validation, to_bridge_config walker_c1.py WalkerC1Robot: connect / state thread / get_observation / send_action / chunk / home / disconnect hand_utils.py Hand 6-channel limit clipping (limits passed to the bridge once via to_bridge_config) camera/* ZMQ image subscription (base64 JPEG → ndarray, resized by W/H) ros2_walker_c1_bridge.py ZMQ↔ROS 2, name-based scattering, chunk blending/upsampling/300 Hz execution, stop publishing, singleton guard walker_c1_camera_relay.py sensor_msgs/Image → resize → JPEG → ZMQ 5663 chunk_processor.py Pure-numpy blending/interpolation/filtering (identical to and reused from walker_s2)

docs.title: Key constraints
docs.text:
1. lock_joints means skip, do not command. It must be an empty list on C1; _validate() drops entries outside the body groups.
  2. CANONICAL_JOINT_NAMES = 26 (excluding head/waist/legs). If you include non-group joints as walker_s2 does, _inactive_fill generates keys that cannot be assigned to the empty groups and send_action grouping fails.
  3. _inactive_fill is generated only when joint_config hits ROBOT_MODELS; the deployment JSON must also pass --robot.joint_config=walker_c1_26d.
  4. Hand limits are defined once: plugin hand_joint_limits → to_bridge_config() → bridge clipping; the bridge no longer hard-codes the V4 limit table.
  5. Arm joint 4 is called elbow_roll in the SDK docs and elbow_pitch in the URDF; the ubt_sim bridge tolerates aliases, but verify the sign on hardware before deployment.
  6. The camera is head monocular only (no wrist, no depth); relay QoS must be BEST_EFFORT. Simulation publishes uncompressed sensor_msgs/Image, hardware publishes shm_msgs/Image6m (1920×1536 yuv422/UYVY); the relay accepts both (including CompressedImage), decodes, resizes, and JPEG-encodes into ZMQ.
  7. The plugin runs in the same container as walker_s2 but with a different registration name (walker_c1 vs walker); do not import one from the other.

docs.title: Quick self-check
docs.text:
# 1. Package registration
python /ubt_IL/walker_c1/init_walker_c1.py

# 2. Config derivation (26D + 1 camera)
PYTHONPATH=/ubt_IL/lerobot/src:/ubt_IL/walker_c1/lerobot_robot_walker_c1 python - <<'PY'
from lerobot_robot_walker_c1 import WalkerC1RobotConfig
cfg = WalkerC1RobotConfig()
print(len(cfg.all_joints), list(cfg.cameras), cfg.zmq_cmd_port, cfg.lock_joints)
PY

# 3. Bridge defaults (no ROS required)
/usr/bin/python3 -c "
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/ubt_IL/walker_c1')
import ros2_walker_c1_bridge as b
print(b._DEFAULT_CFG['robot_model'], len(b._DEFAULT_CFG['body_joint_names']))
"

docs.title: Walker C1 EDU: Imitation Learning Platform
docs.text:
Code: ubt_IL/scripts/{convert,train,eval,deploy}/walker_c1/ (run inside the container) Prerequisite: repository cloned and submodules initialized as described in Getting Started; HDF5 data ready (simulation collection or real-robot collection)

This page documents the shared conversion/training/evaluation/deployment workflow and configuration parameters for Walker C1 EDU. Data-source-specific commands are embedded in the corresponding workflow pages.

docs.title: 1. Environment (ubt_IL container)
docs.text:
See Imitation Learning Platform · Container Setup for build / start / check / bash.

  • The host project is mounted at /ubt_IL; entrypoint.sh installs lerobot and lerobot_robot_walker_c1 (editable) and builds/loads mc_task_msgs / mc_state_msgs (reusing the walker_s2/walker_sdk_ros2 workspace).
  • Communication: LeRobot (Python 3.12) —ZMQ 5661/5662—> Bridge2 (system Python 3.10) —ROS 2 DDS—> robot/simulator. Images go through walker_c1_camera_relay.py over ZMQ 5663.
  • Thor (C1 onboard compute) is detected by docker/run.sh, which switches to Dockerfile.thor (L4T r38 / sm_110). Do not use the Orin Dockerfile.arm64.
  • bash run.sh check should report [OK] walker_c1 plugin / [OK] walker_c1 bridge / [OK] walker ROS2 msgs / [OK] torch; the RMW line is [INFO].
  • If the plugin is missing, reinstall it manually: python /ubt_IL/walker_c1/init_walker_c1.py (expects Robot type: walker_c1 / Camera type: walker_c1_camera).

docs.title: 2. Data conversion (HDF5 -> LeRobot)
docs.text:
Script: /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_c1/convert.sh (shared converter convert/common/convert_to_lerobot.py). It converts raw HDF5 data into a LeRobot v3 dataset at /ubt_IL/dataset/<REPO_ID>/.

Conversion command:

DIM=26 \
CONFIG=/ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_c1/configs/walker_c1_sim_26d_1RGB.json \
SRC_ROOT=/ubt_IL/dataset/walker_c1 \
TGT_PATH=/ubt_IL/dataset \
REPO_ID=walker_c1_sim_26d_1RGB \
TASK_NAME=walker_c1_sim_pick_place \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_c1/convert.sh --overwrite

Examples:

  • Simulation data: Simulation workflow · Data conversion
  • Real-robot data: Real-robot workflow · Data conversion

Conversion configs in /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_c1/configs/:

Config Dimension Image Scenario walker_c1_sim_26d_1RGB.json 26D (both arms 14 + both hands 12) 3×240×320 Simulation (default, DIM=26) walker_c1_sim_13d_1RGB.json 13D (right arm 7 + right hand 6) 3×240×320 Simulation, single-arm task (DIM=13) walker_c1_real_26d_1RGB.json 26D 3×512×640 Real robot walker_c1_real_13d_1RGB.json 13D 3×512×640 Real robot (verified, 30 fps)

Common environment variables (defaults can be omitted; see bash convert.sh -h and Data Conversion):

Variable Description SRC_ROOT HDF5 root (default /ubt_IL/dataset/walker_c1; falls back to /ubt_sim/dataset/walker_c1 if absent) TGT_PATH LeRobot output root (default /ubt_IL/dataset) CONFIG Conversion config JSON (defaults to a sim config based on DIM) DIM 26 (default) / 13; determines the default CONFIG and REPO_ID REPO_ID Output dataset name (default walker_c1_sim_<DIM>d_1RGB; keep it consistent with training) TASK_NAME Task name (default walker_c1_sim_pick_place, written to each frame's task field) FPS Target frame rate (default 15; use FPS=30 for 30 fps real-robot data) ROBOT_TYPE Robot type (default walker_c1, written to metadata) VCODEC Video codec (default h264) HDF5_REL_PATH HDF5 path relative to each episode directory (default trajectory.hdf5) TAIL_TRIM Drop N frames from the end of each episode (default 10). C1 ends with a fast release → retreat → ready reset; without trimming, the policy learns to fling the arm after finishing the task. TRIM_STATIONARY 1 enables stationary-frame trimming (see below) STATIONARY_DIAGNOSE 1 only reports the stationary distribution without writing data (for threshold calibration) RESAMPLE_FPS Target frame rate; enables resampling when set (disabled by default)

Stationary-frame trimming

Stationary frames in a dataset can trap the policy in a local stationary loop. Set TRIM_STATIONARY=1 to trim stationary runs longer than the cap (default 8 frames). Prefix the conversion command with TRIM_STATIONARY=1 \.

Output: a LeRobot v3 dataset under /ubt_IL/dataset/<REPO_ID>/ (meta/, chunk-000/ data parquet, videos/).

docs.title: 3. Data visualization
docs.text:
After conversion, inspect dataset quality with lerobot-dataset-viz. Checking data before training is important to avoid training on bad data:

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 lerobot-dataset-viz \
  --repo-id <REPO_ID> \
  --episode-index 0 \
  --root /ubt_IL/dataset/<REPO_ID>

Note: --root must point to the dataset directory containing meta/ (the repo_id directory itself), not its parent. HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 disables access to the HuggingFace Hub.

Examples: Simulation workflow · Visualization / Real-robot workflow · Visualization.

docs.title: 4. Policy training (ACT)
docs.text:
Training script: /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_c1/train.sh; configs in /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_c1/configs/.

Training command (optional overrides are listed below; unset values come from the config file):

CONFIG=/ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_c1/configs/train_config_walker_c1_sim_act_26d_1RGB.json \
DATASET_REPO_ID=walker_c1_sim_26d_1RGB \
OUTPUT_DIR=/ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_sim_26d_act_1RGB \
STEPS=30000 SAVE_FREQ=5000 BATCH_SIZE=8 \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_c1/train.sh

Training configs (ACT; chunk_size=n_action_steps=100 depending on the config):

Config Dataset Steps / save interval Batch train_config_walker_c1_sim_act_26d_1RGB.json walker_c1_sim_26d_1RGB 30000 / 5000 8 train_config_walker_c1_sim_act_13d_1RGB.json walker_c1_sim_13d_1RGB 30000 / 10000 8 train_config_walker_c1_real_act_13d_1RGB.json walker_c1_real_13d_1RGB 30000 / 10000 8

⚠️ train.sh defaults to the simulation 26D config. For real-robot training you must set CONFIG= explicitly.

Smoke test and resume:

# Smoke test: 2 steps, no checkpoint
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_c1/train.sh --steps=2 --save_checkpoint=false

# Resume (CONFIG points to train_config.json inside the checkpoint)
CONFIG=/ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_sim_26d_act_1RGB/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model/train_config.json \
RESUME=true \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_c1/train.sh

Without train.sh (call lerobot-train directly from /ubt_IL/lerobot):

cd /ubt_IL/lerobot
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /lerobot/.venv/bin/lerobot-train \
  --config_path=/ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_c1/configs/train_config_walker_c1_sim_act_26d_1RGB.json \
  --output_dir=/ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_sim_26d_act_1RGB \
  --steps=30000 --save_freq=5000 --batch_size=8

Common overrides (only applied when the environment variable is set; HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 is enabled by default):

Variable Description CONFIG Training config JSON (default train_config_walker_c1_sim_act_26d_1RGB.json) DATASET_REPO_ID / DATASET_ROOT Dataset name / root (must match the conversion REPO_ID) OUTPUT_DIR Model output directory (checkpoints under checkpoints/<step>/pretrained_model/) STEPS / SAVE_FREQ Training steps / checkpoint interval BATCH_SIZE / SEED Batch size / random seed DEVICE Training device (default cuda) RESUME Resume training (default false) WANDB_ENABLE Enable wandb logging (default false)

docs.title: 5. Policy evaluation (offline MSE)
docs.text:
Script (shared by all robots): /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/eval_policy.py. It runs offline inference over a LeRobot dataset, computes the per-frame MSE between predicted and ground-truth actions, and can plot per-episode comparisons. Quantify policy quality before deployment.

Evaluation command:

/lerobot/.venv/bin/python /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/eval_policy.py \
  --policy-path /ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_sim_26d_act_1RGB/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
  --dataset-path /ubt_IL/dataset/walker_c1_sim_26d_1RGB \
  --episodes 5 \
  --inference-freq 15 \
  --plot \
  --plot-dir /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/output/eval_walker_c1_sim_26d_act \
  --output /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/output/eval_walker_c1_sim_26d_act/results.json \
  --device cuda

--inference-freq 15 emulates a 15 Hz deployment cadence; 1 means step-by-step inference.

Argument Description --policy-path Trained ACT checkpoint (the pretrained_model directory) --dataset-path LeRobot dataset root (containing meta/info.json) --episodes Number of episodes to evaluate (default: all) --inference-freq Run inference every N steps to emulate the deployment chunk queue; defaults to policy.n_action_steps; 1 means every step --plot / --plot-dir Per-episode prediction-vs-ground-truth plots (PNG) --output Result JSON (summary + per-episode MSE) --device cuda (default; falls back to cpu when unavailable)

Once evaluation passes, continue with §6 Model deployment.

docs.title: 6. Model deployment
docs.text:
Script: /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/rollout.sh. It loads a checkpoint and sends actions to Isaac Sim or the real robot through the ROS2-ZMQ bridge. A dimension precheck runs before deployment, and sdk_guard.sh validates the half_sdk state. Helper tools: robot_ready.sh (three-stage ready pose), robot_home.sh (return home), preview_camera.py (camera path check), inference_server.sh (warm-started inference service).

Deployment command (optional variables are listed below; unset values use script defaults):

WALKER_C1_REAL=1 \
POLICY_PATH=<checkpoint pretrained_model directory> \
ROBOT_MODEL=walker_c1_13d \
DURATION=10 FPS=30 \
  bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/rollout.sh

Deployment guides:

  • Simulation deployment (feedback into the simulator; recommended first): Simulation workflow · Sim deployment
  • Real-robot deployment (half_sdk guard and safety precheck): Real-robot workflow · Deployment · Real-robot deployment
  • Inference server (warm start / external calls): Inference server

Common environment variables:

Variable Default Description POLICY_PATH Required, no default Checkpoint directory (containing config.json) ROBOT_MODEL Real: walker_c1_13d / sim: walker_c1_26d ROBOT_MODELS key (also used as --robot.joint_config); must match the training DOF ROBOT_CONFIG configs/<ROBOT_MODEL>.json Hardware config JSON ROBOT_TYPE walker_c1 Plugin registration name WALKER_C1_REAL 1 1 = real robot (13d/task/act_async/guard/real camera); 0 = simulation/offline EPISODES 1 Number of episodes; the base strategy does not support multi-episode runs, so values >1 use an outer loop with a reset per episode DURATION 30 Maximum seconds per episode FPS 15 Control rate (use FPS=30 for 30 fps datasets) RESET_MODE Real: task / sim: sim-scene Reset before each episode: sim-scene / task / both / none INFERENCE_TYPE Real: act_async / sim: sync sync / act_async (chunk -> bridge blending at 300 Hz) INFERENCE_HZ Real: 1 / sim: 2 act_async replanning rate EXECUTION_HORIZON 0 Truncate act_async chunks after N steps (0 = no truncation) CAMERA_TOPIC / CAMERA_MSG_TYPE Real: head left + shm_msgs/Image6m Simulation must override to /sensor/camera/head/color/raw + sensor_msgs/Image SDK_GUARD Real: 1 / sim: auto half_sdk guard: 1 enforce / auto only when a real robot is detected / 0 skip SDK_AUTO_SWITCH 0 1 = run sdk_mode.sh half_sdk automatically when the guard fails, then recheck WALKER_C1_SINGLE_ACTION_SMOOTH_S 0.15 Smoothing window (seconds) for a single sync action; only affects sync; 0 triggers a warning

See Real-robot deployment for all variables, the ROBOT_MODELS registry, and safety prechecks.

docs.text: Symptom Fix joint_config 'walker_c1_26d' not registered Plugin not installed: python /ubt_IL/walker_c1/init_walker_c1.py Conversion fails with a dimension mismatch (31 6) The data was not collected by ubt_sim walker_c1; verify the source or set CONFIG= explicitly Training fails because a camera key is missing observation.images.camera_head was not written; check meta/info.json Normalization explodes (QUANTILES NaN/Inf) Constant dimensions in the data (the left hand stays near 0 in this task). Use the 13D config or drop dead dimensions rollout precheck reports a dimension mismatch Policy dimension and ROBOT_MODEL disagree; confirm whether training used the 26D or 13D dataset Camera timeout Check the topic name, ROS_DOMAIN_ID, and QoS (must be BEST_EFFORT); on the real robot use head_stereo_left/color/raw + shm_msgs/Image6m torch.cuda.is_available() is False The container lacks NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES / NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES; start it with run.sh start The left hand never moves The left hand stays near 0 in the current collection batch (the task only uses the right hand); this is expected

docs.title: Walker C1 EDU: Real-Robot Deployment (Rollout)
docs.text: Deployment script: ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/rollout.sh, shared by simulation and real-robot deployment (differences are described in the workflow pages). This page covers all parameters, the half_sdk guard, safety prechecks, and online evaluation.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The robot is powered, standing, and switched to developer mode + half_sdk (C1 arms accept ROS 2 commands only in HalfSdkActive).
  • Place the robot in a safe position; use DURATION=10 for the first short validation; keep the emergency stop within reach.
  • The real-robot deployment container runs on the robot's Thor board. Copy the project and model to the board, then build and start the container (run.sh detects Thor and switches to Dockerfile.thor).
  • ROS_DOMAIN_ID defaults to 0 on hardware. DDS must match the main control stack (rmw_cyclonedds_cpp + cyclonedds_thor.xml, injected automatically by the container).

docs.title: Deployment matrix
docs.text: Scenario Key command Real robot, 13D model (right arm + right hand) WALKER_C1_REAL=1 ROBOT_MODEL=walker_c1_13d Real robot, 26D model (both arms + both hands) WALKER_C1_REAL=1 ROBOT_MODEL=walker_c1_26d Feedback into simulation WALKER_C1_REAL=0 SDK_GUARD=0 RESET_MODE=sim-scene Long-running deployment Use the inference server (no cold start)

docs.title: Deployment steps (real robot)
docs.text:
# 0. Switch to SDK control (developer mode -> legs STAND -> half_sdk; idempotent)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/sdk_mode.sh half_sdk
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/sdk_mode.sh check      # 0 = deployable, 2 = not satisfied

# 1. Camera check (real head left, shm_msgs/Image6m)
python3 /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/preview_camera.py --once --save-frame /tmp/c1.jpg \
  --msg-type image6m --topic /sensor/camera/head_stereo_left/color/raw

# 2. Move to the ready pose (three stages; dry-run first to inspect targets and durations)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/robot_ready.sh --dry-run
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/robot_ready.sh

# 3. Deploy the real-robot 13D model (async inference)
WALKER_C1_REAL=1 SDK_GUARD=1 \
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_real_13d_act_1RGB/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
ROBOT_MODEL=walker_c1_13d \
INFERENCE_TYPE=act_async INFERENCE_HZ=1 \
FPS=30 DURATION=10 \
  bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/rollout.sh

# 4. Return home (14 arm joints at 0, arms straight down, hands open)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/robot_home.sh --dry-run
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/robot_home.sh

docs.title: SDK modes (half_sdk)
docs.text:
developModeState Arm commands Notes NormalActive (normal) Ignored Built-in motion control owns the body; only CC-API skills can be invoked HalfSdkActive (half_sdk) Executed The only mode for VLA: SDK controls head/arms/waist, the system keeps balance (requires legStatus=standing) FullSdkActive (full_sdk) Executed All motors handed over, built-in balance disabled; the robot must be suspended. Do not use for VLA 
bash sdk_mode.sh status     # work mode / motion permission / legs / e-stop
bash sdk_mode.sh check      # validate only, 0 = deployable, 2 = not satisfied
bash sdk_mode.sh half_sdk   # develop -> legs STAND -> half_sdk
bash sdk_mode.sh normal     # back to normal (keep developer mode)
bash sdk_mode.sh work-mode joystick   # exit developer mode
  • By default commands run over SSH in the robot developer container (ubt@192.168.11.3:2222). For CI/scripted use, set WALKER_C1_SDK_PASSWORD for non-interactive login.
  • half_sdk is idempotent: if already in half_sdk it only prints the state. If the legs are not standing, it first runs skill A000004 to switch to STAND (--no-leg-stand disables this).

docs.title: Deployment guard
docs.text:
rollout.sh, robot_ready.sh / robot_home.sh (without --dry-run), and inference_server.sh call sdk_guard.sh before startup and refuse to run outside half_sdk:

SDK_GUARD=1        # real-robot default (1 when WALKER_C1_REAL=1): enforce
SDK_GUARD=auto     # validate only when a real robot is detected (simulation default)
SDK_GUARD=0        # skip (offline debugging only)
SDK_AUTO_SWITCH=1  # automatically run sdk_mode.sh half_sdk and recheck on failure

docs.title: Ready / home poses (robot_ready.sh / robot_home.sh)
docs.text:
Command Purpose robot_ready.sh Three-stage ready pose: raise shoulder → fold elbow → ready pose (≥5 s each) + open both hands robot_ready.sh --dry-run Print target poses and stage durations only robot_ready.sh --head-pitch 0.5 Adjust the head-down angle (default 0.65 rad) robot_home.sh Three-stage exact reverse to home (all 14 arm joints at 0) robot_home.sh --dry-run Print targets only

The ready pose is an absolute target, not a zero position. When standing with arms hanging naturally, the hands are below the table, so the motion must be staged to avoid sweeping the hand across the table edge.

docs.title: Safety precheck
docs.text:
Before deployment, an action-dimension precheck runs: output_features.action.shape[0] must match the robot config action_order dimension, otherwise deployment is refused.

  • ROBOT_MODEL must match the training DOF (see the table below).
  • If the policy has no action names, set ALLOW_DIM_ONLY_POLICY=1 (enabled by default).
  • Hand limits are clipped on both the plugin and bridge sides (plugin hand_joint_limits → to_bridge_config() → bridge).

docs.title: Environment variables (rollout.sh)
docs.text: Variable Default Description POLICY_PATH Required, no default Checkpoint directory (containing config.json) ROBOT_MODEL Real: walker_c1_13d / sim: walker_c1_26d ROBOT_MODELS key (also --robot.joint_config), switched by WALKER_C1_REAL ROBOT_CONFIG configs/<ROBOT_MODEL>.json Hardware config JSON (selected from ROBOT_MODEL) ROBOT_TYPE walker_c1 Plugin registration name WALKER_C1_REAL 1 1 = real robot (13d/task/act_async/guard/real camera); 0 = simulation/offline EPISODES 1 Number of episodes; the base strategy does not support multi-episode runs, so values >1 use an outer loop with a reset per episode DURATION 30 Maximum seconds per episode FPS 15 Control loop FPS (use FPS=30 for 30 fps datasets) TASK walker c1 pick place Task description RESET_MODE Real: task / sim: sim-scene Reset before each episode: sim-scene / task / both / none ALLOW_DIM_ONLY_POLICY 1 1 = dimension-only check; 0 = also check action_feature_names INFERENCE_TYPE Real: act_async / sim: sync sync / act_async (chunk → bridge blending at 300 Hz) INFERENCE_HZ Real: 1 / sim: 2 act_async replanning rate EXECUTION_HORIZON 0 Truncate act_async chunks after N steps (0 = no truncation) PREVIEW_CAMERA 0 1 = also open the preview window CAMERA_TOPIC Head left when WALKER_C1_REAL=1 Camera topic (simulation overrides to /sensor/camera/head/color/raw) CAMERA_MSG_TYPE shm_msgs/Image6m when WALKER_C1_REAL=1 Camera message type (simulation: sensor_msgs/Image) SDK_GUARD Real: 1 / sim: auto half_sdk guard SDK_AUTO_SWITCH 0 1 = automatically switch to half_sdk when the guard fails WALKER_C1_SINGLE_ACTION_SMOOTH_S 0.15 Smoothing window (seconds) for a single sync action; 0 disables; only affects sync ZMQ_HOST 127.0.0.1 Bridge address (use the robot-side IP for cross-machine deployment)

docs.title: Robot configuration (ROBOT_MODELS registry)
docs.text:
Registry key Dimension End effector Config file walker_c1_13d 13D (right arm 7 + right hand 6) Right dexterous hand (13D variant; left hand held at home via inactive_fill) configs/walker_c1_13d.json walker_c1_26d 26D (left arm 7 + right arm 7 + left hand 6 + right hand 6) Both dexterous hands configs/walker_c1_26d.json

In the 13D config, action_order contains only the right arm and right hand; body.groups still keeps left_arm, and inactive_fill fills the left arm 7 + left hand 6 with home values and sends them (hold position on hardware, home in simulation).

docs.title: Online evaluation (recording inference trajectories)
docs.text: Set RECORD_ACTIONS=1 (and RECORD_OUTPUT_DIR) during deployment to record rollout actions for analyzing model predictions, robot execution, and ACT blending. Records are saved under ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/output by default.

docs.title: Offline policy evaluation
docs.text: Run the offline MSE evaluation (ubt_IL/scripts/eval/eval_policy.py) before deployment; see Imitation Learning Platform §5.

docs.title: Inference server (warm start)
docs.text:
For long-running or multi-task deployment, use the inference server to avoid a cold start each time (rollout.sh must load the policy and start the bridge on every run). It supports launch/load/start/stop/home/status/watch/shutdown; see Inference server.

start / home / shutdown move the robot; keep the operator next to it.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Symptom Fix Robot does not move Does preview_camera.py --once produce an image? Is ROS_DOMAIN_ID / RMW consistent with the robot? Check the ros2_walker_c1_bridge log Only part of the arm moves Policy dimension and action_order mismatch (the precheck exits), or the left hand is all zeros throughout the data (the task only uses the right hand; normal) Motion jitter Increase FPS and --inference-hz, or switch to act_async chunk blending Camera timeout Verify topic name and message type; QoS must be BEST_EFFORT; real shm_msgs/Image6m must be specified explicitly reset.py reports No module named rclpy Use reset.sh (runs /usr/bin/python3), not the venv python3 Port already in use ss -lntp \| grep 566; do not run two bridges on the same host Arm does not return after exit disable_torque_on_disconnect was set false, or the bridge was killed externally sdk_mode.sh reports legs are not standing Switch to standing with the remote/Web UI, or let the script run A000004 (enabled by default) developModeState=sdk_error Press the emergency stop → exit developer mode or restart motion control, then run half_sdk again

docs.title: Walker C1 EDU: Inference Server (Warm Start)
docs.text:
Keep the policy resident in a container on the robot side (or GPU side). The operator machine controls it remotely over ZMQ: load a model, hot-swap checkpoints, start/stop execution, return home, and subscribe to status.

Operator inference_client.py ──ZMQ REQ 5690──► inference_server (lerobot venv)
                              ◄──ZMQ PUB 5691──   │
                                                  ├─ lerobot-rollout (26D / 13D)
                                                  └─ ros2_walker_c1_bridge (ZMQ 5661/5662)

docs.title: 1. Scripts
docs.text: File Purpose scripts/deploy/walker_c1/inference_server.sh Start python -m lerobot.scripts.inference_server in the background (5690/5691) scripts/deploy/walker_c1/inference_client.py Command client / status subscriber scripts/deploy/walker_c1/inference_client.sh Thin wrapper (prefers /lerobot/.venv/bin/python)

docs.title: 2. Quick start
docs.text:
# Robot side (inside the container): confirm/switch to half_sdk (the service validates and refuses otherwise)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/sdk_mode.sh half_sdk

# Background + warm start (set WALKER_C1_REAL=1 on hardware to enable the guard)
# Verified on hardware (Nov 2026): 13D real-robot model
WALKER_C1_REAL=1 \
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_real_13d_act_1RGB/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
  bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/inference_server.sh

# Operator side
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/inference_client.sh status
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/inference_client.sh start
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/inference_client.sh home
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/inference_client.sh stop
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/inference_client.sh shutdown

launch starts the service and polls until READY:

bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/inference_client.sh launch \
  --policy-path /ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_real_13d_act_1RGB/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
  --robot-type walker_c1 --robot-model walker_c1_13d \
  --inference-hz 2 --fps 30

Remote launch (SSH + docker exec on the machine running the container):

bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/inference_client.sh launch --remote \
  --host 192.168.11.3 --ssh-user ubt --ssh-port 22 --container lerobot-tienkung \
  --policy-path /ubt_IL/model/.../pretrained_model \
  --robot-type walker_c1 --robot-model walker_c1_26d

Inference backend recommendation (Walker series): prefer INFERENCE_TYPE=act_async (default). sync is for debugging only and must keep single-action smoothing (WALKER_C1_SINGLE_ACTION_SMOOTH_S, default 0.15 s; setting 0 triggers a warning).

--robot.type is not hard-coded: it uses the robot_type from the load command first, then the ROBOT_TYPE environment variable, and defaults to walker (preserving walker_s2 behavior). The C1 client forwards walker_c1.

docs.title: 3. Client commands
docs.text: Command Description launch Start the service (locally or with --remote) and wait for READY load Hot-swap checkpoint / robot model (--policy-path, --robot-type, --robot-model) start / stop Start / stop sending actions (stop stops immediately; C1 motion control holds the current pose) home Smoothly return home (chunk path, 2 s) status Query status once watch Subscribe to the PUB status stream (state/loop_hz/chunk_id/robot_connected/uptime_s) shutdown Shut down the service

docs.title: 4. State machine
docs.text:
LOADING ──► READY ⇄ RUNNING
              │         │
              ├──► RETURNING_HOME
              ├──► ERROR
              └──► SHUTTING_DOWN
  • READY: model loaded, robot connected, no actions being sent
  • RUNNING: inference and action publishing at inference_hz
  • RETURNING_HOME: returning home; goes back to READY when finished

docs.title: 5. Environment variables
docs.text:
Server (inference_server.sh)

Variable Default Description POLICY_PATH — (required) pretrained_model directory CAMERA_TOPIC /sensor/camera/head_stereo_left/color/raw Camera topic (C1 real head left; simulation uses /sensor/camera/head/color/raw) CAMERA_MSG_TYPE shm_msgs/Image6m Camera message type (real: shm_msgs/Image6m; simulation: sensor_msgs/Image) ROBOT_TYPE walker_c1 LeRobot plugin registration name ROBOT_MODEL walker_c1_13d ROBOT_MODELS key (= --robot.joint_config) ROBOT_CONFIG Empty Explicit hardware config JSON; takes precedence over ROBOT_MODEL INFERENCE_TYPE act_async act_async / sync INFERENCE_HZ 1 Replanning rate (about 1 Hz measured) EXECUTION_HORIZON 0 Truncate chunks after N steps (0 = no truncation) FPS 15 Control loop FPS TASK walker c1 pick place Task description SERVER_CMD_PORT 5690 REQ command port SERVER_STATUS_PORT 5691 PUB status port ALLOW_DIM_ONLY_POLICY 1 Precheck dimensions only BLEND_HORIZON / BODY_PUBLISH_HZ / BODY_V_MAX Bridge defaults Chunk blending parameters (passed to the bridge) WALKER_C1_SINGLE_ACTION_SMOOTH_S 0.15 sync single-action smoothing window (seconds): expands each action into a short current→target trajectory executed at 300 Hz; 0 disables. Recommended 0.15 at FPS=15 and 0.1–0.15 at FPS=30

Client

Variable Default DEPLOY_CONTAINER lerobot-tienkung SERVER_CMD_PORT / SERVER_STATUS_PORT 5690 / 5691 --host 127.0.0.1 --camera-topic / --camera-msg-type /sensor/camera/head_stereo_left/color/raw / shm_msgs/Image6m

launch converts --camera-topic / --camera-msg-type into CAMERA_TOPIC / CAMERA_MSG_TYPE for the server script (for remote launch it prefixes env VAR=... bash ...). The camera is read only at service startup; load does not change the camera source at runtime.

docs.title: 6. FAQ
docs.text: Symptom Fix launch stays in LOADING Check /tmp/walker_c1_inference_server.log; usually a model path or camera timeout status cannot connect Check --host and ports; is the service in another container? Old model still used after load Check the model field with watch; confirm --robot-model matches the policy dimension action dim mismatch Policy dimension and ROBOT_MODEL disagree (26D / 13D); check the training dataset and launch arguments Robot still moves after stop In-flight chunks stop after at most ~1 tick; if motion continues, confirm the bridge was restarted with the new version (hold_trajectory active) Stale PID file /tmp/walker_c1_inference_server.pid; the singleton guard corrects it automatically

docs.title: Walker C1 EDU Real-Robot Workflow: Collect -> Convert -> Train -> Evaluate -> Deploy
docs.text:
Robot: Walker C1 EDU Data source: real-robot teleoperation/scripted collection (Thinker Studio or ubt_sim/teleoperation/control/walker_c1) Code: ubt_IL/scripts/{convert,train,eval,deploy}/walker_c1/

Simulation and the real robot share the same ROS 2 interfaces (mc_task_msgs / mc_state_msgs / sensor_msgs/Image) and are isolated by ROS_DOMAIN_ID. The policy deployment path sends only 26 dimensions (both arms + both hands) or 13 dimensions (right arm + right hand); the head/waist/legs hold their current positions.

✅ Verified on hardware (Nov 2026): the full loop works with 13D = right arm 7 + right hand 6 (ROBOT_MODEL=walker_c1_13d, 30 fps, head camera head_stereo_left/color/raw 640×512): dataset walker_c1_real_13d_1RGB (34 episodes / 11,406 frames) -> model walker_c1_real_13d_act_1RGB -> real-robot deployment.

Real robot ROS 2 ──► ubt_sim/teleoperation/control/walker_c1 (collection) ──► HDF5
                                                                             │
Container: convert.sh → train.sh → eval_policy.py → robot_ready.sh + rollout.sh
                                                                             │
LeRobot (3.12) ──ZMQ 5661/5662──► ros2_walker_c1_bridge.py (3.10) ──► real robot
