docs.text: Stage Location Command Switch SDK control Operator machine / container bash scripts/deploy/walker_c1/sdk_mode.sh half_sdk Real-robot collection Operator machine / ubt_sim container teleoperation/control/walker_c1/save_data.sh Container Operator machine cd ubt_IL/docker && bash run.sh start && bash run.sh bash Conversion Container scripts/convert/walker_c1/convert.sh Training Container (GPU) scripts/train/walker_c1/train.sh Evaluation Container scripts/eval/eval_policy.py Deployment Container (robot side) robot_ready.sh + rollout.sh

docs.title: 1. Real-robot prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Switch to SDK control (half_sdk required): C1 arms accept ROS 2 joint commands only in workMode=develop + developModeState=HalfSdkActive (normal ignores commands; full_sdk hands over whole-body balance and is not used for VLA). The deployment script performs the full sequence (enter developer mode → legs STAND → half_sdk) over SSH in the robot's developer container (ubt@192.168.11.3:2222):
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/sdk_mode.sh status     # work mode / motion permission / legs / e-stop
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/sdk_mode.sh check      # validate only (0 = deployable)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/sdk_mode.sh half_sdk   # switch
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/sdk_mode.sh normal     # restore normal

rollout.sh / robot_ready.sh / robot_home.sh / inference_server.sh include the guard and refuse to run outside half_sdk (on hardware set WALKER_C1_REAL=1 or SDK_GUARD=1; simulation uses the default SDK_GUARD=auto and skips the check).

  1. ROS domain: the real robot defaults to ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0; simulation and real deployment must use the same value. Set both to 146 when isolation is needed.

  2. DDS: Thor (C1 onboard compute) must use the same RMW as the main control stack — the robot stack uses rmw_cyclonedds_cpp + CYCLONEDDS_URI (bound to mgbe2_0, local 192.168.11.3). docker/run.sh injects the same environment and mounts docker/cyclonedds_thor.xml (CYCLONEDDS_URI=file:///opt/cyclonedds_thor.xml), so no manual setup is needed. Two field-tested caveats when editing the config:

  3. <Interfaces> must be inside <General> (Humble's CycloneDDS 0.10+). Under <Domain> it reports unknown element and falls back to the default NIC. List only mgbe2_0, not lo (not multicast).

  4. Domain 0 has many participants; the default limit raises Failed to find a free participant index for domain 0. The config sets ParticipantIndex=none and MaxAutoParticipantIndex=120.

For FastDDS (simulation/remote machines), set RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_fastrtps_cpp and add the local NIC IP (Thor 192.168.11.3, Walker peer 192.168.11.99) to the docker/fastdds_no_shm.xml whitelist.

  1. State self-check (inside the container, after run.sh bash):
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
source /ubt_IL/walker_s2/walker_sdk_ros2/install/setup.bash
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0
ros2 topic hz /mc/sdk/robot_state                                 # measured ≈ 460-490 Hz on Thor
ros2 topic hz /sensor/camera/head_stereo_left/color/raw           # shm_msgs/Image6m
ros2 topic info -v /mc/sdk/robot_command                          # should have subscribers (SDK control active)

The real-robot RobotState contains only 19 joints (14 arm + 2 head + 3 waist, no legs). The bridge selects the 14 arm joints by name, so it is unaffected; head/waist/legs are not part of the policy and are not commanded.

  1. Safety: place the robot in a safe position; use DURATION=10 for the first short validation; keep the emergency stop within reach.

docs.title: 2. Real-robot collection
docs.text:
# Inside the ubt_sim container (same domain as the robot; do not reuse simulation processes)
bash teleoperation/control/walker_c1/save_data.sh
bash teleoperation/control/walker_c1/save_data.sh --batch 20

The output matches simulation: ubt_sim/dataset/walker_c1/<epoch>/trajectory.hdf5 (15 Hz, 31 body joints + 6+6 hand channels, one RGB stream). You can also use the Thinker Studio teleoperation platform and export a LeRobot v3 dataset directly.

The collection side needs the real camera topics — C1 hardware does not publish /sensor/camera/head/color/raw; it provides:

Topic Type Notes /sensor/camera/head_stereo_left/color/raw shm_msgs/Image6m Policy input: 1920×1536, yuv422 (UYVY), step=3840, fixed 6 MB ~~/sensor/camera/head_stereo_left/color/compressed~~ sensor_msgs/CompressedImage No longer published after the onboard vision stack restart head_stereo_right / head_fisheye_left,right / mono_chin / wrist_left,right Same family Other views

Aspect ratio: native 1920×1536 (5:4). The collection side stores JPEG at half size (960×768, still 5:4). Training and deployment consistently use 640×512 (5:4, exactly 1/3 of 1920×1536) with no cropping and no aspect-ratio change.

Use WALKER_C1_CAMERA_TOPIC + WALKER_C1_CAMERA_MSG_TYPE for collection/deployment (the deployment script uses CAMERA_TOPIC / CAMERA_MSG_TYPE). Topics ending in /compressed are inferred as compressed images; everything else defaults to sensor_msgs/Image. The real shm_msgs/Image6m type must be specified explicitly, otherwise the subscription type does not match.

docs.title: 3. Start the container
docs.text:
cd ubt_IL/docker
bash run.sh build && bash run.sh start && bash run.sh check && bash run.sh bash

Thor (L4T r38 / sm_110) is selected automatically by env.sh, which uses Dockerfile.thor (image lerobot-tienkung:humble-thor, based on the robot's ros2_ws:humble-dyn). Do not use the Orin Dockerfile.arm64 (r36 base + sm_87 wheels; it does not run on Thor).

run.sh check should include:

  • [OK] walker_c1 plugin: installed
  • [OK] walker_c1 bridge: available
  • [OK] walker ROS2 msgs: installed (mc_state_msgs / mc_task_msgs, sharing the workspace with walker_s2)
  • [OK] torch: 2.9.0+cu130 | arch: ...,sm_110,... | kernel: ok
  • [INFO] RMW: rmw_cyclonedds_cpp | CYCLONEDDS_URI=file:///opt/cyclonedds_thor.xml

docs.title: 4.1 Conversion command
docs.text:
Verified path: real-robot 13D (config configs/walker_c1_real_13d_1RGB.json, 13D = right arm 7 + right hand 6, head camera 640×512, 30 fps):

CONFIG=/ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_c1/configs/walker_c1_real_13d_1RGB.json \
SRC_ROOT=/ubt_IL/dataset/walker_c1 \
REPO_ID=walker_c1_real_13d_1RGB \
FPS=30 \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_c1/convert.sh --overwrite
  • If the data is still in ubt_sim/dataset/walker_c1, omit SRC_ROOT (the script falls back automatically) or set it explicitly.
  • Real-robot recordings are 30 fps; keep the conversion FPS equal to the dataset frame rate. Use RESAMPLE_FPS for other rates.
  • For 26D real-robot data use walker_c1_real_26d_1RGB.json (dual-arm task).
  • Real hand ranges were verified: right hand thumb_swing ≤0.68 / thumb_mcp ≤0.82 / four fingers ≤0.85, all within deployment limits (0.96 / 1.04 / 1.57).

For simulation conversion see Simulation workflow · Data conversion.

docs.title: 4.2 Data visualization
docs.text:
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 lerobot-dataset-viz \
  --repo-id walker_c1_real_13d_1RGB \
  --episode-index 0 \
  --root /ubt_IL/dataset/walker_c1_real_13d_1RGB

Check especially: image resolution (3×512×640), state/action dimension and order (13D = right arm 7 + right hand 6), hand range, and empty episodes.

docs.title: 5. Training and evaluation
docs.text:
Verified path: real-robot 13D training (config train_config_walker_c1_real_act_13d_1RGB.json, dataset walker_c1_real_13d_1RGB, output walker_c1_real_13d_act_1RGB):

CONFIG=/ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_c1/configs/train_config_walker_c1_real_act_13d_1RGB.json \
OUTPUT_DIR=/ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_real_13d_act_1RGB \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_c1/train.sh

train.sh defaults to the simulation 26D config; real-robot training must set CONFIG= explicitly. When real lighting differs strongly from simulation, image_transforms is enabled by default in the config (color jitter / random affine).

Offline evaluation (real-robot dataset):

/lerobot/.venv/bin/python /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/eval_policy.py \
  --policy-path /ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_real_13d_act_1RGB/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
  --dataset-path /ubt_IL/dataset/walker_c1_real_13d_1RGB \
  --episodes 5 --inference-freq 1 --plot \
  --plot-dir /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/output/eval_walker_c1_real_13d_act \
  --output /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/output/eval_walker_c1_real_13d_act/results.json \
  --device cuda

With small real datasets, inspect per-dimension curves for plausibility (hand jitter, wrist overshoot) instead of relying only on the total MSE.

docs.title: 6. Deployment
docs.text:
Real-robot deployment (on-site photo):

# ⓪ Switch to half_sdk (developer mode + half-body SDK; idempotent, only prints state if already ready)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/sdk_mode.sh half_sdk
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/sdk_mode.sh check      # 0 = deployable

# ① Camera check (real: head_stereo_left/color/raw, shm_msgs/Image6m)
python3 /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/preview_camera.py --once --save-frame /tmp/c1.jpg \
  --msg-type image6m --topic /sensor/camera/head_stereo_left/color/raw

# ② Move to the ready pose (dry-run first to inspect targets and stage durations)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/robot_ready.sh --dry-run
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/robot_ready.sh

# ③ Single-episode rollout (WALKER_C1_REAL=1 enables the half_sdk guard; refuses outside half_sdk)
#    Verified path: real-robot 13D model (on hardware ROBOT_MODEL defaults to walker_c1_13d)
WALKER_C1_REAL=1 SDK_GUARD=1 \
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_real_13d_act_1RGB/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
DURATION=10 FPS=30 RESET_MODE=task \
CAMERA_TOPIC=/sensor/camera/head_stereo_left/color/raw \
CAMERA_MSG_TYPE=shm_msgs/Image6m \
  bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/rollout.sh

# ④ Return home (home = all 14 arm joints at 0, arms straight down, hands open)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/robot_home.sh --dry-run
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/robot_home.sh

# ⑤ Optional warm-started inference server (see inference-server.md)
WALKER_C1_REAL=1 \
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_real_13d_act_1RGB/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
  bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/inference_server.sh
  • Ready pose includes a head-down angle of head_pitch=0.65 rad (37.2°): field tests show 0.50 only sees the table edge, while 0.65 covers the full table. Adjust with --head-pitch; --no-head leaves the head untouched. The three stages (raise shoulder → fold elbow → ready pose) default to ≥ 5 s each (15 s total + 0.5 s hold), and the log prints peak displacement and velocity (≈0.5 rad/s).
  • home is the exact reverse of the three ready stages (wrist/shoulder pitch to zero → unfold elbow → lower shoulder); measured final error max |pos| ≈ 0.02 rad. It moves only the arm and hand; head/waist/legs are untouched.
  • Inference backend: prefer act_async (default); serial sync is for debugging only and must keep single-action smoothing (default 0.15 s; setting 0 triggers a warning).
  • RESET_MODE: the real robot has no /sim/cmd_reset; use task (pose only) or none.
  • max_relative_target: null in the config JSON; set e.g. 0.05 rad/step when per-step limiting is needed.
  • disable_torque_on_disconnect=true: smoothly return home on exit (2 s chunk).

Real-robot deployment demo:

See Real-robot deployment for the full guard, registry, and safety precheck details.

docs.title: 7. FAQ
docs.text: Symptom Fix Arm does not move at all Run sdk_mode.sh check: is it develop + HalfSdkActive + standing? Then check whether /mc/sdk/robot_command has subscribers and whether ROS_DOMAIN_ID matches Only the right hand moves The left hand is all zeros in the data (task characteristic); the policy reproduces this, which is normal Joint 4 direction/name mismatch SDK docs call it elbow_roll, the URDF calls it elbow_pitch; the bridge tolerates aliases, but verify the sign on hardware Sudden motion Set max_relative_target; lower FPS; check hand limits Camera artifacts / no image Simulation sensor_msgs/Image encoding should be rgb8; real is shm_msgs/Image6m (UYVY); QoS must be BEST_EFFORT Arm does not return after exit disable_torque_on_disconnect was set false, or the bridge was killed externally Inference service unreachable Ports 5690/5691; check the state machine with inference_client.sh status Empty topic list / no /mc/* RMW mismatch: on hardware use rmw_cyclonedds_cpp + cyclonedds_thor.xml (see §1 item 3) Failed to find a free participant index CycloneDDS default participant limit is too low; use ParticipantIndex=none + MaxAutoParticipantIndex=120 Camera topic missing / no frames On hardware use CAMERA_TOPIC=.../head_stereo_left/color/raw + CAMERA_MSG_TYPE=shm_msgs/Image6m; green/purple colors mean UYVY is being decoded as YUYV torch.cuda.is_available() is False The container lacks NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all / NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=all (run.sh start sets them)

docs.title: Walker C1 EDU: Simulation Platform
docs.text:
The Walker C1 EDU simulation is built on NVIDIA Isaac Sim (Isaac Lab 2.2.0). A ROS2-ZMQ bridge publishes simulation state and images on exactly the same ROS 2 topics as the real robot, enabling sim-to-real consistent teleoperation and data collection. The whole environment runs in a Docker container.

C1 shares the same SDK topic surface (mc_task_msgs / mc_state_msgs) with Walker S2 EDU, but the message packages are isolated and selected by UBT_SIM_ROBOT=walker_c1. Both robots use simulation bridge ports 5655-5658, so they cannot run at the same time.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: Commands are split into two parts: build/enter the container on the host; launch simulation and collect data inside the container (container root is /ubt_sim).

docs.title: 1. Build and start the container (host)
docs.text:
cd ubt_sim/docker
bash run.sh build      # build the ROS 2 + Isaac Sim image
bash run.sh start      # create/start the container
bash run.sh init       # build robot message packages (including walker_c1_msgs), first time only
bash run.sh check      # verify GPU / ROS 2 / message packages / numpy<2

See Simulation Platform · Container Setup for the build workflow.

⚠️ Must be changed before building (real-robot or cross-machine deployment): edit interfaceWhiteList in ubt_sim/docker/fastdds_no_shm.xml and set <address> to the IP of the direct-link NIC (Thor side 192.168.11.3, Walker peer 192.168.11.99). The file is copied into the image at build time; changes after the build have no effect. Pure local simulation over loopback can keep the default.

docs.title: 2. Launch simulation (container)
docs.text:
# Enter the container (ROS 2 and C1 message packages sourced automatically)
UBT_SIM_ROBOT=walker_c1 bash run.sh bash

# Option 1: C1-specific script (GPU rendering + CPU PhysX, 100 Hz physics step by default)
bash scripts/start_c1_pick_place_sim.sh

# Option 2: unified launcher
UBT_SIM_TASK=UBTSim-WalkerC1-Parlor-v0 bash scripts/start_sim.sh

Startup prints the ZMQ ports, action joint order, and a hand joint limit/gain summary.

  • Press R to reset the robot/scene; Space requests saving the current episode (works with the ROS-side recorder).
  • When the simulation window closes, the exit trap in start_sim.sh stops the bridge automatically.

Demo (picking an apple from the table):

Common environment variables/arguments (combinable):

Variable / argument Purpose Default UBT_SIM_TASK Task name (determines the robot) UBTSim-TienkungPro-Parlor-v0; use UBTSim-WalkerC1-Parlor-v0 for C1 UBT_SIM_ROBOT Message package selection inside the container Set to walker_c1 when entering the container UBT_SIM_WALKER_C1_USD_PATH Override the robot USD usd/walker_c1_merged.usd UBT_SIM_C1_STEP_HZ Physics step rate 100 UBT_SIM_LOAD_ONLY=1 Load the scene only, no bridge Off --headless Run without a window Common on headless servers --device cpu\|cuda Execution device cpu (default in the C1-specific script)

docs.title: 3. Data collection (container, system Python 3.10)
docs.text:
# Single episode: reset scene -> ready pose -> one online-IK pick-and-place -> save only on success
bash teleoperation/control/walker_c1/save_data.sh

# Batch: 20 episodes, reset between episodes, save only successful ones
bash teleoperation/control/walker_c1/save_data.sh --batch 20

# Interactive recording (Enter/s/q)
bash teleoperation/control/walker_c1/save_data.sh --manual
  • Episode flow: reset scene -> task ready pose -> one online-IK pick-and-place -> save only if the task succeeds.
  • Sampling rate 15 Hz; one camera_head stream at 640×480 PNG, 31 body joints + 6 channels per hand.
  • Output path: /ubt_sim/dataset/walker_c1/<epoch seconds>/trajectory.hdf5 (directories 0777, files 0666).
  • Before collecting, verify /mc/sdk/robot_state is publishing (about 48 Hz) and keep hand gains at 10/1 with effort_limit_sim=2.

HDF5 layout for one episode:

Path Shape Meaning joint_observations/joint_position (T, 31) L arm 0-6 / R arm 7-13 / head 14-15 / waist 16-18 / legs 19-30 hand_observations/hand_left_position (T, 6) Left hand SDK 6 channels hand_observations/hand_right_position (T, 6) Right hand SDK 6 channels action_observations/* Same Most recently commanded values camera_observations/color_images/camera_head (T,) PNG byte stream, 640×480 timestamp (T,) Collection timestamp

docs.title: 4. Reset (container)
docs.text:
# Task ready pose (three stages: raise shoulder -> fold elbow -> ready pose)
/usr/bin/python3 teleoperation/control/walker_c1/reset.py --mode task

# Scene reset (equivalent to pressing R in the simulation window)
/usr/bin/python3 teleoperation/control/walker_c1/reset.py --mode sim-scene

reset.py also supports sim-task (scene + task ready pose) and sdk-home (all SDK joints at zero).

docs.title: 5. Dataset preview and playback (container)
docs.text:
# Preview an HDF5 episode (Rerun)
/usr/bin/python3 teleoperation/tools/playback_walker_c1.py --mode preview

# Action playback (same topics in simulation and on the real robot)
/usr/bin/python3 teleoperation/tools/playback_walker_c1.py \
    --episode dataset/walker_c1/<epoch seconds>/trajectory.hdf5 --mode control

See Playback for all options and safety notes.

docs.title: Simulation modules
docs.text: Module Path Description Docker orchestration ubt_sim/docker/run.sh Image build, container lifecycle, bridge start/stop Environment variables ubt_sim/docker/env.sh Container name, image, ROS_DOMAIN_ID Simulation launcher ubt_sim/scripts/start_sim.sh Detects the robot from UBT_SIM_TASK and starts the bridge C1-specific launcher ubt_sim/scripts/start_c1_pick_place_sim.sh GPU rendering + CPU PhysX, 100 Hz step Task definition ubt_sim/source/ubt_sim/task/walker_c1_parlor/ Parlor apple-picking scene Simulation config ubt_sim/config/walker_c1/parlor.yaml Scene/camera/device parameters ROS2-ZMQ bridge ubt_sim/teleoperation/bridges/walker_c1/ Bridge script + walker_c1_bridge_config.yaml Control and collection ubt_sim/teleoperation/control/walker_c1/ reset.py / pick_place_controller.py / save_data.sh / online IK Playback ubt_sim/teleoperation/tools/playback_walker_c1.py Preview / action playback Data output ubt_sim/dataset/walker_c1/<timestamp>/trajectory.hdf5 Collected episodes

docs.title: ZMQ ports
docs.text:
Port Purpose 5655 Control commands (bridge PUB) 5656 Robot state (bridge SUB) 5657 Raw camera images (RGB + depth, C++ bridge) 5658 JPEG stream (debugging)

The ubt_IL C1 plugin uses 5661/5662/5663, which do not conflict with the simulation bridge ports 5655-5658, so both can run together. See Architecture · ZMQ ports for the cross-robot overview.

docs.title: ROS 2 topics
docs.text: Direction Topic Type sub /mc/sdk/robot_command mc_task_msgs/RobotCommand sub /mc/left_hand/command, /mc/right_hand/command mc_task_msgs/JointCommand pub /mc/sdk/robot_state mc_state_msgs/RobotState (31 joints) pub /mc/{left,right}_hand/joint_states sensor_msgs/JointState (SDK 6-joint order) pub /sim/object_state std_msgs/String pub /sim/episode_complete std_msgs/Bool pub /sensor/camera/head/color/raw sensor_msgs/Image (BEST_EFFORT)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• bash run.sh check reports errors: follow the prompt and rerun bash run.sh init; verify numpy<2 and walker_c1_msgs.
  • Collection script fails to import rclpy / message types: make sure you are using /usr/bin/python3, not Isaac Sim Python, and that bash run.sh init has been run.
  • Bridge exits with RMW implementation not installed: the image only ships rmw_cyclonedds_cpp. start_sim.sh / save_data.sh detect it automatically; export it manually when starting the bridge yourself.
  • Address already in use (tcp://*:5656): a previous bridge did not exit cleanly. kill -9 the remaining sim_runner / ros2_zmq_bridge, confirm ports 5655-5658 are free, then restart.
  • Command streams mix when Walker S2 is also running: both use ports 5655-5658; run only one robot at a time.
  • Controller reports no /mc/sdk/robot_state: the bridge is not running (usually a port conflict). Check with ros2 topic hz /mc/sdk/robot_state (about 48 Hz).
  • Apple is missed or flies away: keep hand gains at 10/1 and effort_limit_sim=2; do not increase them to old debug values.
  • X11 unavailable / no simulation window: run xhost + on the host and verify DISPLAY is forwarded; on a headless machine use --headless with save_data.sh --batch.

After collection, continue with Imitation Learning Platform.

docs.title: Walker C1 EDU Simulation Workflow: Collect -> Convert -> Train -> Evaluate -> Deploy
docs.text:
Robot: Walker C1 EDU Data source: Isaac Sim collection (ubt_sim, task UBTSim-WalkerC1-Parlor-v0) Container: lerobot-tienkung (built/started by ubt_IL/docker/run.sh, project mounted at /ubt_IL)

This guide covers the complete workflow from raw simulation HDF5 to a LeRobot dataset, ACT training, offline evaluation, and finally feedback deployment into the simulator. All conversion/training/evaluation/deployment scripts run inside the ubt_IL container.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• 0. Workflow overview
  • 1. Prerequisite: simulation collection (ubt_sim)
  • 2. Start the container (ubt_IL)
  • 3. Data conversion (HDF5 -> LeRobot)
  • 3.1 Conversion command
  • 3.2 Data visualization
  • 4. Policy training
  • 5. Policy evaluation (offline MSE)
  • 6. Simulation deployment (closed-loop)
  • 7. FAQ

docs.title: 0. Workflow overview
docs.text:
ubt_sim HDF5 ──► convert.sh ──► LeRobot dataset ──► lerobot-train ──► checkpoint
                                                                  │
                                                                  ├─► eval_policy.py (offline)
                                                                  └─► rollout.sh (sim closed loop)
Stage Command Output Simulation collection ubt_sim/teleoperation/control/walker_c1/save_data.sh ubt_sim/dataset/walker_c1/<epoch>/trajectory.hdf5 Conversion scripts/convert/walker_c1/convert.sh ubt_IL/dataset/walker_c1_sim_{26d,13d}_1RGB Training scripts/train/walker_c1/train.sh ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_sim_26d_act_1RGB Evaluation scripts/eval/eval_policy.py scripts/eval/output/.../results.json Deployment scripts/deploy/walker_c1/rollout.sh Simulated arm motion

docs.title: 1. Prerequisite: simulation collection (ubt_sim)
docs.text:
See Simulation Platform for scene, reset, and playback details.

# ① Launch simulation inside the ubt_sim container (separate terminal)
UBT_SIM_ROBOT=walker_c1 bash run.sh bash
bash scripts/start_c1_pick_place_sim.sh        # or UBT_SIM_TASK=UBTSim-WalkerC1-Parlor-v0 bash scripts/start_sim.sh

# ② Collect: one episode by default; --batch 20 randomizes object poses
bash teleoperation/control/walker_c1/save_data.sh --batch 20
  • In the simulation window, R resets the scene and Space requests saving the current episode.
  • Output: ubt_sim/dataset/walker_c1/<epoch seconds>/trajectory.hdf5, 15 Hz, one camera_head stream at 640×480 PNG.
  • Before collecting, confirm /mc/sdk/robot_state is publishing (about 48 Hz) and hand gains are 10/1 with effort 2 N·m.

docs.title: 2. Start the container (ubt_IL)
docs.text:
cd ubt_IL/docker
bash run.sh build      # first time; Thor switches to Dockerfile.thor automatically
bash run.sh start
bash run.sh check      # expect [OK] for walker_c1 plugin / bridge / ROS2 msgs
bash run.sh bash       # enter the container; run the remaining commands there

Inside the container, /ubt_sim is a read-only mount. If ls /ubt_sim fails, the container was created with an old mount; rebuild it with bash run.sh rm && bash run.sh start.

docs.title: 3. Data conversion (HDF5 -> LeRobot)
docs.text: Simulation data is written to ubt_sim/dataset/walker_c1/<epoch seconds>/trajectory.hdf5. The ubt_IL container mounts ubt_sim/ read-only at /ubt_sim, so conversion reads it directly without copying.

docs.title: 3.1 Conversion command
docs.text:
# Convert one episode first to validate the pipeline
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_c1/convert.sh --save_one true --overwrite

# Full run (26D: both arms + both hands)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_c1/convert.sh --overwrite

# 13D (right arm + right hand, single-arm task)
DIM=13 bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_c1/convert.sh --overwrite

Defaults: DIM=26, CONFIG=configs/walker_c1_sim_26d_1RGB.json, REPO_ID=walker_c1_sim_26d_1RGB, FPS=15, TASK_NAME=walker_c1_sim_pick_place, HDF5_REL_PATH=trajectory.hdf5, TAIL_TRIM=10.

Common overrides: REPO_ID, TASK_NAME, FPS, SRC_ROOT, TGT_PATH, TRIM_STATIONARY. Run bash convert.sh --help for all options.

Validation:

python - <<'PY'
import json
info = json.load(open("/ubt_IL/dataset/walker_c1_sim_26d_1RGB/meta/info.json"))
print(info["total_episodes"], info["features"]["observation.state"]["shape"],
      info["features"]["observation.images.camera_head"]["shape"])
PY

Expected output: 11 [26] [3, 240, 320] (the episode count depends on how much data was collected).

The repository ships about 11 episodes × 100 frames, enough only for smoke tests and pipeline validation. Collect more data for real simulation training (50+ episodes recommended).

docs.title: 3.2 Data visualization
docs.text:
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 lerobot-dataset-viz \
  --repo-id walker_c1_sim_26d_1RGB \
  --episode-index 0 \
  --root /ubt_IL/dataset/walker_c1_sim_26d_1RGB

--root must point to the dataset directory containing meta/; --episode-index visualizes one episode at a time.

docs.title: 4. Policy training
docs.text:
# Smoke test: 2 steps, no checkpoint
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_c1/train.sh --steps=2 --save_checkpoint=false

# Full training (default ACT / 26D simulation config)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_c1/train.sh

# Override common parameters
OUTPUT_DIR=/ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_sim_26d_act_1RGB_v2 \
STEPS=50000 SAVE_FREQ=5000 BATCH_SIZE=8 \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_c1/train.sh

# Resume (CONFIG points to train_config.json inside the checkpoint)
CONFIG=/ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_sim_26d_act_1RGB/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model/train_config.json \
RESUME=true bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_c1/train.sh

Key config (configs/train_config_walker_c1_sim_act_26d_1RGB.json):

Item Value Policy ACT, chunk_size=n_action_steps=100 Input observation.images.camera_head [3,240,320] + observation.state [26] Output action [26] Training batch_size=8, steps=30000, save_freq=5000

Output: checkpoints/<step>/pretrained_model (with config.json + model.safetensors) and checkpoints/last.

docs.title: 5. Policy evaluation (offline MSE)
docs.text:
/lerobot/.venv/bin/python /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/eval_policy.py \
  --policy-path /ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_sim_26d_act_1RGB/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
  --dataset-path /ubt_IL/dataset/walker_c1_sim_26d_1RGB \
  --episodes 5 \
  --inference-freq 15 \
  --plot \
  --plot-dir /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/output/eval_walker_c1_sim_26d_act \
  --output /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/output/eval_walker_c1_sim_26d_act/results.json \
  --device cuda

--inference-freq 15 emulates a 15 Hz deployment cadence; --plot writes per-joint GT-vs-prediction curves to --plot-dir (one per episode).

You can also run a single-frame inference check:

python /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/infer_check.py \
  --checkpoint /ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_sim_26d_act_1RGB/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
  --dataset /ubt_IL/dataset/walker_c1_sim_26d_1RGB --frame 0

docs.title: 6. Simulation deployment (closed-loop)
docs.text:
# ① Confirm simulation is running (ubt_sim container) and the ROS domain matches
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0        # must be identical for simulation and deployment (ubt_sim defaults to 0; set both to 146 to isolate)

# ② Camera
python3 /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/preview_camera.py --once --save-frame /tmp/c1.jpg

# ③ Reset + ready pose (three stages)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/robot_ready.sh

# ④ rollout (WALKER_C1_REAL=0 for simulation)
WALKER_C1_REAL=0 SDK_GUARD=0 RESET_MODE=sim-scene \
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_sim_26d_act_1RGB/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
  bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/rollout.sh

# ⑤ Multiple episodes (reset + restart per episode; the base strategy does not support --strategy.num_episodes)
EPISODES=5 DURATION=20 RESET_MODE=both \
WALKER_C1_REAL=0 SDK_GUARD=0 \
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/walker_c1_sim_26d_act_1RGB/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
  bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_c1/rollout.sh

Ports: C1 plugin 5661/5662/5663; ubt_sim C1 bridge 5655-5658; both can run together. For a 13D model add ROBOT_MODEL=walker_c1_13d (simulation defaults to walker_c1_26d).

Demo:

docs.title: 7. FAQ
docs.text: Symptom Fix Conversion reports "Found 0 episodes" No */trajectory.hdf5 under SRC_ROOT; verify HDF5_REL_PATH meta/info.json shows 640×480 images The config was modified; it should be image_size: [320,240] Training loss does not decrease Too little data (about 11 episodes); collect more or reduce dim_model rollout dimension precheck fails Policy dimension and ROBOT_MODEL disagree (26D / 13D), or ROBOT_CONFIG points to another robot's config Head/waist/legs slowly sink Joints not commanded by the simulator should hold HOME_POSE; check that no external node is publishing them No camera image Check preview_camera.py --topic, ROS_DOMAIN_ID, and QoS (BEST_EFFORT) Motion is very slow / stutters Increase FPS; use INFERENCE_TYPE=act_async INFERENCE_HZ=2 Apple missed / knocked away Residual state after reset is dirty: restart sim_runner, restore the apple with /sim/cmd_set_object_pose, then rerun robot_ready.sh

docs.title: Walker S2 EDU
docs.text: Walker S2 EDU is a humanoid robot with 34 DOF, equipped with two PGC two-finger grippers (optionally two 7-DOF V4 dexterous hands).

docs.title: Specifications
docs.text:
Item Specification DOF 34 (17 body + hands) End effectors 2 × PGC two-finger grippers (optional 2 × 7-DOF V4 dexterous hands) Common training dimensions 10D (right arm 7 + head 2 + right gripper 1) / 19D (17 body + 2 grippers) / 31D (17 body + 2 V4 hands, 14) LeRobot plugin ubt_IL/walker/lerobot_robot_walker USD model ubt_sim/assets/robots/walker_s2/s2_v1.usd Cameras Four: head stereo left/right + wrist left/right

Constant dimensions in single-arm / single-gripper data break normalization during training (QUANTILES NaN/Inf). For real-robot data, reduce the action space to 10D (right arm + head + right gripper).

docs.text: Task ID Scene Description UBTSim-WalkerS2-PartSorting-v0 Part sorting 4 parts + bins (default) UBTSim-WalkerS2-PickPart-v0 Part sorting Single-part picking: only one part remains on the table; use with pick_part.py

Platform entry points (shared architecture and commands are on the platform overview pages):

  1. Simulation workflow - End to end: simulation collection -> conversion -> training -> evaluation -> sim deployment
  2. Real-robot workflow - End to end: real collection -> conversion -> training -> evaluation -> real deployment
  3. Real-robot deployment - Rollout details, safety prechecks, ROBOT_MODELS registry, online evaluation

docs.title: Application Case: VLA Pick-and-Carry
docs.text:
Scenario: a tabletop VLA tidying task with the Walker S2 EDU humanoid robot. The robot picks parts from the table, places them into a storage box, and then carries the box to a distant target.

Approach:

  • Train a tabletop-tidying VLA model with the Thinker-IL-LAB toolchain.
  • Deploy with the inference server and hot-load the picking model; call the service with the inference client.
  • Build a task manager for robot navigation, carrying, and VLA picking to switch between multiple tasks and complete the full flow. For robot navigation and carrying, see the Walker S2 high-level motion interface.

docs.text:
