  • Inference server - Warm start, ZMQ commands, model hot-swap

docs.title: Walker S2 EDU: Imitation Learning Platform
docs.text:
Code: ubt_IL/scripts/{convert,train,eval,deploy} (run inside the container) Prerequisite: repository cloned and submodules initialized as described in Getting Started; HDF5 data ready (simulation collection or real-robot collection)

This page documents the shared conversion/training/evaluation/deployment workflow and configuration parameters for Walker S2 EDU. Data-source-specific commands are embedded in the corresponding workflow pages.

docs.title: 1. Environment (ubt_IL container)
docs.text:
See Imitation Learning Platform · Container Setup for build / start / bash. Run all remaining commands inside the container.

  • Two Python environments: use /usr/bin/python3 for ROS-related code and /lerobot/.venv/bin/python (default) for LeRobot scripts.
  • For real-robot deployment, the container is built on the robot Vision board (Jetson); the build script detects the board and builds an ARM container.

docs.title: 2. Data conversion (HDF5 -> LeRobot)
docs.text:
Script: /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/convert.sh (core converter ubt_IL/scripts/convert/common/convert_to_lerobot.py). It converts raw HDF5 into a LeRobot v3 dataset.

Conversion command (values for each variable are described in the config and environment tables below):

CONFIG=<conversion config JSON> \
SRC_ROOT=<HDF5 source directory> \
TGT_PATH=<LeRobot output root> \
REPO_ID=<output dataset name> \
TASK_NAME=<task name> \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/convert.sh

Examples (including a stationary-trimmed variant):

  • Simulation data: Simulation workflow · Data conversion
  • Real-robot data: Real-robot workflow · Data conversion

Conversion configs live in /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/configs/ and include field filtering and mapping. Choose or adapt one for your training needs:

Config Dimension Scenario walker_s2_sim_10d_2RGB.json 10D (right arm 7 + head 2 + right gripper 1) Simulation (recommended) walker_s2_sim_33d_4RGB.json 33D (with depth) Simulation walker_s2_real_10d_2RGB.json 10D Real robot (recommended, avoids normalization blow-up from constant dimensions)

convert.sh default config is not in the repository

convert.sh defaults to CONFIG=configs/walker_s2_real_19d_1RGBD.json, which does not exist in the repository. Always specify an existing config from the table above.

Common environment variables (defaults can be omitted; see bash convert.sh -h and Data Conversion):

Variable Description SRC_ROOT HDF5 root (default /ubt_IL/dataset/walker-s2-real-data; change it to the simulation data directory for sim data) TGT_PATH LeRobot output root (default /ubt_IL/dataset) CONFIG Conversion config JSON (see above; must be specified explicitly) REPO_ID Output dataset name (keep it consistent with training) TASK_NAME Task name (written to each frame's task field and used as the language condition) FPS Target frame rate (default 13 sim / 15 real; auto uses the source HDF5 rate) ROBOT_TYPE Robot type (default walker_s2, written to metadata) HDF5_REL_PATH HDF5 path relative to each episode directory (default hdf5/metadata_aligned.hdf5; simulation data uses trajectory.hdf5) VCODEC Video codec (default h264; jpeg / png also supported) TRIM_STATIONARY 1 enables stationary-frame trimming (see below) RESAMPLE_FPS Target frame rate; enables resampling when set (disabled by default)

Stationary-frame trimming

Stationary frames can trap the policy in a local stationary loop. Prefix the conversion command with TRIM_STATIONARY=1 \ to trim them (threshold/window/cap settings are described in Data Conversion).

19D real-robot data: the repository only provides a 10D real conversion config. For 19D, write a config based on the joint order in walker_s2_gripper_19d.json.

Output: a LeRobot v3 dataset under /ubt_IL/dataset/<REPO_ID>/ (meta/, chunk-000/ data parquet, videos/).

docs.title: 3. Data visualization
docs.text:
After conversion, inspect dataset quality with lerobot-dataset-viz. Checking data before training is important to avoid training blindly:

Visualization command 

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 lerobot-dataset-viz \
  --repo-id <REPO_ID> \
  --episode-index 0 \
  --root /ubt_IL/dataset/<REPO_ID>

Note: --root must point to the dataset directory containing meta/ (the repo_id directory itself), not its parent. HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 disables access to the HuggingFace Hub.

Examples: Simulation workflow · Visualization / Real-robot workflow · Visualization.

Check especially: image resolution, video frame rate, state/action dimension and order, grip range, and empty episodes. Simulation RGB is [3,240,320] (10D) or [3,480,640] (33D); real is [256,320] etc. Model input must match the training data — do not mix them.

docs.title: 4. Policy training (ACT)
docs.text:
Training script: /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/train.sh; configs in /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/configs/.

Training command (optional overrides are listed below; only explicitly set values override the config):

CONFIG=<training config JSON> \
DATASET_REPO_ID=<dataset repo_id> \
OUTPUT_DIR=<model output directory> \
STEPS=<training steps> SAVE_FREQ=<save interval> BATCH_SIZE=<batch size> \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/train.sh

Examples:

  • Simulation training: Simulation workflow · Training
  • Real-robot training: Real-robot workflow · Training

Without train.sh (call lerobot-train directly from /ubt_IL/lerobot):

# Smoke test (quick pre-training check, 2 steps, no checkpoint)
cd /ubt_IL/lerobot
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /lerobot/.venv/bin/lerobot-train \
  --config_path=/ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/configs/train_config_walker_s2_sim_act_10_2RGB.json \
  --steps=2 --save_checkpoint=false \
  --output_dir=/ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_act_smoke

# Continue training + tuning
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /lerobot/.venv/bin/lerobot-train \
  --config_path=/ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model/train_config.json \
  --resume=true \
  --steps=150000 \
  --dataset.image_transforms.enable=true      # enable image augmentation

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /lerobot/.venv/bin/lerobot-train \
  --config_path=/ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model/train_config.json \
  --resume=true \
  --steps=100000 \
  --optimizer.lr=5e-06                        # lower the learning rate for fine-tuning

Common overrides (only applied when the environment variable is explicitly set; HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 is enabled by default):

Variable Description CONFIG Training config JSON (default configs/train_config_walker_s2_sim_act_10_2RGB.json); ⚠️ defaults to the simulation config, so real training must specify a real config (e.g. train_config_pick_part_real_10d_2RGB.json) DATASET_REPO_ID / DATASET_ROOT Dataset name / root (default Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB / /ubt_IL/dataset; must match the conversion REPO_ID) OUTPUT_DIR Model output directory (default /ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB_act; checkpoints under checkpoints/<step>/pretrained_model/) STEPS Training steps (default 50000) SAVE_FREQ Checkpoint save interval (default 5000) BATCH_SIZE Batch size (default 8) SEED Random seed (default 1000) DEVICE Training device (default cuda) RESUME Resume training (default false; true resumes from the checkpoint) WANDB_ENABLE Enable wandb logging (default false)

docs.title: 5. Policy training (Pi0.5 VLA)
docs.text:
Pi0.5 is Physical Intelligence's ~4B-parameter vision-language-action (VLA) model, built on a PaliGemma-2B vision-language backbone plus a Gemma-300M action expert, using flow matching to generate actions.

Hardware: requires a GPU with ≥24 GB VRAM (e.g. RTX 4090); in bf16 it needs about 16-20 GB with gradient checkpointing. Pretrained weights: Pi0.5 must be initialized from lerobot/pi05_base; it cannot be trained from scratch. Download the weights before first use.

cd /ubt_IL/lerobot

# First training run
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /lerobot/.venv/bin/lerobot-train \
  --config_path=/ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/configs/train_config_walker_s2_sim_pi05.json

# Continue training + tuning
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /lerobot/.venv/bin/lerobot-train \
  --config_path=/ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_pi05/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model/train_config.json \
  --resume=true --steps=10000 \
  --policy.freeze_vision_encoder=false       # unfreeze the vision encoder

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /lerobot/.venv/bin/lerobot-train \
  --config_path=/ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_pi05/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model/train_config.json \
  --resume=true --steps=5000 \
  --policy.train_expert_only=true            # train only the action expert (freeze the VLM)

Key differences from ACT:

Item ACT Pi0.5 Model size ~30M ~4B Architecture ResNet18 + Transformer PaliGemma-2B + Gemma-300M Normalization MEAN_STD (all) QUANTILES (state/action) + IDENTITY (visual) Image size Original (360×640 etc.) Resize to 224×224 Action prediction VAE + absolute Flow matching Language input None Task description (requires a task field in the data) batch_size 8 4 Training steps 50,000 5,000 Optimizer AdamW (1e-5) AdamW (2.5e-5, cosine decay + warmup)

docs.title: 6. Policy evaluation (offline MSE)
docs.text:
Script (shared with TienKung): /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/eval_policy.py. It runs offline inference over a LeRobot dataset, computes the per-frame MSE between predicted and ground-truth actions, and can plot per-episode comparisons. Quantify policy quality before deployment.

Evaluation command:

/lerobot/.venv/bin/python /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/eval_policy.py \
  --policy-path <pretrained_model directory (config.json + model.safetensors)> \
  --dataset-path <LeRobot dataset directory containing meta/info.json> \
  --episodes <number of episodes> \
  --inference-freq <infer every N steps> \
  --plot --plot-dir <plot output directory> \
  --output <result JSON path> \
  --device cuda

Examples:

  • Simulation model: Simulation workflow · Evaluation
  • Real-robot model: Real-robot workflow · Evaluation
Argument Description --policy-path pretrained_model directory (containing config.json + model.safetensors) --dataset-path LeRobot dataset root (containing meta/info.json) --episodes Number of episodes to evaluate (default: all) --inference-freq Run inference every N steps and reuse the predicted chunk in between (emulates real deployment; 1 = every step) --plot / --plot-dir Per-episode prediction-vs-ground-truth plots and output directory --output Result JSON path --device cuda or cpu (default cuda, falls back automatically)

Once evaluation passes, continue with §7 Model deployment.

docs.title: 7. Model deployment
docs.text:
Script: /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/rollout.sh. It loads a checkpoint and sends actions to Isaac Sim or the real robot through the ROS2-ZMQ bridge. A safety precheck (action dimension match) runs before deployment and must pass before motion is allowed. Helper tools: robot_ready.sh (initialize/home), preview_camera.py (camera path check), inference_server.sh (warm-started inference service).

Deployment command (optional variables are listed below; unset values use script defaults):

POLICY_PATH=<checkpoint pretrained_model directory> \
ROBOT_MODEL=<robot DOF config> \
INFERENCE_TYPE=<inference engine> \
ZMQ_HOST=<simulation bridge/robot address> \
TASK=<task description> \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/rollout.sh

Deployment guides:

  • Simulation deployment (feedback into the simulator; recommended first): Simulation workflow · Model deployment
  • Real-robot deployment (ROBOT_MODELS registry and safety precheck): Real-robot workflow · Model deployment · Real-robot deployment
  • Inference server (warm start/external calls): Inference server

Common environment variables:

Variable Description POLICY_PATH Required, no default; checkpoint directory (containing config.json) ROBOT_MODEL ROBOT_MODELS registry key (default walker_s2_31d; walker_s2_10d = right arm + head + right gripper 10D, walker_s2_19d = 17 body + 2 grippers); must match the training DOF INFERENCE_TYPE Inference engine: sync (default) / act_async (asynchronous replanning with INFERENCE_HZ) INFERENCE_HZ act_async replanning rate (default 0.6) STRATEGY Rollout strategy (default base = autonomous) ZMQ_HOST Bridge address: 127.0.0.1 for simulation feedback (default); use the robot-side IP for cross-machine real deployment FPS Control rate (default 13, aligned with training fps) DURATION Run time (seconds, default 30) TASK Task description PREVIEW_CAMERA / RECORD_ACTIONS Camera preview window / rollout action recording switches

See Real-robot deployment for all variables, the ROBOT_MODELS registry, and safety prechecks.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Symptom Fix Conversion reports "config does not exist" The convert.sh default CONFIG is not in the repository; specify an existing config from configs/ Real-robot 19D data cannot be converted The repository only provides a 10D real config; for 19D, write one based on the joint order in walker_s2_gripper_19d.json Dataset frame rate differs from expected Collection runs at 15 Hz and conversion defaults to FPS=13 (real config uses 15); use FPS=auto to keep the source rate or RESAMPLE_FPS to resample Normalization explodes (QUANTILES NaN/Inf) Caused by 9 constant dimensions in 19D real data; convert with the 10D config (right arm + head + right gripper) to drop dead dimensions Long stationary segments; the policy stops during deployment Add TRIM_STATIONARY=1 during conversion Occasional non-convergence Insufficient data; collect more episodes; confirm image_transforms is enabled

docs.title: Walker S2 EDU: Real-Robot Deployment (Rollout)
docs.text: Deployment script: ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/rollout.sh, shared by simulation and real-robot deployment (differences are described in the workflow pages). This page covers all parameters, safety prechecks, and online evaluation.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• The robot is powered, standing, and in developer mode.
  • Startup sequence: power on, enable servos and press D to start internal motion control -> place the robot on the ground, hold A to enter standing mode. See the Walker S2 EDU development guide for remote details.
  • Walker real deployment runs on the robot Vision board; copy the project and model there, then build and start the container. The build script detects the board and builds the corresponding ARM container.

docs.title: Deployment matrix
docs.text: Scenario Key command 19D simulation model -> 19D PGC gripper hardware ROBOT_MODEL=walker_s2_19d 10D simulation model -> real deployment (act_async) ROBOT_MODEL=walker_s2_10d INFERENCE_TYPE=act_async Simulation feedback validation ZMQ_HOST=127.0.0.1 (start the simulation task and bridge first) Long-running deployment Use the inference server (no cold start)

docs.title: Deployment steps (real robot)
docs.text:
# 0. Enter developer mode -- ubt container on the robot control PC
ssh -p 2222 ubt@192.168.11.2    # password: Ubtubt@9880
# Request developer mode: true to enter, false to exit
ros2 service call /sys/task/developer_mode std_srvs/srv/SetBool "{data: true}"
# true = developer mode, false = normal mode
ros2 topic echo /sys/state/walker_mode

# 1. Build and start the inference container -- robot Vision board
# 1.1 Copy the project (code + models) to the Vision board
scp project-code-and-models /home/walker/
# 1.2 Log in to the Vision board and build the container
ssh walker@192.168.11.3          # password: aa
cd project-path/ubt_IL/docker
bash run.sh build
# 1.3 Start the container
bash run.sh start
bash run.sh bash

# 2. Initialize the pose (raise the arm above the table; use --home to return to zero)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/robot_ready.sh

# 3. Deploy the real-robot 10D model with asynchronous inference
ROBOT_MODEL=walker_s2_10d \
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/walker_pick_part_real_10d_2RGB_act/checkpoints/080000/pretrained_model \
INFERENCE_TYPE=act_async INFERENCE_HZ=1 \
FPS=13 DURATION=60 \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/rollout.sh

# 4. (Optional) Verify the camera path; specify camera topic/robot config
/usr/bin/python3 scripts/deploy/walker_s2/preview_camera.py --robot walker_s2_10d

Know the two machines: - Jetson 192.168.11.3 (SSH walker, password aa): runs the lerobot-tienkung container and inference. - Robot control PC 192.168.11.2 (SSH ubt, port 2222): developer mode / ROS 2. It does not run the inference container.

docs.title: Initialize / home (robot_ready.sh)
docs.text: Command Purpose robot_ready.sh Ready pose (--init, three safe stages, 13 s by default) robot_ready.sh --home Return to zero (three stages, 15 s by default); use after inference robot_ready.sh --legacy-init / --legacy-home Fall back to the old four-stage flow Other arguments Passed through to robot_control.py (e.g. --init-duration 20)

docs.title: Safety precheck
docs.text:
Deployment runs an action dimension precheck: policy output_features.action.shape[0] must match robot config action_order; otherwise deployment is refused.

  • ROBOT_MODEL must match the training DOF (see below).
  • If the policy has no action names, set ALLOW_DIM_ONLY_POLICY=1 (enabled by default).

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Default Description POLICY_PATH Required, no default Checkpoint directory (containing config.json) ROBOT_MODEL walker_s2_31d ROBOT_MODELS registry key (see below) ROBOT_CONFIG configs/<ROBOT_MODEL>.json Full path to the robot config (override for custom configs) ALLOW_DIM_ONLY_POLICY 1 Allow dimension-only matching when the policy has no action names STRATEGY base Rollout strategy FPS 13 Control rate DURATION 30 Run time (seconds) TASK walker s2 rollout Task description PREVIEW_CAMERA 1 Show the camera preview window RECORD_ACTIONS 1 Record rollout actions (RECORD_OUTPUT_DIR sets the output) INFERENCE_TYPE sync Inference engine (sync / act_async) INFERENCE_HZ 0.6 act_async replanning rate EXECUTION_HORIZON 0 Truncate chunks after N steps (0 = no truncation) ZMQ_HOST 127.0.0.1 Bridge address (local for simulation feedback; robot IP for cross-machine deployment)

Exported parameters: BLEND_HORIZON=10, BODY_PUBLISH_HZ=300, BODY_V_MAX=2.0 (bridge chunk blending and publish rate limiting).

docs.title: Robot configuration (ROBOT_MODELS registry)
docs.text: Registry key Dimension End effector Config file walker_s2_10d 10D (right arm 7 + head 2 + right gripper 1) PGC right gripper walker_s2_gripper_19d.json (10D is a subset) walker_s2_19d 19D (17 body + 2 grippers) PGC 1-DOF gripper walker_s2_gripper_19d.json walker_s2_31d 31D (17 body + 14 hands) V4 dexterous hand 7 DOF walker_s2_v4_hand_31d.json

docs.title: Online evaluation (recording inference trajectories)
docs.text: RECORD_ACTIONS=1 (enabled by default) records rollout actions for analyzing model predictions, robot execution, and ACT blending. Records are saved under ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/output.

docs.title: Offline policy evaluation
docs.text: Run the offline MSE evaluation (ubt_IL/scripts/eval/eval_policy.py, shared with TienKung) before deployment; see Imitation Learning Platform §6.

docs.title: Inference server (warm start)
docs.text:
For long-running or multi-task deployment, use the inference server to avoid a cold start (verified on hardware 2026-08-09: ~6 s warm-up to READY; start/stop/home/shutdown all pass). It supports start/stop/home/status/shutdown, model hot-swap with load, and remote launch. See Inference server.

start / home / shutdown move the robot; execute them next to the robot.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Symptom Fix Deployment reports a dimension mismatch Safety precheck refused: match ROBOT_MODEL to the policy dimension (10D -> walker_s2_10d, 19D -> walker_s2_19d, 31D -> walker_s2_31d) Robot does not move On hardware, confirm Bridge2 is running (5561/5562), the camera relay is running (5563), and developer mode is active; in simulation confirm ZMQ_HOST=127.0.0.1 and the simulation task is running Inference server start fails start/stop require INFERENCE_TYPE=act_async; the sync engine has no pause/resume semantics launch --remote fails Confirm --host is the Jetson 192.168.11.3 (SSH walker), not the control PC; the SSH user needs sudo docker exec permission Repeated inference server launch fails The singleton PID file /tmp/walker_inference_server.pid exists; shutdown cleanly or remove it manually Simulation and hardware camera sizes differ Simulation RGB is [3,240,320] (10D) or [3,480,640] (33D); hardware is [256,320] etc. Model input must match the training data — do not mix them

docs.title: Walker S2 EDU: Inference Server (Warm Start)
docs.text:
Every cold start of rollout.sh reloads the policy to CUDA and starts the bridge, which is slow. The inference server keeps a resident process that loads the model and connects to the robot/simulation bridge once. External clients can then use ZMQ commands start/stop/home/status/shutdown at any time and load models for hot-swapping, avoiding repeated cold starts.

It supports both simulation feedback deployment and real-robot deployment; only the bridge address and camera source differ.

docs.title: Scripts and architecture
docs.text:
Script Description ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/inference_server.sh Server: starts the resident inference service (pre-warms in the background to READY) ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/inference_client.sh Thin client wrapper: launch/load/start/stop/home/status/shutdown/watch ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/inference_client.py Client implementation (ZMQ commands + SSH remote launch)

The server is implemented in lerobot/src/lerobot/scripts/inference_server.py, reusing build_rollout_context + ACTAsyncChunkEngine.pause/resume without modifying the engine/bridge/walker core.

Architecture:

  • Warm-up: reuses build_rollout_context (policy + robot + processor + engine), same as lerobot-rollout.
  • Start/stop: ACTAsyncChunkEngine.pause()/resume()/reset() map to stop/start/new episode; the engine background thread pushes whole chunks to the bridge (300 Hz densify), while the main loop only feeds observations.
  • Control interface: ZMQ REP (5570) for commands + ZMQ PUB (5571) for status broadcast.
  • load hot-swap: rebuilds the whole context (stop the old engine + disconnect the old robot + rebuild the new cfg), including robot reconnection; the main thread skips observation acquisition during LOADING.
  • home: pause first, then send a smooth home_position chunk to avoid dual-source jitter.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
# 1. Start the service (inside the container; pre-warms in the background to READY in ~6 s; the engine is paused and the robot does not move)
ROBOT_MODEL=walker_s2_10d \
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB_act/checkpoints/020000/pretrained_model \
INFERENCE_TYPE=act_async INFERENCE_HZ=2 FPS=13 \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/inference_server.sh

# 2. Poll until READY (after that, start/stop/home respond in seconds without reloading)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/inference_client.sh status

# 3. Start / stop inference (start moves the robot; execute next to it)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/inference_client.sh start
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/inference_client.sh stop

# 4. Return home / shut down (both return to home_position)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/inference_client.sh home
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/inference_client.sh shutdown

Inside the container, python is not on PATH; use python3 or bash inference_client.sh (the latter picks /lerobot/.venv/bin/python automatically).

Scenario differences:

Scenario Bridge address Notes Simulation feedback ZMQ_HOST=127.0.0.1 (local bridge, container --network=host) Start the Isaac Sim task and bridge in the simulation container first Real robot Bridge started automatically by the container entrypoint Verified on hardware (2026-08-09): ~6 s warm-up to READY, start/stop/home/shutdown all pass; load not tested

docs.title: Client commands
docs.text:
bash inference_client.sh status                       # query state (state/model/loop_hz/chunk_id/...)
bash inference_client.sh start                        # start inference (engine reset+resume -> RUNNING)
bash inference_client.sh stop                         # stop inference (engine pause -> READY, hold current pose)
bash inference_client.sh home                         # return to home_position (pause, then smooth chunk)
bash inference_client.sh load --policy-path /ubt_IL/model/<other>/.../pretrained_model --robot-model walker_s2_10d
                                                       # hot-swap the model while running (full rebuild incl. reconnect)
bash inference_client.sh shutdown                     # shut down (home + kill bridge + exit)
bash inference_client.sh watch                        # subscribe to the status PUB stream (Ctrl-C to exit)

ZMQ commands connect to 127.0.0.1:5570 by default; the container uses --network=host, so from the host or a remote machine simply use --host <target IP>.

docs.title: Remote launch (load a model with explicit parameters)
docs.text:
Launch remotely from another machine (SSH + docker exec on the Jetson running the container, polling until READY):

bash inference_client.sh launch \
  --policy-path /ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB_act/checkpoints/020000/pretrained_model \
  --robot-model walker_s2_10d --inference-hz 2 --fps 13 \
  --remote --host 192.168.11.3 --ssh-user walker

Know the two machines: - Jetson 192.168.11.3 (SSH walker): runs the lerobot-tienkung container and inference. This is the --host for launch --remote. - Robot control PC 192.168.11.2 (SSH ubt, port 2222): dev_mode.sh developer mode / ROS 2. It does not run the inference container; do not use it as --host.

launch --remote defaults to --ssh-user ubt --ssh-port 22 --container lerobot-tienkung; use --ssh-user walker for the Jetson. The SSH user needs sudo docker exec permission (passwordless sudo). Without --remote, it launches bash inference_server.sh locally. --host is both the SSH target and the ZMQ polling target.

docs.title: State machine
docs.text:
LOADING (warm-up/rebuild) -> READY (idle) ⇄ RUNNING (executing)
home -> RETURNING_HOME -> READY
load -> LOADING -> READY
fatal error -> ERROR
shutdown -> SHUTTING_DOWN

docs.title: inference_server.sh
docs.text:
Variable Default Description POLICY_PATH Required, no default pretrained_model directory (containing config.json) ROBOT_MODEL walker_s2_31d ROBOT_MODELS registry key (walker_s2_10d / walker_s2_19d / walker_s2_31d) ROBOT_CONFIG Empty Custom robot config JSON (overrides ROBOT_MODEL) INFERENCE_TYPE act_async Inference engine (start/stop require act_async) INFERENCE_HZ 0.6 act_async replanning rate EXECUTION_HORIZON 0 Truncate chunks after N steps (0 = no truncation) FPS 13 Control loop FPS BLEND_HORIZON 10 Bridge chunk blending overlap points BODY_PUBLISH_HZ 300 Bridge 300 Hz body publish rate BODY_V_MAX 2.0 Bridge rate-limit maximum joint velocity SERVER_CMD_PORT 5570 ZMQ REP command port SERVER_STATUS_PORT 5571 ZMQ PUB status port PREVIEW_CAMERA 0 Server does not open the preview window by default (reserved for rollout.sh)

Difference from rollout.sh: it does not run a single duration-bounded rollout but stays resident; DURATION is meaningless. --use_torch_compile is not supported by the server (ACT needs no compile warm-up).

docs.title: inference_client.sh / inference_client.py
docs.text: Variable / argument Default Description SERVER_HOST / --host 127.0.0.1 Server host (also the SSH target) SERVER_CMD_PORT / --cmd-port 5570 ZMQ REP command port DEPLOY_CONTAINER lerobot-tienkung Container name for remote docker-exec DEPLOY_SSH_USER / --ssh-user ubt SSH user (use walker for the Jetson) DEPLOY_SSH_PORT / --ssh-port 22 SSH port

docs.title: Common launch arguments
docs.text: Argument Description --policy-path pretrained_model directory --robot-model ROBOT_MODELS registry key --inference-type / --inference-hz / --fps Engine type / replanning rate / control loop FPS --blend-horizon / --body-publish-hz / --body-v-max Bridge blending and rate-limit parameters --remote Launch remotely via SSH + docker-exec (without it, launch locally)

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Problem Cause / fix Repeated launch fails The singleton PID file /tmp/walker_inference_server.pid exists; shutdown cleanly or remove it manually start fails start/stop rely on act_async pause/resume; the sync engine has no such semantics, so use INFERENCE_TYPE=act_async Client cannot connect Confirm the server is READY (status); for remote access use --host <target IP> (container --network=host, so 5570 is the host port) Where is the log? /tmp/walker_inference_server.log load hot-swap does not take effect Not verified on hardware; it rebuilds everything including robot reconnection, commands are skipped during LOADING; wait for READY and check status to confirm the model switched

docs.title: Walker S2 EDU Real-Robot Workflow: Collect -> Convert -> Train -> Evaluate -> Deploy
docs.text: Complete closed loop for real-robot collection -> Walker S2 EDU deployment: real collection -> data conversion -> training -> evaluation -> real deployment. Code: ubt_IL/scripts/{convert,train,deploy}/walker_s2/.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• 0. Workflow overview
  • 1. Prerequisite: real-robot data collection
  • 2. Start the container
  • 3. Data conversion (HDF5 -> LeRobot)
  • 3.1 Conversion command
  • 3.2 Data visualization
  • 4. Policy training
  • 5. Policy evaluation (offline MSE)
  • 6. Model deployment (real robot)
  • 6.1 Inference deployment
  • 6.2 Inference server (warm start/external calls)
  • 7. FAQ

docs.title: 0. Workflow overview
docs.text: A[Real-robot teleoperation] --> B[HDF5 conversion] --> C[Model training] --> D[Offline MSE] --> E[Real deployment / inference server] --> F[Task validation]

docs.title: 1. Prerequisite: real-robot data collection
docs.text: Data is currently collected with the Thinker Studio teleoperation platform (see the official documentation), which can export LeRobot v3.0 datasets directly. You can also place collected real-robot HDF5 data under /ubt_IL/dataset/hdf5/ (or any SRC_ROOT) and proceed to conversion.

docs.title: 2. Start the container
docs.text:
Training/conversion/deployment all run in the lerobot-tienkung container:

cd ubt_IL/docker

# ⚠️ Must be checked before building: edit interfaceWhiteList in ubt_IL/docker/fastdds_no_shm.xml
# and set <address> to 192.168.11.99 (Walker S2 direct-link subnet). The file is copied into the image
# at build time; changes after the build have no effect.
bash run.sh build      # first time
bash run.sh start
bash run.sh bash       # enter the container; run conversion/training/evaluation there

The container has two Python environments: use /usr/bin/python3 for ROS and /lerobot/.venv/bin/python (default) for LeRobot. For real deployment, the container is built on the robot Jetson board; the build script detects the board and builds the corresponding ARM container.

docs.title: 3.1 Conversion command
docs.text:
Script: ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/convert.sh Core converter: ubt_IL/scripts/convert/common/convert_to_lerobot.py Configs: /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/configs/; choose or adapt one for your training needs.

Real-robot 10D example (right arm + head + right gripper, 2 RGB):

CONFIG=/ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/configs/walker_s2_real_10d_2RGB.json \
SRC_ROOT=/ubt_IL/dataset/walker-s2-pick-part-real-hdf5 \
TGT_PATH=/ubt_IL/dataset \
REPO_ID=Walker_S2_pick_part_real_10_2RGB \
TASK_NAME=walker_s2_pick_part \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/convert.sh

# Stationary-trimmed variant (removes grasp-waiting stationary segments to avoid local stationary loops)
TRIM_STATIONARY=1 \
CONFIG=/ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/configs/walker_s2_real_10d_2RGB.json \
SRC_ROOT=/ubt_IL/dataset/walker-s2-pick-part-real-hdf5 \
TGT_PATH=/ubt_IL/dataset \
REPO_ID=Walker_S2_pick_part_real_10_2RGB \
TASK_NAME=walker_s2_pick_part \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/convert.sh

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Default Description SRC_ROOT /ubt_IL/dataset/walker-s2-real-data HDF5 source directory (default real-data location) TGT_PATH /ubt_IL/dataset LeRobot output root CONFIG configs/walker_s2_real_19d_1RGBD.json Conversion config (the default file is not in the repository; always specify an existing config) REPO_ID Walker_S2_real_19_1RGBD Output dataset repo_id (local directory name + HF repo name) ROBOT_TYPE walker_s2 Robot type (written to metadata) TASK_NAME walker_s2_real Task name (written to metadata) FPS 15 Dataset frame rate (auto uses the source HDF5 rate) VCODEC h264 Video codec (h264/jpeg/png) HDF5_REL_PATH hdf5/metadata_aligned.hdf5 Source HDF5 relative path RESAMPLE_FPS Empty Resample to the target rate when set LABEL_ROOT Empty Label root (used when task labels exist) TRIM_STATIONARY Empty Trim stationary frames when set (--trim-stationary) STATIONARY_KEY action Key used for stationary detection STATIONARY_WINDOW Auto (0.3 × fps) Stationary detection window STATIONARY_THRESH 0.03 Stationary detection threshold STATIONARY_CAP 8 Maximum consecutive stationary frames STATIONARY_MIN_RUN 3 Minimum valid run length STATIONARY_RANGE_EPS 1e-3 Stationary interval tolerance

Pass-through options: --overwrite replaces an existing dataset; --save_one true uses single-file mode.

docs.title: 3.2 Data visualization
docs.text:
After conversion, inspect the dataset with the LeRobot visualizer:

# Inside the container:
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 lerobot-dataset-viz \
  --repo-id <dataset name> \
  --episode-index 0 \
  --root /ubt_IL/dataset/<dataset name>

Example:

# Visualize the dataset converted in section 3.1
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 lerobot-dataset-viz \
  --repo-id Walker_S2_real_10_2RGB \
  --episode-index 0 \
  --root /ubt_IL/dataset/Walker_S2_real_10_2RGB

Preview:

Check especially: image resolution, state/action dimension and order, grip range, and empty episodes.

docs.title: 4. Policy training
docs.text:
Training script: /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/train.sh Configs: /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/configs/; choose or adapt one for your training needs.

# Specify the real-robot training config explicitly, or override common parameters.
# Single-part policy: use the pick_part config + matching dataset.
CONFIG=/ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/configs/train_config_pick_part_real_10d_2RGB.json \
DATASET_REPO_ID=Wlaker_Pick_part_real_10d_2RGB \
OUTPUT_DIR=/ubt_IL/model/Wlaker_Pick_part_real_10d_2RGB_act \
STEPS=50000 SAVE_FREQ=5000 BATCH_SIZE=8 \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/train.sh

# Resume (CONFIG points to train_config.json inside the checkpoint)
CONFIG=/ubt_IL/model/Wlaker_Pick_part_real_10d_2RGB_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model/train_config.json \
RESUME=true \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/train.sh

Without train.sh (call lerobot-train directly with --xxx=yyy overrides; run from /ubt_IL/lerobot):

# Train from scratch
cd /ubt_IL/lerobot
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /lerobot/.venv/bin/lerobot-train \
  --config_path=/ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/configs/train_config_pick_part_real_10d_2RGB.json \
  --output_dir=/ubt_IL/model/Wlaker_Pick_part_real_10d_2RGB_act \
  --steps=50000 --save_freq=5000 --batch_size=8

# Resume
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /lerobot/.venv/bin/lerobot-train \
  --config_path=/ubt_IL/model/Wlaker_Pick_part_real_10d_2RGB_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model/train_config.json \
  --resume=true

docs.title: Overrides
docs.text:
Variable Default Description CONFIG $SCRIPT_DIR/configs/train_config_walker_s2_sim_act_10_2RGB.json Training config JSON (defaults to the simulation config; specify a real config such as train_config_pick_part_real_10d_2RGB.json) DATASET_REPO_ID From config Dataset repo_id DATASET_ROOT From config Dataset root OUTPUT_DIR From config Model output directory STEPS From config Total training steps SAVE_FREQ From config Checkpoint save frequency BATCH_SIZE From config Batch size SEED From config Random seed DEVICE From config Training device (cuda/cpu) RESUME false true resumes from the checkpoint WANDB_ENABLE false wandb logging switch

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 is enabled by default (offline training). Environment variables override config values only when explicitly set.

docs.title: 5. Policy evaluation (offline MSE)
docs.text:
Runs offline MSE evaluation (prediction vs ground truth) on a LeRobot dataset without connecting to the robot and generates per-episode comparison plots. Script (shared with TienKung): ubt_IL/scripts/eval/eval_policy.py.

Example: 

cd /ubt_IL/lerobot

/lerobot/.venv/bin/python /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/eval_policy.py \
  --policy-path /ubt_IL/model/walker_pick_part_real_10d_2RGB_act/checkpoints/080000/pretrained_model \
  --dataset-path /ubt_IL/dataset/Wlaker_Pick_part_real_10d_2RGB \
  --episodes 10 \
  --inference-freq 1 \
  --plot \
  --plot-dir /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/output/eval_walker_pick_part_real_10d_2RGB_act \
  --output /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/output/eval_walker_pick_part_real_10d_2RGB_act/results.json \
  --device cuda

Preview:

Argument Description --policy-path pretrained_model directory (containing config.json + model.safetensors) --dataset-path LeRobot dataset root (containing meta/info.json) --episodes Number of episodes to evaluate (default: all) --inference-freq Run inference every N steps and reuse the predicted chunk in between (emulates real deployment; 1 = every step) --plot / --plot-dir Per-episode prediction-vs-ground-truth plots and output directory --output Result JSON path --device cuda or cpu (default cuda, falls back automatically)

docs.title: Prerequisites:
docs.text:
• The robot is powered, standing, and in developer mode.
  • Sequence: power on, enable servos and press D to start internal motion control -> place the robot on the ground, hold A to enter standing mode. See the Walker S2 EDU development guide for remote details.
  • Walker real deployment runs on the robot Vision board; copy the project and model to the board, then build and start the container.

docs.title: 6.1 Inference deployment
docs.text:
Script: ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/rollout.sh.

Deployment steps:

# 0. Enter developer mode -- ubt container on the robot Vision board
ssh -p 2222 ubt@192.168.11.2/3  # password: Ubtubt@9880
# Request developer mode: true to enter, false to exit
ros2 service call /sys/task/developer_mode std_srvs/srv/SetBool "{data: true}"
# true = developer mode, false = normal mode
ros2 topic echo /sys/state/walker_mode

# 1. Build and start the inference container -- robot Vision board
# 1.1 Copy the project to the Vision board
scp project-code-and-models /home/walker/
# 1.2 Log in to the Vision board and build the container
ssh walker@192.168.11.3 # password: aa
cd project-path/ubt_IL/docker
# ⚠️ Must be checked before building: edit interfaceWhiteList in fastdds_no_shm.xml
# and set <address> to 192.168.11.99 (Walker S2 direct-link subnet); the file is copied at build time.
bash run.sh build
# 1.3 Start the container
bash run.sh start
bash run.sh bash

# 2. Initialize the pose (raise the arm above the table)
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/robot_ready.sh

# 3. Deploy the real-robot 10D model with asynchronous inference
ROBOT_MODEL=walker_s2_10d \
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/walker_pick_part_real_10d_2RGB_act/checkpoints/080000/pretrained_model \
INFERENCE_TYPE=act_async INFERENCE_HZ=1 \
FPS=13 DURATION=60 \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/rollout.sh

# (Optional) Verify the camera path; specify camera topic/robot config
/usr/bin/python3 scripts/deploy/walker_s2/preview_camera.py --robot walker_s2_10d

Demo (real-robot deployment):

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description POLICY_PATH Required, no default Checkpoint directory (containing config.json) ROBOT_MODEL walker_s2_31d ROBOT_MODELS registry key (see below) ROBOT_CONFIG configs/<ROBOT_MODEL>.json Full path to the robot config (override for custom configs) ALLOW_DIM_ONLY_POLICY 1 Allow dimension-only matching when the policy has no action names STRATEGY base Rollout strategy FPS 13 Control rate DURATION 30 Run time (seconds) TASK walker s2 rollout Task description PREVIEW_CAMERA 1 Show the camera preview window RECORD_ACTIONS 1 Record rollout actions (RECORD_OUTPUT_DIR sets the output) INFERENCE_TYPE sync Inference engine (sync / act_async) INFERENCE_HZ 0.6 act_async replanning rate EXECUTION_HORIZON 0 Truncate chunks after N steps (0 = no truncation) ZMQ_HOST 127.0.0.1 Bridge address (keep default when Bridge2 is on the same host; use the robot IP for cross-machine deployment)

docs.title: Online evaluation (recording inference trajectories)
docs.text: Set RECORD_ACTIONS=1 during deployment to record rollout actions for analyzing model predictions, robot execution, and ACT blending. Records are saved under ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/output.

docs.title: Robot configuration (ROBOT_MODELS registry)
docs.text: Registry key Dimension End effector Config file walker_s2_10d 10D (right arm 7 + head 2 + right gripper 1) PGC right gripper walker_s2_gripper_19d.json (10D is a subset) walker_s2_19d 19D (17 body + 2 grippers) PGC 1-DOF gripper walker_s2_gripper_19d.json walker_s2_31d 31D (17 body + 14 hands) V4 dexterous hand 7 DOF walker_s2_v4_hand_31d.json

docs.title: 6.2 Inference server (warm start/external calls)
docs.text:
Inference server script: ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/inference_server.sh Client script: ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/inference_client.sh

rollout.sh pays a long cold start on every run (policy load to CUDA + bridge startup). The inference server stays resident and pre-warmed; external clients use ZMQ commands start/stop/home/status/shutdown and can load models for hot-swapping VLA tasks and other tasks such as navigation or box carrying. See Inference server.

✅ Verified on hardware (2026-08-09): pre-warm to READY in ~6 s; start -> RUNNING; stop / home (no jitter) / shutdown all pass.

# 1. Start the service (inside the container; pre-warms in the background to READY; the engine is paused and the robot does not move)
cd /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2
ROBOT_MODEL=walker_s2_10d \
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/walker_pick_part_real_10d_2RGB_act/checkpoints/080000/pretrained_model \
INFERENCE_TYPE=act_async INFERENCE_HZ=1 FPS=15 \
bash inference_server.sh

# 2. Check whether the service is READY; if false, wait and query again
bash inference_client.sh status

# 3. Start / stop inference (moves the robot!)
bash inference_client.sh start
bash inference_client.sh stop

# 4. Return home / shut down (both return to home_position)
bash inference_client.sh home
bash inference_client.sh shutdown

start / home / shutdown move the robot; execute them next to the robot.

docs.title: Remote launch (load a model with explicit parameters)
docs.text:
Launch remotely from another machine (SSH + docker exec on the Jetson running the container, polling until READY):

cd /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2
bash inference_client.sh launch \
  --policy-path /ubt_IL/model/walker_pick_part_real_10d_2RGB_act/checkpoints/080000/pretrained_model \
  --robot-model walker_s2_10d --inference-hz 2 --fps 13 \
  --remote --host 192.168.11.3 --ssh-user walker

Know the two machines: - Jetson 192.168.11.3 (SSH walker, port 22/2222): runs the lerobot-tienkung container and inference. This is the --host for launch --remote. - Robot control PC 192.168.11.2 (SSH ubt, port 2222): dev_mode.sh developer mode / ROS 2. It does not run the inference container; do not use it as --host.

docs.title: Client commands
docs.text:
bash inference_client.sh status                       # query state (state/model/loop_hz/chunk_id/...)
bash inference_client.sh start                        # start inference (engine reset+resume -> RUNNING)
bash inference_client.sh stop                         # stop inference (engine pause -> READY, hold current pose)
bash inference_client.sh home                         # return to home_position (pause, then smooth chunk)
bash inference_client.sh load --policy-path /ubt_IL/model/<other>/.../pretrained_model --robot-model walker_s2_10d
                                                       # hot-swap the model while running (full rebuild incl. reconnect)
bash inference_client.sh shutdown                     # shut down (home + kill bridge + exit)
bash inference_client.sh watch                        # subscribe to the status PUB stream (Ctrl-C to exit)

docs.title: Environment variables (inference_server.sh)
docs.text:
Variable Default Description POLICY_PATH Required pretrained_model directory ROBOT_MODEL walker_s2_31d ROBOT_MODELS registry key ROBOT_CONFIG Empty Custom robot config JSON (overrides ROBOT_MODEL) INFERENCE_TYPE act_async Inference engine (start/stop require act_async) INFERENCE_HZ 0.6 act_async replanning rate EXECUTION_HORIZON 0 Truncate chunks after N steps FPS 13 Control loop FPS BLEND_HORIZON 10 Bridge chunk blending overlap points BODY_PUBLISH_HZ 300 Bridge 300 Hz body publish rate BODY_V_MAX 2.0 Bridge rate-limit maximum joint velocity SERVER_CMD_PORT 5570 ZMQ REP command port SERVER_STATUS_PORT 5571 ZMQ PUB status port PREVIEW_CAMERA 0 Server does not open the preview window by default

Singleton: /tmp/walker_inference_server.pid; a second launch is refused while it exists. Log: /tmp/walker_inference_server.log. State machine: LOADING (warm-up/rebuild) -> READY (idle) ⇄ RUNNING (executing); home -> RETURNING_HOME -> READY.

docs.title: 7. FAQ
docs.text: Problem Cause / fix Conversion reports "config does not exist" The convert.sh default CONFIG=configs/walker_s2_real_19d_1RGBD.json is not in the repository; specify an existing config (walker_s2_real_10d_2RGB.json) Real-robot 19D data cannot be converted The repository only provides a 10D real config; write walker_s2_real_19d_*.json based on the joint order in walker_s2_gripper_19d.json Dataset frame rate differs from expected Collection runs at 15 Hz and conversion defaults to FPS=15; use FPS=auto for the source rate or RESAMPLE_FPS to resample Deployment reports a dimension mismatch Safety precheck refused: policy output_features.action.shape[0] does not match robot config action_order. Match ROBOT_MODEL to the policy dimension (10D -> walker_s2_10d, 19D -> walker_s2_19d, 31D -> walker_s2_31d); policies without action names need ALLOW_DIM_ONLY_POLICY=1 Inference server start fails start/stop rely on act_async pause/resume; the sync engine has no such semantics, so use INFERENCE_TYPE=act_async launch --remote fails Confirm --host is the Jetson 192.168.11.3 (SSH walker), not the control PC; the SSH user needs sudo docker exec permission Robot does not move during deployment Confirm Bridge2 is running (5561/5562/5563), dev_mode.sh has switched to developer mode, and status shows the bridge connected Repeated inference server launch fails The singleton PID file /tmp/walker_inference_server.pid exists; shutdown cleanly or remove it manually

docs.title: Walker S2 EDU: Simulation Platform
docs.text: The Walker S2 EDU simulation is built on NVIDIA Isaac Sim (Isaac Lab 2.2.0). A ROS2-ZMQ bridge publishes simulation state and images on exactly the same ROS 2 topics as the real robot, enabling sim-to-real consistent teleoperation and data collection. The whole environment runs in a Docker container.

docs.title: 1. Build the environment (host)
docs.text:
The container build is identical for all robots; see Simulation Platform · Container Setup (build / start / init / check / bash).

⚠️ Must be changed before building: edit interfaceWhiteList in ubt_sim/docker/fastdds_no_shm.xml and set <address> to 192.168.11.99 (the Walker S2 direct-link subnet). The file is copied into the image at build time; changes after the build have no effect.

docs.title: 2. Launch simulation (container)
docs.text:
bash run.sh bash                       # enter the container (ROS 2 + Walker SDK environment sourced automatically)
UBT_SIM_TASK=UBTSim-WalkerS2-PickPart-v0 bash /ubt_sim/scripts/start_sim.sh   # start simulation + bridge

Select the task scene with UBT_SIM_TASK.

Task ID Scene Description UBTSim-WalkerS2-PartSorting-v0 Part sorting 4 parts + bins (default) UBTSim-WalkerS2-PickPart-v0 Part sorting Single-part picking: only one part on the table, used with pick_part.py

Demo (pick-and-place):

  • Press R to reset the robot/scene; the collection script can also publish /sim/cmd_reset with --reset-scene.
  • When the simulation window closes, the exit trap in start_sim.sh stops the bridge automatically.

Common environment variables/arguments (combinable):

Variable Purpose Default UBT_SIM_TASK Task name (also determines the robot type) UBTSim-TienkungPro-Parlor-v0; see the task table for Walker S2 EDU --headless Run without a window Common on headless servers --perf_stats Print performance statistics Frame-rate debugging --device cpu\|cuda\|cuda:N Execution device For switching GPUs outside load-only mode

docs.title: 3. Data collection (container, system Python 3.10)
docs.text:
# Grasp a part and record
/usr/bin/python3 /ubt_sim/teleoperation/control/walker_s2/pick_part.py --save --reset-scene --robot-init

# Batch loop (400 iterations by default)
bash /ubt_sim/teleoperation/control/walker_s2/save_data.sh
  • pick_part.py performs one part pick-and-place: reads /sim/part_states live -> pregrasp -> grasp -> lift -> place in the bin -> return.
  • --save enables recording: 17 body joints + both hands + grippers + four RGB cameras and timestamps are written to HDF5 (by default only successful episodes are saved).
  • --reset-scene resets the scene first; --robot-init moves the robot to its initial pose (setup actions, not recorded).
  • save_data.sh is the batch script; adjust its internal parameters per task (currently 400 single-part grasps by default).
  • Output: /ubt_sim/dataset/walker_s2/<timestamp>/trajectory.hdf5.

Detailed parameters:

Argument Default Description --part <name> part_a_red Part name (part_a_ori / part_a_red / part_b_blue / part_b_ori) --all-parts / --parts <name...> - Grasp all four parts in order / custom order --side left\|right right Grasping arm --reset-scene Off Publish /sim/cmd_reset before grasping --robot-init Off Move to READY_POSE before grasping (equivalent to state --init) --randomize-parts / --no-randomize-parts On Randomize part poses before multi-part grasping --save Off Record HDF5 (with --save-only-success, only successful episodes by default) --capture-hz <Hz> 15.0 HDF5 capture rate --unlock-waist Off Unlock waist IK

docs.title: 4. Robot controller (container, system Python 3.10)
docs.text:
Unified entry point walker_s2_controller.py, usable for both simulation and hardware:

# Initialize the robot pose (staged move to READY_POSE)
/usr/bin/python3 /ubt_sim/teleoperation/control/walker_s2/walker_s2_controller.py --init
# See --help for more; subcommand parameters: <subcommand> --help

Subcommands:

Subcommand Description Common arguments state Joint/gripper/end-effector state, single-joint moves, ready pose, gripper control --print-state --init --grip-open --move-joint --joint <name> --pos <rad> joint Joint/hand debugging --print --move JOINT=ANGLE --hand-open --monitor endpoint End-effector/TCP pose test --no-move --side left home Staged return to all-zero home + open hands No arguments analyze Joint step/sine response analysis + CSV --joint <name> --step <rad> --sine --listen --csv <path> camera Camera topic info/preview/save --preview --save --count 5 --topic <topic>

Examples:

/usr/bin/python3 walker_s2_controller.py state --print-state                # show joint/gripper/end-effector state
/usr/bin/python3 walker_s2_controller.py state --init                       # staged move to the ready pose
/usr/bin/python3 walker_s2_controller.py joint --move R_elbow_yaw_joint=0.5 # move one joint to 0.5 rad (press Enter to confirm)
/usr/bin/python3 walker_s2_controller.py home                               # staged return to all-zero home + open hands
/usr/bin/python3 walker_s2_controller.py analyze --joint R_elbow_yaw_joint --step 0.5  # joint step analysis
/usr/bin/python3 walker_s2_controller.py camera --preview                   # live camera preview

docs.title: Camera test (camera subcommand)
docs.text:
Walker S2 EDU publishes four cameras (head stereo left/right + wrist left/right) over ZMQ (5657) and ROS 2 topics:

# Live preview (cv2.imshow, requires X11; use -X forwarding over SSH; press Q/ESC to exit)
/usr/bin/python3 /ubt_sim/teleoperation/control/walker_s2/walker_s2_controller.py camera --preview

# Inspect/save all four camera images
/usr/bin/python3 /ubt_sim/teleoperation/control/walker_s2/walker_s2_controller.py camera --save --count 5
Argument Default Description --topic bridge config -> /sensor/camera/stereo/color/raw Camera topic to subscribe to --msg-type Image2m Message type (Image8k/Image512k/Image1m/Image2m/Image4m/Image6m/Image8m/sensor_msgs/Image) --preview Off cv2.imshow live preview (Q/ESC to exit, requires X11) --save Off Save frames as PNG (camera_frame_<timestamp>.png) --count <N> 0 (unlimited) Maximum frames to save/preview, then exit --interval <seconds> 1.0 Print/save loop interval --no-print Off Suppress frame info (all modes)

docs.title: 5. Dataset preview and playback (container)
docs.text:
Reads dataset/walker_s2/<timestamp>/trajectory.hdf5, previews cameras + joint curves (Rerun), or replays recorded actions on simulation/hardware topics.

# Preview an HDF5 dataset
/usr/bin/python3 /ubt_sim/teleoperation/tools/playback_walker_s2.py \
    --episode dataset/walker_s2/1786681892 --mode preview --web-port 9090

# Action playback (simulation/hardware)
/usr/bin/python3 /ubt_sim/teleoperation/tools/playback_walker_s2.py \
    --episode dataset/walker_s2/1786681892 --mode control

See Playback for all options and safety notes.

docs.title: Simulation modules
docs.text: Module Path Description Docker orchestration ubt_sim/docker/run.sh Image build, container lifecycle, bridge start/stop Environment variables ubt_sim/docker/env.sh Container name, image, ROS_DOMAIN_ID Simulation launcher ubt_sim/scripts/start_sim.sh Detects the robot from UBT_SIM_TASK and starts the bridge Task definitions ubt_sim/source/ubt_sim/task/walker_*/ Walker S2 scene definitions Simulation config ubt_sim/config/walker_s2/ part_sorting.yaml / pick-part.yaml / parlor.yaml ROS2-ZMQ bridge ubt_sim/teleoperation/bridges/walker_s2/ Bridge script + walker_s2_bridge_config.yaml Teleoperation and collection ubt_sim/teleoperation/control/walker_s2/ walker_s2_controller.py / pick_part.py / carry_box.py / keyboard_ee_control.py / save_data.sh Data output ubt_sim/dataset/walker_s2/<timestamp>/trajectory.hdf5 Collected episodes

docs.title: GPU rendering + CPU PhysX
docs.text: Walker S2 EDU uses GPU rendering + CPU PhysX by default: start_sim.sh / sim_runner.py set the rendering/AppLauncher device to cuda:0 but the Isaac Lab physics/env device to cpu. This avoids a PhysX GPU tensor device mismatch triggered by get_dof_velocities() during Walker S2 articulation initialization with Isaac Sim 5.0 + Isaac Lab 2.2. Do not switch physics back to GPU by default; for experiments set UBT_SIM_WALKER_S2_PHYSICS_DEVICE=cuda:0 explicitly.

docs.title: Walker SDK ROS 2 message packages
docs.text: The bridge and collection scripts depend on Walker SDK ROS 2 messages (rosa_msgs / shm_msgs / mc_task_msgs / mc_state_msgs / ecat_task_msgs), built by bash run.sh init into /opt/ubt_sim/walker_sdk_ros2_msgs/install and sourced automatically by run.sh bash. The DDS middleware is rmw_cyclonedds_cpp.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• bash run.sh check reports errors: follow the prompt and rerun bash run.sh init; verify numpy<2, bodyctrl_msgs, and the Walker SDK ROS 2 messages.
  • Collection script fails to import rclpy / message types: use /usr/bin/python3, not Isaac Sim Python, and confirm bash run.sh init built the message packages.
  • save_data.sh trips the consecutive-failure breaker: usually the bridge is not ready. Verify the simulation window is running and the bridge process exists (pgrep -f walker_s2_ros2_zmq_bridge), or run bash run.sh bridge-start separately.
  • Simulation reports "Walker SDK messages not built": run cd /ubt_sim/docker && bash run.sh init inside the container.
  • X11 unavailable / no simulation window: run xhost + on the host and verify DISPLAY is forwarded; on headless machines only UBT_SIM_LOAD_ONLY=1 preview is available.
  • Keyboard teleoperation cannot capture input: pynput does not work in headless containers; run keyboard_ee_control.py on the host with a graphical session.

After collection, continue with Imitation Learning Platform.

docs.title: Walker S2 EDU Simulation Workflow: Collect -> Convert -> Train -> Evaluate -> Deploy
docs.text: Complete closed loop for Isaac Sim -> Walker S2 EDU hardware: simulation collection -> data conversion -> training -> evaluation -> simulation feedback deployment. Code: ubt_IL/scripts/{convert,train,deploy}/walker_s2/ and the ubt_sim/ simulation project.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• 0. Workflow overview
  • 1. Prerequisite: simulation data collection
  • 2. Start the container
  • 3. Data conversion (HDF5 -> LeRobot)
  • 3.1 Conversion command
  • 3.2 Data visualization
  • 4. Policy training
  • 5. Policy evaluation (offline MSE)
  • 6. Model deployment (simulation feedback)
  • 6.1 Rollout deployment
  • 6.2 Inference server (warm start/external calls)
  • 7. FAQ

docs.title: 0. Workflow overview
docs.text: A[Simulation collection hdf5] --> B[Data conversion] --> C[Model training] --> D[Offline MSE] --> E[Simulation deployment]

docs.title: 1. Prerequisite: simulation data collection
docs.text: Data comes from Isaac Sim collection (ubt_sim); see Simulation Platform for details.

docs.title: 1.1 Launch the simulation environment and task
docs.text:
cd ubt_sim/docker
bash run.sh bash                       # enter the container (ROS 2 + Walker SDK environment sourced)
UBT_SIM_TASK=UBTSim-WalkerS2-PickPart-v0 bash /ubt_sim/scripts/start_sim.sh   # start simulation + bridge

docs.title: 1.2 Collection commands
docs.text:
Single episode (--save records, --reset-scene resets, --robot-init initializes the pose):

/usr/bin/python3 /ubt_sim/teleoperation/control/walker_s2/pick_part.py --save --reset-scene --robot-init

Batch collection (400 iterations by default):

bash /ubt_sim/teleoperation/control/walker_s2/save_data.sh

docs.title: 1.3 Output
docs.text:
• Output directory: /ubt_sim/dataset/walker_s2/<timestamp>/trajectory.hdf5 (15 Hz)
  • After collection, copy the HDF5 data to /ubt_IL/dataset/walker-s2-sim-data/ so the container can mount it easily.

docs.title: 2. Start the container
docs.text:
Training/conversion/deployment all run in the lerobot-tienkung container:

cd ubt_IL/docker
bash run.sh build      # first time
bash run.sh start
bash run.sh bash       # enter the container; run conversion/training/evaluation there

The container has two Python environments: use /usr/bin/python3 for ROS and /lerobot/.venv/bin/python (default) for LeRobot.

docs.title: 3.1 Conversion command
docs.text:
Script: ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/convert.sh; configs in /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/configs/; choose or adapt one for your training needs.

# Simulation conversion
CONFIG=/ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/configs/walker_s2_sim_10d_2RGB.json \
SRC_ROOT=/ubt_IL/dataset/Walker-s2-pick-part-sim \
HDF5_REL_PATH=trajectory.hdf5 \
TGT_PATH=/ubt_IL/dataset \
REPO_ID=Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB \
TASK_NAME=walker_s2_sim_pick_part \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/convert.sh


# Stationary frames can trap the policy in a local stationary loop; enable trimming with TRIM_STATIONARY=1
TRIM_STATIONARY=1 \
CONFIG=/ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/configs/walker_s2_sim_10d_2RGB.json \
SRC_ROOT=/ubt_IL/dataset/Walker-s2-pick-part-sim \
HDF5_REL_PATH=trajectory.hdf5 \
TGT_PATH=/ubt_IL/dataset \
REPO_ID=Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB \
TASK_NAME=walker_s2_sim_pick_part \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/convert/walker_s2/convert.sh

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Default Description SRC_ROOT /ubt_IL/dataset/walker-s2-real-data HDF5 source directory (change to the sim data directory for simulation) TGT_PATH /ubt_IL/dataset LeRobot output root CONFIG configs/walker_s2_real_19d_1RGBD.json Conversion config (the default file is not in the repository; always specify an existing config) REPO_ID Walker_S2_real_19_1RGBD Output dataset repo_id (local directory name + HF repo name) ROBOT_TYPE walker_s2 Robot type (written to metadata) TASK_NAME walker_s2_real Task name (written to metadata) FPS 13 Dataset frame rate (auto uses the source HDF5 rate) VCODEC h264 Video codec (h264/jpeg/png) HDF5_REL_PATH hdf5/metadata_aligned.hdf5 Source HDF5 relative path RESAMPLE_FPS Empty Resample to the target rate when set LABEL_ROOT Empty Label root (used when task labels exist) TRIM_STATIONARY Empty Trim stationary frames when set (--trim-stationary) STATIONARY_KEY action Key used for stationary detection STATIONARY_WINDOW Auto (0.3 × fps) Stationary detection window STATIONARY_THRESH 0.03 Stationary detection threshold STATIONARY_CAP 8 Maximum consecutive stationary frames STATIONARY_MIN_RUN 3 Minimum valid run length STATIONARY_RANGE_EPS 1e-3 Stationary interval tolerance

Pass-through options: --overwrite replaces an existing dataset; --save_one true uses single-file mode.

docs.title: 3.2 Data visualization
docs.text:
After conversion, inspect the dataset with the LeRobot visualizer:

# Inside the container:
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 lerobot-dataset-viz \
  --repo-id <dataset name> \
  --episode-index 0 \
  --root /ubt_IL/dataset/<dataset name>

Example:

# Visualize the dataset converted in section 3.1
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 lerobot-dataset-viz \
  --repo-id Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB \
  --episode-index 0 \
  --root /ubt_IL/dataset/Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB

Preview:

Check especially: video frame rate, state/action dimension and order, grip range, and empty episodes.

docs.title: 4. Policy training
docs.text:
Training script: /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/train.sh Configs: /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/configs/; choose or adapt one for your training needs.

# Train with the default config
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/train.sh

# Specify a config path explicitly and override common parameters
CONFIG=/ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/configs/train_config_walker_s2_sim_act_10_2RGB.json \
OUTPUT_DIR=/ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB_act \
STEPS=50000 SAVE_FREQ=5000 BATCH_SIZE=8 \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/train.sh

# Resume (CONFIG points to train_config.json inside the checkpoint)
CONFIG=/ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model/train_config.json \
RESUME=true \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/train.sh

Without train.sh (call lerobot-train directly with --xxx=yyy overrides; run from /ubt_IL/lerobot):

# Train from scratch
cd /ubt_IL/lerobot
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /lerobot/.venv/bin/lerobot-train \
  --config_path=/ubt_IL/scripts/train/walker_s2/configs/train_config_walker_s2_sim_act_10_2RGB.json \
  --output_dir=/ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB_act \
  --steps=50000 --save_freq=5000 --batch_size=8

# Resume
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /lerobot/.venv/bin/lerobot-train \
  --config_path=/ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model/train_config.json \
  --resume=true

docs.title: Overrides
docs.text:
Variable Default (config) Description CONFIG $SCRIPT_DIR/configs/train_config_walker_s2_sim_act_10_2RGB.json Training config JSON DATASET_REPO_ID Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB Dataset repo_id DATASET_ROOT /ubt_IL/dataset Dataset root OUTPUT_DIR /ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB_act Model output directory STEPS 50000 Total training steps SAVE_FREQ 5000 Checkpoint save frequency BATCH_SIZE 8 Batch size SEED 1000 Random seed DEVICE cuda Training device (cuda/cpu) RESUME false true resumes from the checkpoint WANDB_ENABLE false wandb logging switch

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 is enabled by default (offline training). Environment variables override config values only when explicitly set.

docs.title: 5. Policy evaluation (offline MSE)
docs.text:
Runs offline MSE evaluation (prediction vs ground truth) on a LeRobot dataset without connecting to the robot and generates per-episode comparison plots. Script (shared with TienKung): ubt_IL/scripts/eval/eval_policy.py.

Example: 

cd /ubt_IL/lerobot

/lerobot/.venv/bin/python /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/eval_policy.py \
  --policy-path /ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
  --dataset-path /ubt_IL/dataset/Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB \
  --episodes 10 \
  --inference-freq 1 \
  --plot \
  --plot-dir /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/output/eval_Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB_act \
  --output /ubt_IL/scripts/eval/output/eval_Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB_act/results.json \
  --device cuda
Preview:

Argument Description --policy-path pretrained_model directory (containing config.json + model.safetensors) --dataset-path LeRobot dataset root (containing meta/info.json) --episodes Number of episodes to evaluate (default: all) --inference-freq Run inference every N steps and reuse the predicted chunk in between (emulates real deployment; 1 = every step) --plot / --plot-dir Per-episode prediction-vs-ground-truth plots and output directory --output Result JSON path --device cuda or cpu (default cuda, falls back automatically)

docs.title: 6. Model deployment (simulation feedback)
docs.text:
Simulation deployment shares rollout.sh / the inference server with hardware. Differences:

  • Robot commands are fed back into Isaac Sim through the ROS2-ZMQ Bridge, with ZMQ_HOST=127.0.0.1 (local bridge);
  • Cameras come from simulation (four RGB streams or the configured cameras), no hardware camera needed;
  • A safety precheck (action dimension match) runs before deployment and must pass before motion is allowed.

docs.title: 6.1 Rollout deployment
docs.text:
Script: ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/rollout.sh.

Deployment steps (run in the simulation and inference containers separately):

# 1. Start simulation -- host, enter the simulation container
cd ubt_sim/docker 
bash run.sh start
bash run.sh bash
UBT_SIM_TASK=UBTSim-WalkerS2-PickPart-v0 bash /ubt_sim/scripts/start_sim.sh      # start the task matching the model

# 2. Start the inference container -- host
cd ubt_IL/docker
bash run.sh start
bash run.sh bash

# 3. Initialize the pose (raise the arm above the table) -- inference container; /usr/bin/python3 has ROS access
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/robot_ready.sh

# Deploy simulation asynchronous inference (020000 checkpoint shown)
ROBOT_MODEL=walker_s2_10d \
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB_act/checkpoints/020000/pretrained_model \
INFERENCE_TYPE=act_async INFERENCE_HZ=2 \
FPS=13 DURATION=60 \
ZMQ_HOST=127.0.0.1 \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/rollout.sh

# (Optional) Verify the camera path; specify camera topic/robot config
/usr/bin/python3 scripts/deploy/walker_s2/preview_camera.py --robot walker_s2_10d
Demo:

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Default Description POLICY_PATH Required, no default Checkpoint directory (containing config.json) ROBOT_MODEL walker_s2_31d ROBOT_MODELS registry key (see below) ROBOT_CONFIG configs/<ROBOT_MODEL>.json Full path to the robot config (override for custom configs) ALLOW_DIM_ONLY_POLICY 1 Allow dimension-only matching when the policy has no action names STRATEGY base Rollout strategy FPS 13 Control rate DURATION 30 Run time (seconds) TASK walker s2 rollout Task description PREVIEW_CAMERA 1 Show the camera preview window RECORD_ACTIONS 1 Record rollout actions (RECORD_OUTPUT_DIR sets the output) INFERENCE_TYPE sync Inference engine (sync / act_async) INFERENCE_HZ 0.6 act_async replanning rate EXECUTION_HORIZON 0 Truncate chunks after N steps (0 = no truncation) ZMQ_HOST 127.0.0.1 Bridge address (local for simulation feedback)

Exported parameters: BLEND_HORIZON=10, BODY_PUBLISH_HZ=300, BODY_V_MAX=2.0 (bridge chunk blending and publish rate limiting).

docs.title: Online evaluation (recording inference trajectories)
docs.text: Set RECORD_ACTIONS=1 during deployment to record rollout actions for analyzing model predictions, robot execution, and ACT blending. Records are saved under ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/output.

docs.title: Robot configuration (ROBOT_MODELS registry)
docs.text: Registry key Dimension End effector Config file walker_s2_10d 10D (right arm 7 + head 2 + right gripper 1) PGC right gripper walker_s2_gripper_19d.json (10D is a subset) walker_s2_19d 19D (17 body + 2 grippers) PGC 1-DOF gripper walker_s2_gripper_19d.json walker_s2_31d 31D (17 body + 14 hands) V4 dexterous hand 7 DOF walker_s2_v4_hand_31d.json

docs.title: 6.2 Inference server (warm start/external calls)
docs.text:
Inference server script: ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/inference_server.sh Client script: ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/inference_client.sh

rollout.sh pays a long cold start (policy load + bridge startup) on every run. The inference server stays resident and pre-warmed; external clients control it over ZMQ and can switch VLA tasks and other tasks such as navigation or box carrying. See Inference server.

# 1. Start the service (inside the container; pre-warms in the background to READY; the engine is paused and the robot does not move)
cd /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2
ROBOT_MODEL=walker_s2_10d \
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/Walker_S2_sim_10_2RGB_act/checkpoints/last/pretrained_model \
INFERENCE_TYPE=act_async INFERENCE_HZ=2 FPS=13 \
bash inference_server.sh

# 2. Check whether the service is READY
bash inference_client.sh status

# 3. Start / stop inference
bash inference_client.sh start
bash inference_client.sh stop

# 4. Return home / shut down
bash inference_client.sh home
bash inference_client.sh shutdown

State machine: LOADING (warm-up/rebuild) -> READY (idle) ⇄ RUNNING (executing); home -> RETURNING_HOME -> READY.

docs.title: 7. FAQ
docs.text: Problem Cause / fix Conversion reports "config does not exist" The convert.sh default CONFIG=configs/walker_s2_real_19d_1RGBD.json is not in the repository; specify an existing config (walker_s2_sim_10d_2RGB.json / walker_s2_sim_33d_4RGB.json) Dataset frame rate differs from expected Collection runs at 15 Hz and conversion defaults to FPS=13; use FPS=auto to keep the source rate or RESAMPLE_FPS to resample Deployment reports a dimension mismatch Safety precheck refused: policy output_features.action.shape[0] does not match robot config action_order. Match ROBOT_MODEL to the policy dimension (10D -> walker_s2_10d, 19D -> walker_s2_19d, 31D -> walker_s2_31d); policies without action names need ALLOW_DIM_ONLY_POLICY=1 Inference server start fails start/stop rely on act_async pause/resume; the sync engine has no such semantics, so use INFERENCE_TYPE=act_async Simulation and hardware camera sizes differ Simulation RGB is [3,240,320] (10D) or [3,480,640] (33D); hardware is [256,320] etc. Model input must match the training data — do not mix them Repeated inference server launch fails The singleton PID file /tmp/walker_inference_server.pid exists; shutdown cleanly or remove it manually before relaunching

docs.title: Walker S2 EDU: Wrist Camera (RealSense D405)
docs.text: ubt_IL/walker/realsense_wrist_camera/: an Intel RealSense D405 wrist camera ROS 2 publisher that provides wrist vision input for Walker S2 EDU real-robot deployment.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
# 1. Install (auto-discover cameras, generate config, persist PATH)
bash /ubt_IL/walker/realsense_wrist_camera/scripts/install.sh

# 2. Start (runs in the background by default)
bash /ubt_IL/walker/realsense_wrist_camera/scripts/start.sh

# 3. Check status / stop
bash /ubt_IL/walker/realsense_wrist_camera/scripts/start.sh --status
bash /ubt_IL/walker/realsense_wrist_camera/scripts/start.sh --stop

For debugging, run in the foreground with bash start.sh --fg; other arguments are passed through to the CLI (e.g. bash start.sh --fg --discover).

docs.title: Verify publishing
docs.text: ros2 topic echo /sensor/camera/wrist_right/color/raw --once --qos-reliability best_effort

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
install.sh generates configs/wrist_cameras.json automatically; regenerate it with:

find-realsense-cameras

Start with an explicit config:

realsense-wrist-camera --config /path/to/cameras.json &

Config format (one D405 per wrist, shm_msgs/Image1m, 640×480@15fps):

{
  "cameras": [
    {
      "serial": "261122273724",
      "topic": "/sensor/camera/wrist_right/color/raw",
      "msg_type": "shm_msgs/Image1m",
      "frame_id": "wrist_right",
      "width": 640,
      "height": 480,
      "fps": 15
    },
    {
      "serial": "261022273252",
      "topic": "/sensor/camera/wrist_left/color/raw",
      "msg_type": "shm_msgs/Image1m",
      "frame_id": "wrist_left",
      "width": 640,
      "height": 480,
      "fps": 15
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Integration with real-robot deployment
docs.text:
The wrist cameras publish shm_msgs/Image1m on standard topics; walker_camera_relay.py picks them up automatically, so rollout needs no extra configuration:

# Terminal 1
bash /ubt_IL/walker/realsense_wrist_camera/scripts/start.sh

# Terminal 2 - normal rollout
POLICY_PATH=/ubt_IL/model/<policy>/checkpoints/080000/pretrained_model \
bash /ubt_IL/scripts/deploy/walker_s2/rollout.sh

docs.title: Installation prerequisites
docs.text:
udev rules (host, one time):

sudo sh -c 'echo "SUBSYSTEM==\"usb\", ATTR{idVendor}==\"8086\", ATTR{idProduct}==\"0b5b\", MODE=\"0666\"" > /etc/udev/rules.d/99-realsense-d405.rules'
sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
sudo udevadm trigger

Docker: the container must run with --privileged (already included in the project run.sh).

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Symptom Fix No RealSense devices detected Check the USB connection and udev rules ModuleNotFoundError: pyrealsense2 Rerun install.sh ModuleNotFoundError: rclpy source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash USB Permission denied Docker is missing --privileged
